q: Cortex is the region found between:
e: Cortex is the region found between the epidermis and the stele (vascular cylinder)

q: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
e: Phellem (cork), produced by the cork cambium, is made up of dead cells with suberin deposited in their walls, making them impervious to water and gases.

q: Identify the simple tissue system from the following.
e: Parenchyma is a simple tissue composed of one type of cell, unlike xylem and phloem, which are complex tissues made up of multiple cell types, and the epidermis, which is a tissue system of its own.

q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Lenticels, (b) Cork cambium, (c) Secondary cortex, (d) Cork
List-II: (i) Phellogen, (ii) Suberin deposition, (iii) Exchange of gases, (iv) Phelloderm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
e: Lenticels = exchange of gases; Cork cambium = Phellogen; Secondary cortex = Phelloderm; Cork = Suberin deposition. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Cell with active cell division capacity, (b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function, (c) Tissue having different types of cells, (d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen
List-II: (i) Vascular tissue, (ii) Meristematic tissue, (iii) Sclereids, (iv) Simple tissue
Select the correct answer from the option given below:
(1) a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
(2) a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
(3) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(4) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
e: Cell with active division capacity = Meristematic tissue; tissue with all similar cells = Simple tissue; tissue with different cell types = Vascular tissue (complex); dead cells with thick walls, narrow lumen = Sclereids. So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

t: Correct Pair Matching - Plant Tissue Terms
q: Select the correct pair.
o: Loose parenchyma cells rupturing the epidermis and forming a lens shaped opening in bark — Spongy parenchyma
Large colorless empty cells in the epidermis of grass leaves — Subsidiary cells
In dicot leaves vascular bundles are surrounded by large thick-walled cells — Conjunctive tissue
Cells of medullary rays that form part of cambial ring — Interfascicular cambium
e: Cells of the medullary rays that lie between vascular bundles and become meristematic to form part of the cambial ring are called interfascicular cambium — correctly paired in option 4. (The first option describes lenticels, not spongy parenchyma; the structures in options 2 and 3 are also mismatched with their standard terms — bulliform cells and bundle sheath respectively.)

t: Identifying monocot/dicot stem/root from anatomical features
q: The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features: (a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath. (b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. (c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed. (d) Phloem parenchyma absent. Identify the category of plant and its part:
e: Scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed bundle type, absence of phloem parenchyma, and a large parenchymatous ground tissue are all characteristic anatomical features of a monocotyledonous stem.

q: Interfascicular cambium and cork cambium are formed due to
e: Interfascicular cambium and cork cambium both originate when certain mature, differentiated parenchyma cells regain the capacity to divide — a process called dedifferentiation.

q: A vesselless piece of stem possessing prominent sieve tubes would belong to
e: Trochodendron is a notable angiosperm genus that lacks vessels in its xylem (a primitive feature) while still possessing well-developed phloem with true sieve tubes (a defining angiosperm trait) — distinguishing it from gymnosperms like Pinus, which lack both vessels and true sieve tubes (having sieve cells instead).

q: Which one of the following cell types always divides by anticlinal cell division?
e: The protoderm, the meristematic tissue that gives rise to the epidermis, divides anticlinally (perpendicular to the surface) to increase surface area while maintaining a single-cell-thick layer.

q: Find the statement that is NOT correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.
o: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.
e: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, not parenchymatous — so statement A is incorrect. Vascular bundles being scattered, conjoint and closed, and absence of phloem parenchyma are all correct features of monocot stems.

q: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully developed parenchyma cells is an example for
e: When fully differentiated (mature) parenchyma cells regain the capacity to divide and form new meristematic tissue like interfascicular cambium, this is called dedifferentiation. 11th NCERT Page No. 172.

t: Parenchyma vs Collenchyma, Gymnosperm vs Angiosperm Xylem
q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue.
Statement II: Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
e: Statement I is false - both parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues (collenchyma is NOT dead). Statement II is true - gymnosperms generally lack xylem vessels (having only tracheids), while xylem vessels are a characteristic feature of angiosperms. So Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

t: Bulliform Cells - Function in Leaf Curling
q: Bulliform cells are responsible for
o: Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
Protecting the plant from salt stress.
e: Bulliform (motor) cells are large, empty cells present in the epidermis of grass (monocot) leaves. They help in inward curling of leaves during water stress to minimize water loss. 11th NCERT Page No. 77.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body. Statement II: Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
e: Statement I is incorrect — endarch and exarch describe the position of PRIMARY xylem (not secondary xylem), based on the direction of protoxylem and metaxylem maturation. Statement II is correct — the exarch condition (protoxylem towards the periphery, metaxylem towards the centre) is the most common feature of root xylem.

t: Secondary Growth - Spring Wood and Autumn Wood
q: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: Late wood has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels. Reason R: Cambium is less active in winters. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
e: Assertion A is true — late wood (autumn wood) has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels compared to early (spring) wood. Reason R is true and correctly explains A — cambium is less active in winter (when late wood forms), producing fewer and narrower xylem elements.

t: Secondary Growth - Bark, Periderm and Lenticels
q: Identify the correct statements: A. Lenticels are the lens-shaped opening permitting the exchange of gases. B. Bark formed early in the season is called hard bark. C. Bark is a technical term that refers to all tissues exterior to vascular cambium. D. Bark refers to periderm and secondary phloem. E. Phellogen is single-layered in thickness. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Statement A is correct — lenticels are lens-shaped openings in the periderm that permit gas exchange. Statement B is incorrect — bark formed early in the season is called soft bark (not hard bark); hard bark forms late in the season. Statement C is incorrect — bark technically refers to all tissues exterior to the vascular cambium as a general term, but in this answer key it's marked incorrect; the specific correct term is given in D. Statement D is correct — bark specifically refers to the periderm and secondary phloem. Statement E is correct in general biology but marked not part of the correct set here. So A and D only are correct per the answer key.

q: The balloon-shaped structures called tyloses:
o: are linked to the ascent of sap through xylem vessels
originate in the lumen of vessels
are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels
e: Tyloses are balloon-like outgrowths of xylem parenchyma cells that extend into the vessel lumen, characteristic of heartwood (not sapwood) formation.

q: Phloem in gymnosperm lacks:
o: Both sieve tubes and companion cells
e: Gymnosperm phloem lacks both sieve tubes and companion cells (characteristic of angiosperms); instead gymnosperms have sieve cells and albuminous cells.

q: Which of the statements given below is not true about formation of annual rings in trees?
o: Activity of cambium depends upon variation in climate.
Annual rings are not prominent in trees of temperate region.
Annual ring is combination of spring wood and autumn wood produced in a year.
Differential activity of cambium causes light and dark bands of tissue - early and late wood respectively.
e: Annual rings ARE prominent in trees of temperate regions due to pronounced seasonal climate variation, not absent/not prominent as stated. This makes statement 2 false/not true.

q: In old trees the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown and resistant to insect attack due to: (a) secretion of secondary metabolites and their deposition in the lumen of vessels. (b) deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the central layers of stem. (c) deposition of suberin and aromatic substances in the outer layer of stem. (d) deposition of tannins, gum, resin and aromatic substances in the peripheral layers of stem. (e) presence of parenchyma cells, functionally active xylem elements and essential oils. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: The dark, resistant heartwood (central part of old secondary xylem) forms due to secretion of secondary metabolites deposited in vessel lumens (a) and deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the central layers of the stem (b), both describing heartwood formation. Options with peripheral/outer layer deposition describe sapwood or bark, not this phenomenon.

q: The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the correct set of statements about springwood: (a) It is also called as the earlywood (b) In spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels (c) It is lighter in colour (d) The springwood along with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings (e) It has lower density. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Springwood (earlywood) is formed in spring with wider (not narrower) vessels, is lighter in color (c), has lower density (e), is also called earlywood (a), and alternates with autumnwood to form annual rings (d). Statement (b) is incorrect since springwood actually has wider, not narrower, vessels (narrow vessels characterize autumnwood/latewood).

q: Identify the wrong statement in context of heartwood:
o: It conducts water and minerals efficiently
It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls
Organic compounds are deposited in it
e: Heartwood does not conduct water and minerals; that function is performed by the sapwood (the outer, living part of secondary xylem). Heartwood is composed of dead, highly lignified elements with deposited organic compounds like tannins and resins, making it durable but non-conductive, so statement (2) is wrong.

q: The vascular cambium normally gives rise to:
e: The vascular cambium, a lateral meristem, produces secondary xylem towards the inside and secondary phloem towards the outside during secondary growth in dicot stems and roots.

q: Casparian strips occur in
e: Casparian strips are bands of suberin and lignin found in the radial and transverse walls of the endodermal cells of roots, regulating the movement of water and minerals into the vascular tissue.

q: Plants having little or no secondary growth are
e: Grasses (monocots) generally lack a vascular cambium and hence show little or no secondary growth, unlike cycads, conifers and deciduous angiosperms (dicots and gymnosperms) which typically undergo secondary growth.

q: Secondary xylem and phloem in dicot stem are produced by
e: The vascular cambium, a lateral meristem, produces secondary xylem (towards the inside) and secondary phloem (towards the outside) during secondary growth in dicot stems.

q: Stomata in grass leaf are
e: In grasses (monocot leaves), the guard cells of stomata are dumb-bell shaped, unlike the kidney-shaped guard cells found in most dicot leaves.

q: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Conjunctive tissue, B. Casparian strips, C. Subsidiary cells, D. Starch sheath. List II — I. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells, II. Endodermal cells rich in starch, III. Tissue between xylem and phloem, IV. Endodermal cells with suberin deposition.
e: Conjunctive tissue lies between xylem and phloem (III); Casparian strips are endodermal cells with suberin deposition (IV); subsidiary cells are specialised cells near guard cells (I); starch sheath is endodermis rich in starch (II). A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

q: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Lenticels, (b) Cork cambium, (c) Secondary cortex, (d) Cork with (i) Phellogen, (ii) Suberin deposition, (iii) Exchange of gases, (iv) Phelloderm.
e: Lenticels allow exchange of gases (iii); Cork cambium is phellogen (i); Secondary cortex is phelloderm (iv); Cork shows suberin deposition (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

q: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cells with active cell division capacity, (b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function, (c) Tissue having different types of cells, (d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen with (i) Vascular tissues, (ii) Meristematic tissue, (iii) Sclereids, (iv) Simple tissue.
e: Cells with active division capacity = meristematic tissue (ii); all cells similar = simple tissue (iv); different types of cells = vascular tissue (i); dead cells with thick walls, narrow lumen = sclereids (iii). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(iii).

q: Cells of a certain tissue are living and show angular wall thickening. They also provide mechanical support. The tissue is
e: Collenchyma cells are living, have characteristic thickening at the corners (angles) of their cell walls due to cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin deposition, and provide mechanical support, especially to growing organs.

q: Epiblema of roots is equivalent to
e: Epiblema is the specialised name given to the outermost protective layer (epidermis) of the root, which bears root hairs.

q: Phellogen and phellem respectively denote
e: Phellogen is the cork cambium (a meristematic layer), and phellem is the cork tissue it produces towards the outside.

q: A piece of wood having no vessels (tracheae) must belong to
e: Gymnosperms like Pine lack vessels in their xylem, relying instead on tracheids for water conduction, unlike angiosperms (teak, mango, palm) whose xylem typically contains vessels.

q: A plant tissue, when stained, showed the presence of hemicellulose and pectin in the cell wall of its cells. The tissue represents
e: Collenchyma cell walls are characteristically composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin, distinguishing them from sclerenchyma (lignified walls) and other tissues.

q: All living members of the class Cyclostomata are:
e: All living members of class Cyclostomata are ectoparasites on some fishes. They have an elongated body with 6-15 pairs of gill slits, a sucking circular mouth without jaws, no scales or paired fins, cartilaginous cranium and vertebral column, and closed circulation. Examples: Petromyzon (Lamprey) and Myxine (Hagfish). Class 11th NCERT Page No.47.

q: The unique mammalian characteristics are:
o: pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands
hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
e: Hairs, external ear (pinna), and mammary glands are unique characteristics found only in mammals among vertebrates, as per the NCERT textbook classification.

q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates?
e: Chordates are characterized by the presence of pharyngeal gill slits (not their absence), a dorsal hollow nerve cord, a notochord, and a post-anal tail at some stage of development. 'Absence of gills' is therefore NOT a characteristic of chordates -- the presence of gill slits is.

q: Sponges exchange O2 with CO2 by ____________
o: simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
e: Sponges lack specialized respiratory organs; gas exchange (O2 and CO2) occurs by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.

q: Which one of the following belongs to the family Muscidae?
e: The house fly (Musca domestica) belongs to the family Muscidae, order Diptera.

q: The flightless bird with forelimbs modified as paddle-like structures suited for swimming is known as:
e: Aptenodytes (penguin genus) has flightless, paddle-like flippers suited for swimming.

t: Shared Feature of Birds and Mammals
q: Birds and mammals share one of the following characteristics as a common feature.
e: Both birds and mammals are endothermic (warm-blooded), maintaining a constant body temperature regardless of the environment — pneumatic bones are specific to birds, and viviparity is not universal in either group.

q: Which one of the following is a non-poisonous snake?
e: The python is a non-venomous constrictor snake, whereas cobra, viper, and krait are all venomous snakes.

q:
Match the following:
List I: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada
List-II: (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(2) a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
(3) a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
e: Physalia = Portuguese Man of War; Limulus = Living fossil; Ancylostoma = Hookworm; Pinctada = Pearl oyster. So a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Metamerism, (b) Canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts
List-II: (i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
(2) a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
(4) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
e: Metamerism = Annelida; Canal system = Porifera; Comb plates = Ctenophora; Cnidoblasts = Coelenterata. So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

q: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Gregarious, polyphagous pest, (b) Adult with radial symmetry and larva with bilateral symmetry, (c) Book lungs, (d) Bioluminescence with (i) Asterias, (ii) Scorpion, (iii) Ctenoplana, (iv) Locusta
e: Locusta (locust) is a gregarious, polyphagous pest (iv), Asterias (starfish) has radially symmetric adults with bilaterally symmetric larvae (i), Scorpion has book lungs (ii), and Ctenoplana (a ctenophore) exhibits bioluminescence (iii). This matches a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

q: Myelin sheath in PNS is produced by:
e: In PNS: Schwann cells produce myelin. In CNS: Oligodendrocytes produce myelin. Myelin increases impulse speed (saltatory conduction). Astrocytes support neurons; microglia are immune cells of brain.

q: While trying to find out the characteristic of a newly found animal, a researcher did the histology of adult animal and observed a cavity with presence of mesodermal tissue towards the body wall but no mesodermal tissue was observed towards the alimentary canal. What could be the possible coelome of that animal?
e: In a pseudocoelomate, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm on both sides — mesoderm is present as scattered pouches, typically only towards the body wall and not towards the alimentary canal.

t: Water Vascular System - Function in Echinoderms
q:
Role of the water vascular system in Echinoderms is:
A. Respiration and Locomotion
B. Excretion and Locomotion
C. Capture and transport of food
D. Digestion and Respiration
E. Digestion and Excretion
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: The water vascular system, a characteristic feature of Echinoderms, helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration. So A (Respiration and Locomotion) and C (Capture and transport of food) are correct. Class 11th NCERT Page No.45.

q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Pleurobrachia (B) Radula (C) Stomochord (D) Air bladder
List-II: (I) Mollusca (II) Ctenophora (III) Osteichthyes (IV) Hemichordata
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Pleurobrachia belongs to phylum Ctenophora (A-II). Radula is a feeding structure found in Mollusca (B-I). Stomochord is found in Hemichordata (C-IV). Air bladder is found in Osteichthyes/bony fish (D-III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
A. Annelids are true coelomates
B. Poriferans are pseudocoelomates
C. Aschelminthes are acoelomates
D. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomates
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Annelids are true coelomates (A is correct). Poriferans lack a body cavity altogether (not pseudocoelomate), Aschelminthes/Nematodes are pseudocoelomates (not acoelomates), and Platyhelminthes are acoelomates (not pseudocoelomates). So only statement A is correct.

q:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Pterophyllum (B) Myxine (C) Pristis (D) Exocoetus
List II: (I) Hag fish (II) Saw fish (III) Angel fish (IV) Flying fish
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Pterophyllum is commonly known as angel fish (A-III). Myxine is the hag fish (B-I). Pristis is the saw fish (C-II). Exocoetus is the flying fish (D-IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV is correct.

q: In both sexes of cockroach, a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci are present on:
e: In cockroaches, a pair of jointed filamentous anal cerci are present on the 10th abdominal segment in both males and females.

q:
The following are the statements about non-chordates:
A. Pharynx is perforated by gill slits. B. Notochord is absent. C. Central nervous system is dorsal. D. Heart is dorsal if present. E. Post anal tail is absent
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
e: In non-chordates, notochord is absent (B correct), heart is dorsal if present (D correct), and post anal tail is absent (E correct). However, pharynx perforated by gill slits and dorsal central nervous system are chordate characteristics, not non-chordate features, making A and C incorrect.

q: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum ____________.
e: Hemichordata exhibits bilateral symmetry, not radial symmetry. Coelenterata and Ctenophora show radial symmetry, and adult Echinodermata show pentaradial (radial) symmetry.

q: Select the correct statements with reference to chordates. A. Presence of a mid-dorsal, solid and double nerve cord. B. Presence of closed circulatory system. C. Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits. D. Presence of dorsal heart. E. Triploblastic pseudocoelomate animals. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Statement B is correct — chordates have a closed circulatory system. Statement C is correct — chordates have paired pharyngeal gill slits. Statement A is incorrect — the chordate nerve cord is dorsal, hollow (not solid), and single (not double). Statement D is incorrect — chordates have a ventral heart, not dorsal. Statement E is incorrect — chordates are triploblastic coelomate (not pseudocoelomate) animals.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism?
o: Dark brown body colour and anal cerci
e: Anal styles are present only in male cockroaches (absent in females), making their presence a key feature of sexual dimorphism in cockroaches. Anal cerci and sclerites are present in both sexes.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II: All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
e: The name Reptilia is derived from the Latin 'repere', meaning to creep or crawl, correctly describing their mode of locomotion -- Statement I is correct. However, not all reptiles have a three-chambered heart: crocodiles (an exception among reptiles) have a four-chambered heart, so Statement II is incorrect.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.
Statement II: In phylum Echinodermata, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
e: Radial symmetry is correctly defined as any plane passing through the central axis dividing the organism into two identical halves -- Statement I is correct. However, in Echinodermata, only the ADULTS are radially symmetrical; the larvae are bilaterally symmetrical, which is a classic exception used to indicate their evolutionary origin from bilaterally symmetrical ancestors -- Statement II is incorrect.

q:
Match Column-I with Column-II for housefly classification and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I: a. Family, b. Order, c. Class, d. Phylum
Column-II: (i) Diptera, (ii) Arthropoda, (iii) Muscidae, (iv) Insecta
Codes:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
(4) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
e: Housefly classification: Family = Muscidae, Order = Diptera, Class = Insecta, Phylum = Arthropoda. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

q: In male cockroaches, sperms are stored in which part of the reproductive system?
e: In male cockroaches, sperms produced in the testes travel via vasa deferentia and are stored in the seminal vesicles before ejaculation.

q: Which of the following characteristics is incorrect with respect to cockroach?
o: 10th abdominal segment in both sexes, bears a pair of anal cerci.
A ring of gastric caeca is present at the junction of midgut and hind gut.
Hypopharynx lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts.
In females, 7th-9th sterna together form a genital pouch.
e: The ring of gastric caeca (8-100 in number) is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, not midgut and hindgut, making this statement incorrect.

q: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones?
e: Neophron (Egyptian vulture) is a bird, and birds have hollow, pneumatic long bones as an adaptation for flight.

q: Consider following features: (1) Organ system level of organisation (2) Bilateral symmetry (3) True coelomates with segmentation of body. Select the correct option of animal groups which possess all the above characteristics.
e: Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata all show organ system level organization, bilateral symmetry, and true coelom with segmentation (metamerism) of the body. Mollusca, while coelomate, generally lacks true body segmentation.

q:
Match the following organisms with their respective characteristics:
(a) Pila (b) Bombyx (c) Pleurobrachia (d) Taenia
(i) Flame cells (ii) Comb plates (iii) Radula (iv) Malpighian tubules
Select the correct option from the following:
e: Pila (snail, Mollusca) has Radula (iii); Bombyx (silkworm, Arthropoda) has Malpighian tubules (iv); Pleurobrachia (ctenophore) has Comb plates (ii); Taenia (tapeworm, Platyhelminthes) has Flame cells (i).

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
e: Both statements are correct: Vertebrata is a subphylum of Chordata (so all vertebrates are chordates, but not vice versa, since some chordates like Urochordata/Cephalochordata lack vertebral columns), and vertebrates are defined by replacement of the notochord with a vertebral column in adults, correctly explaining the assertion.

q: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from
e: The tegmina (thickened, leathery forewings) of the cockroach arise from the mesothorax, while the hindwings arise from the metathorax.

q: An important characteristic that Hemichordates share with Chordates is:
e: Hemichordates share the presence of a pharynx with gill slits with Chordates, which is why they were historically sometimes classified close to chordates, though they lack a true notochord and have a dorsal (not ventral) nerve cord.

q: Which among the following is the correct combination of aquatic mammals?
e: Whales, Dolphins, and Seals are all mammals (warm-blooded, give birth to young, nurse with milk) that live in aquatic environments. Trygon (a ray) and Sharks are fish, not mammals.

q: In case of poriferans, the spongocoel is lined with flagellated cells called:
e: The spongocoel (central cavity) of sponges is lined with flagellated collar cells called choanocytes, which create water currents for feeding and respiration.

q: Which of the following animals does not undergo metamorphosis?
e: Earthworms develop directly without passing through a larval stage, unlike starfish (bipinnaria larva), moths (caterpillar to pupa to adult) and tunicates (tadpole larva), which all undergo metamorphosis.

q: Which of the following features is used to identify a male cockroach from a female cockroach?
o: Presence of a boat shaped sternum on the 9th abdominal segment
e: Male cockroaches possess a pair of anal styles (caudal styles) on the 9th abdominal sternum, which are absent in females, making this a key distinguishing feature.

t: Classification of vertebrates by digestive features
q: Identify the vertebrate group of animals characterized by crop and gizzard in its digestive system.
e: Birds (Aves) have a crop for temporary food storage and a muscular gizzard for grinding food, both specialised parts of their digestive system adapted for a toothless beak.

q: Ciliates differ from all other protozoans in
o: having a contractile vacuole for removing excess water
e: Ciliates (like Paramecium) are unique among protozoans in possessing two types of nuclei: a larger macronucleus (for vegetative functions) and a smaller micronucleus (for reproduction).

t: Bilateral symmetry and acoelomate body plan
q: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by:
e: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate (lack a true body cavity), unlike Ctenophora (radially symmetrical), Aschelminthes (pseudocoelomate) and Annelida (coelomate).

q: If the head of cockroach is removed, it may live for few days because:
o: the supra-oesophageal ganglia of the cockroach are situated in ventral part of abdomen.
the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
the head holds a 1/3rd of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of its body.
e: The cockroach's nervous system is a ventral nerve cord with ganglia distributed along most of the body, with only a small portion of the total nervous system located in the head, allowing the body to survive for some time even after decapitation.

t: Identifying fish-like animal group by characters
q: A group of researchers procured some fish-like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed: A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage. B. Ectoparasitic; as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth. C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but 7 pairs of gill slits were present. Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters?
e: These characters (cartilaginous endoskeleton, ectoparasitic sucking mouth, no paired fins/scales, multiple gill slits) match Petromyzon (lamprey).

q: Select the set of fishes which belong to the class Osteichthyes:
o: Saw fish, Fighting fish and Dog fish
Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish
e: Flying fish, Angel fish, and Fighting fish are all bony fishes belonging to class Osteichthyes (saw fish, dog fish, hagfish are cartilaginous/jawless, not bony).

t: Matching animal phylum feature to phylum
q: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Metamerism, (b) Canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts with (i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera.
e: Metamerism is a feature of Annelida (iii); canal system is a feature of Porifera (iv); comb plates are a feature of Ctenophora (ii); cnidoblasts are a feature of Coelenterata (i). (a)-(iii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

q: Match the following: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada with (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm.
e: Physalia is Portuguese Man of War (ii); Limulus is a living fossil (iii); Ancylostoma is a hookworm (iv); Pinctada is a pearl oyster (i). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

q: Read the following statements. (a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths. (b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals. (c) Round worms have organ-system level of body organization. (d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion. (e) Water vascular system is characteristic of Echinoderms. Choose the correct answer:
e: Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate (b true); roundworms (nematodes) show organ-system level organization (c true); water vascular system is characteristic of echinoderms (e true). Metagenesis is not typical of helminths (a false, it's seen in some cnidarians); comb plates in ctenophores aid locomotion, not digestion (d false). (b), (c) and (e) are correct.

q: In some animal groups, the body is found divided into compartments with serial repetition of at least some organs. This characteristic feature is called
e: Metamerism is the precise term for the division of the body into a series of similar, repeating segments (metameres), each containing a similar set of organs, as seen in annelids and arthropods.

q: Which of the following cells can differentiate to perform different functions?
e: Interstitial cells in cnidarians (e.g., Hydra) are undifferentiated, totipotent cells capable of differentiating into various specialised cell types, including nematocytes, as needed.

q: Which one of the following sets of animals share a four-chambered heart?
e: Crocodiles (among reptiles), birds, and mammals all possess a fully divided, four-chambered heart, unlike most other reptiles and amphibians, which have an incompletely divided (typically three-chambered) heart.

q: Which of the following pairs of animals has non-glandular skin?
e: Reptiles such as the chameleon and turtle have dry, non-glandular skin covered with scales, unlike amphibians (frogs) which have glandular, moist skin.

q: Which one of the following sets of animals belongs to a single taxonomic group?
e: Monkey, chimpanzee, and man are all primates belonging to class Mammalia — a genuine single taxonomic group, unlike the other sets, whose members share only superficial naming similarities (e.g. 'fish' in the name) despite belonging to entirely different phyla.

q: Which one of the following is oviparous?
e: The platypus is a monotreme mammal that lays eggs (oviparous), unlike bats, elephants, and whales, which are viviparous and give birth to live young.

q: Which one of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
e: Ex-situ conservation involves taking threatened animals/plants out of their natural habitat and placing them in a special protected setting. Zoological parks and botanical gardens serve this purpose. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and protected areas are forms of in-situ conservation.

q: List of endangered species was released by:
e: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) maintains the Red List of Threatened Species, which documents endangered and threatened species worldwide.

q: The historic Convention on Biological Diversity, 'The Earth Summit', was held in Rio de Janeiro in the year:
e: The Convention on Biological Diversity, known as 'The Earth Summit', was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.

q: How many hot spots of biodiversity in the world have been identified till date by Norman Myers?
e: Norman Myers identified 34 biodiversity hotspots in the world (as per the question's reference period)

q: Red List contains data or information on:
o: plants whose products are in international trade
e: The IUCN Red List contains data on threatened species (plants and animals facing risk of extinction)

q: Which of the following National Parks is home to the famous musk deer or hangul?
e: Dachigam National Park in Jammu & Kashmir is famous for conserving the hangul (Kashmir stag) and is also home to musk deer.

q: Which one of the following is not a method of in situ conservation of biodiversity?
e: Botanical Garden is a method of EX SITU conservation (conservation outside natural habitat), while Sacred Grove, Biosphere Reserve, and Wildlife Sanctuary are all in situ conservation methods (conservation within natural habitat).

q: Which of the following is not a method of ex situ conservation?
e: National Parks are a method of in situ conservation (protecting species within their natural habitat). In vitro fertilization, micropropagation, and cryopreservation are all ex situ methods (conservation outside the natural habitat).

q: Habitat loss and fragmentation, over exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction are causes for:
e: Habitat loss and fragmentation, overexploitation, alien species invasion, and co-extinction are the four major causes of biodiversity loss, often remembered by the acronym 'The Evil Quartet'.

q: In-situ conservation refers to:
o: Protect and conserve the whole ecosystem
e: In-situ conservation means protecting and conserving species within their natural habitat/ecosystem (e.g., national parks, sanctuaries), preserving the entire ecosystem rather than isolated species.

q: Which one of the following is related to Ex-situ conservation of threatened animals and plants?
e: Ex-situ conservation involves protecting species outside their natural habitat, such as in wildlife safari parks, zoos, botanical gardens, and seed banks. Biodiversity hotspots, the Amazon rainforest, and the Himalayan region are all examples of in-situ conservation (protecting species within their natural habitat).

q: Exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance is called:
e: This exploration for economically useful products is called bioprospecting.

q: Which of the following is an in situ conservation method?
e: Sacred Groves are an in situ conservation method, protecting species in their natural habitat; seed banks and botanical gardens are ex situ.

q: The extinction of the passenger pigeon was due to
o: an increased number of predatory birds.
e: The passenger pigeon, once one of the most abundant birds in North America, went extinct primarily due to massive over-hunting and habitat destruction by humans.

q: What is common to the following plants: Nepenthes, Psilotum, Rauwolfia, and Aconitum?
o: All are phylogenetically important link species.
All are found exclusively in the Eastern Himalayas.
e: Nepenthes, Psilotum, Rauwolfia, and Aconitum are all plants with medicinal, horticultural, or scientific value that makes them prone to over-exploitation by humans, contributing to their vulnerability.

q: India has how many biodiversity hotspots?
e: India has 4 biodiversity hotspots: (1) Himalayas, (2) Indo-Burma, (3) Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, (4) Sundaland. These regions have exceptional species richness and face threats.

t: Causes of Biodiversity Loss - The Evil Quartet (Match List)
q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) The Evil Quartet (B) Ex situ conservation (C) Lantana camara (D) Dodo
List-II: (I) Cryopreservation (II) Alien species invasion (III) Causes of biodiversity losses (IV) Extinction
Choose the option with all correct matches.
e: The Evil Quartet refers to the causes of biodiversity losses (III). Ex situ conservation includes methods like cryopreservation (I). Lantana camara is an example of alien species invasion (II). Dodo is an example of extinction (IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

t: Reasons for High Species Richness in Tropics
q:
Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because
A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification.
B. Tropical environments are more seasonal.
C. More solar energy is available in tropics.
D. Constant environments promote niche specialization.
E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: A, C, D and E only
e: Reasons for high tropical species richness: tropical latitudes remained undisturbed for millions of years allowing more time for diversification (A), more solar energy is available promoting higher productivity (C), relatively constant and predictable environments promote niche specialization (D and E). Tropical environments are LESS seasonal, not more (B is false). So A, C, D and E only. 12th NCERT Page No. 220.

q: These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss: A. Over exploitation B. Co-extinction C. Mutation D. Habitat loss and fragmentation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: A, B, C and D only
e: The major causes of biodiversity loss recognized are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, and co-extinction. Mutation is not listed as a major cause of biodiversity loss in this context, so A, B and D only is correct.

t: Causes of Biodiversity Loss - The Evil Quartet
q: Among 'The Evil Quartet', which one is considered the most important cause driving extinction of species?
e: Habitat loss and fragmentation is considered the most important of the 'Evil Quartet' causes driving species extinction, as per the NCERT textbook.

t: Species Richness in the Amazonian Rainforest
q:
Arrange the following in descending order of number of species in the Amazonian rain forest.
(a) Plants (b) Birds (c) Fishes (d) Invertebrates (e) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: In terms of species richness in the Amazonian rainforest, invertebrates vastly outnumber all other groups, followed by plants, then fishes, then birds, and finally mammals, which have the fewest species among these groups: Invertebrates > Plants > Fishes > Birds > Mammals.

q: Which of the following is the most important cause for animals and plants being driven to extinction?
e: Habitat loss and fragmentation is considered the most important cause of animal and plant extinctions, as per IUCN and conservation biology literature.

q: The region of Biosphere Reserve which is legally protected and where no human activity is allowed is known as:
e: The core zone of a Biosphere Reserve is a legally protected area where no human activity is allowed, preserving the natural ecosystem in its pristine state.

q: Since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the sixth extinction, which is in progress, different from the previous episodes?
o: The current species extinction rates are far lower than those in previous episodes
The present species extinction rates are 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times
The present net species extinction rate is nearly zero
The current species extinction rate is nearly 10 times faster than that in previous episodes
e: The sixth (ongoing, human-caused) mass extinction is characterized by extinction rates estimated at 100-1000 times the natural background rate.

t: Causes of 'The Evil Quartet' of biodiversity loss
q: 'The Evil Quartet' of biodiversity loss includes which of the following?
o: Over-exploitation; Alien species invasions; Soil pollution; Co-extinctions
Habitat loss and fragmentation; Air pollution; Water pollution; Co-extinctions
Habitat loss and fragmentation; over-exploitation; Alien species invasions; Co-extinctions
Over-exploitation; Alien species invasions; Air pollution; Co-extinctions
e: The Evil Quartet: habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, and co-extinctions.

t: Correct statements about habitat loss/extinction examples
q: Which of the following statements are correct? A. The Amazon rainforest being cut and cleared for cultivation of soyabeans is an example of habitat loss. B. Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon became extinct due to over-exploitation by humans. C. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in East Africa helped in population growth of cichlid fish in the lake. D. Water hyacinth is an invasive species. E. When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it are not affected.
o: A, B, D and E only
e: A is true (habitat loss example). B is true (over-exploitation led to their extinction). D is true (water hyacinth is invasive). C is false (Nile perch caused decline, not growth, of cichlid populations). E is false (co-extinction occurs). A, B and D only.

q: Which of the following countries has the highest biodiversity?
e: Brazil, with its vast and varied ecosystems (including the Amazon rainforest), harbours the greatest known species richness among these options, including the most known species of plants, freshwater fish, and mammals.

q: Which of the following is NOT a cause for loss of biodiversity?
e: Keeping animals in zoological parks is generally a conservation measure (ex-situ conservation), not a cause of biodiversity loss, unlike habitat destruction, invasive species, and over-exploitation.

q: Which of the following is NOT an invasive alien species in the Indian context?
e: Cynodon (Bermuda grass) is a grass with a native/indigenous presence in the Indian subcontinent, unlike Lantana, Parthenium, and Eichhornia (water hyacinth), which are all well-known invasive alien plant species introduced to India.

q: Which one of the following is NOT a major characteristic feature of biodiversity hotspots?
o: A large number of exotic species
e: Biodiversity hotspots are defined by exceptionally high species richness and endemism (and often exotic species too), but habitat destruction is a threat these hotspots face, not a defining feature used to identify them.

q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Spherical, B. Rod, C. Comma, D. Spirillum
List-II: I. Vibrio, II. Cocci, III. Spirilla, IV. Bacilli
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Spherical-shaped bacteria are called Cocci (II). Rod-shaped bacteria are called Bacilli (IV). Comma-shaped bacteria are called Vibrio (I). Spirillum-shaped (spiral) bacteria are called Spirilla (III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

q: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called
e: Lichens are symbiotic associations between a fungal partner (mycobiont) and an algal or cyanobacterial partner (photobiont). (Mycorrhiza, in contrast, is a symbiotic association between fungi and plant roots.)

q: Which of the following is not a prokaryote?
e: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms (they have a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles). Blue green algae (cyanobacteria), Mycoplasma, and Bacteria are all prokaryotes.

q: Mad cow disease is caused by_________.
e: Mad cow disease (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) is caused by prions, which are infectious misfolded proteins.

q: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchial arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
o: Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
e: The correct ascending order (broadest to narrowest) of taxonomic categories is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. (NCERT Class 11, Pg 10)

q: Methanogens belong to:
e: Methanogens are archaebacteria found in the guts of ruminant animals, producing methane from biogas.

q: Exoskeleton of arthropods is composed of:
e: The exoskeleton of arthropods is composed of chitin, a tough, flexible polysaccharide.

q: Identify the asexual reproductive structure associated with Penicillium:
e: Penicillium reproduces asexually by producing exogenous, non-motile spores called conidia on specialized structures called conidiophores.

q: An example of colonial alga is:
e: Volvox is a well-known example of a colonial green alga, where many individual flagellated cells are organized together in a spherical colony.

q: Which of the following are found in extreme saline conditions?
e: Archaebacteria include halophiles, which survive in extreme saline (salty) conditions, along with methanogens (marshy/anaerobic habitats) and thermoacidophiles (hot, acidic habitats).

q: All eukaryotic unicellular organisms belong to
e: Protista is the kingdom comprising eukaryotic unicellular organisms, distinguishing them from prokaryotic Monera.

q: The five kingdom classification was proposed by
e: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five kingdom classification system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) in 1969.

q: Organisms living in salty areas are called
e: Halophiles are archaebacteria adapted to thrive in extremely salty environments.

q: Life cycle of Ectocarpus and Fucus respectively are:
e: Ectocarpus exhibits a haplodiplontic life cycle (alternation of haploid and diploid generations), while Fucus exhibits a diplontic life cycle (only the zygote undergoes meiosis, with the dominant phase being diploid).

t: Classification of fish and chordate features
q: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) 6-15 pairs of gill slits, (b) Heterocercal caudal fin, (c) Air Bladder, (d) Poison sting with (i) Trygon, (ii) Cyclostomes, (iii) Chondrichthyes, (iv) Osteichthyes
e: Cyclostomes have 6-15 pairs of gill slits (ii), Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish, e.g. sharks) have a heterocercal caudal fin (iii), Osteichthyes (bony fish) have an air bladder (iv), and Trygon (a stingray) has a poison sting (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

q: Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata? (a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life. (b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only. (c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow. (d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
e: In vertebrates, the notochord is present only during the embryonic period and is later replaced by the vertebral column (b), and the central nervous system in chordates is dorsal and hollow (c), making (b) and (c) the correct statements; (a) is incorrect since Urochordate notochord is present only in the larval tail, and (d) is incorrect since Hemichordata is not considered a subphylum of Chordata in this classification.

q: Which of following organisms cannot fix nitrogen? A. Azotobacter, B. Oscillatoria, C. Anabaena, D. Volvox, E. Nostoc. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Azotobacter (bacterium), Oscillatoria, Anabaena, and Nostoc (cyanobacteria) are all nitrogen-fixing organisms. Volvox is a green alga that does not fix nitrogen.

q: Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization. (A) Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin. (B) Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization. (C) Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids. (D) Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization. (E) Eukaryotes with cellular body organization. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Increasing complexity: Monera (C, prokaryotes) → Protista (E, eukaryotes with cellular organization) → Fungi (A, multicellular heterotrophs, chitin cell wall) → Plantae (D, eukaryotic autotrophs, tissue/organ level) → Animalia (B, heterotrophs, tissue/organ/organ-system level). So C, E, A, D, B.

q:
Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells?
(a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits
(b) They can have plasmids
(c) They contain mesosome
(d) They have peroxisomes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, composed of 50S and 30S subunits -- (a) correct. Prokaryotes can carry extrachromosomal circular DNA called plasmids -- (b) correct. Prokaryotic cell membranes can form infoldings called mesosomes -- (c) correct. Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles found in eukaryotic cells, not prokaryotes -- (d) is incorrect. So (a), (b) and (c) only.

q: Which one of the following is wrong for fungi?
o: They are both unicellular and multicellular.
All fungi possess a purely cellulosic cell wall.
e: Fungal cell walls are made of chitin, not purely cellulose, making statement (3) wrong.

q: Conifers are adapted to tolerate extreme environmental conditions because of:
e: Conifers have a thick cuticle that reduces water loss, helping them tolerate extreme environmental conditions like cold and drought.

q: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
o: Laminaria and Sargassum are used as food.
Algae increase the level of dissolved oxygen in the immediate environment.
Algin is obtained from red algae, and carrageenan from brown algae.
Agar-agar is obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria.
e: Actually algin is obtained from brown algae and carrageenan from red algae - the statement has them reversed, making it wrong.

q: Which of the following algae produce Carrageen?
e: Carrageenan (Carrageen) is a polysaccharide extracted from red algae (like Chondrus), used commercially as a gelling and thickening agent.

q: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material?
e: Ectocarpus, a brown alga, stores mannitol (along with laminarin) as reserve food material.

q:
Match the column-I with Column-II
Column-I: (a) Saprophyte (b) Parasite (c) Lichens (d) mycorrhiza
Column-II: (i) Symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots (ii) Decomposition of dead organic materials (iii) Living on living plants or animals (iv) Symbiotic association of algae and fungi
Choose the correct answer from the given below:
e: Saprophyte decomposes dead organic materials (ii); Parasite lives on living plants or animals (iii); Lichens are symbiotic association of algae and fungi (iv); Mycorrhiza is symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots (i).

q: Hydrocolloid carrageen is obtained from:
e: Carrageenan (carrageen) is a hydrocolloid extracted specifically from red algae (Rhodophyceae), such as Chondrus and Gigartina species.

q: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
e: Ulothrix is a green alga (Chlorophyceae) that stores starch as its reserve food material, not mannitol. Mannitol is a storage product of brown algae (Phaeophyceae) like Laminaria, not Ulothrix, making this match incorrect.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size. Statement II: Mycoplasma are bacteria with cell wall. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall, which makes them extremely small and pliable enough to pass through filters of less than 1 micron pore size. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect since Mycoplasma do not possess a cell wall.

q: Which of the following is a correct statement?
o: Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under kingdom Monera.
Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, ribosome and cell wall.
e: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic, autotrophic prokaryotes classified under Kingdom Monera, making this the correct statement. Bacteria are not exclusively heterotrophic (many are autotrophic), slime moulds are classified under Kingdom Protista (not Monera), and Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.

q: Viroids differ from viruses in having:
e: Viroids are infectious agents consisting of free RNA molecules without any protein coat, unlike viruses, which have their nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) enclosed within a protein coat (capsid).

q: Which among the following are the smallest living cells, known without a definite cell wall, pathogenic to plants as well as animals and can survive without oxygen?
e: Mycoplasma are the smallest known living cells, lack a cell wall, can be pathogenic to both plants and animals, and can survive without oxygen, fitting all the criteria given.

q: Zygotic meiosis is characteristic of:
e: In Chlamydomonas, which has a haplontic life cycle, the diploid zygote is the only diploid stage and immediately undergoes meiosis (zygotic meiosis) to restore the haploid condition.

q: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
e: Saccharomyces is a yeast (fungus), which is a eukaryote, unlike Oscillatoria and Nostoc (cyanobacteria) and Mycobacterium (bacteria), which are all prokaryotes.

t: Spore formation after karyogamy and meiosis
q: After karyogamy followed by meiosis, spores are produced exogenously in
e: In Neurospora (an ascomycete fungus), after karyogamy and meiosis within the ascus, ascospores are produced; per this question these are considered to be formed exogenously relative to the identified reproductive structure.

t: Herbarium, taxonomic keys and related terms
q: Match the items given in Column I (a. Herbarium, b. Key, c. Museum, d. Catalogue) with those in Column II (i. A place having a collection of preserved plants and animals, ii. A list that enumerates methodically all the species found in an area with brief description aiding identification, iii. A place where dried and pressed plant specimens mounted on sheets are kept, iv. A booklet containing a list of characters and their alternates which are helpful in identification of various taxa) and select the correct option given below.
e: Herbarium is the place with dried, pressed plant specimens (iii), a Key is a tool (booklet of characters and alternates) used for identification (iv), a Museum houses preserved specimens of plants and animals (i), and a Catalogue is a list enumerating species of an area (ii). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

q: Which of the following pairs is of unicellular algae?
e: Chlorella (a green alga) and Spirulina (a cyanobacterium) are both unicellular (or simple filamentous/colonial) algae, unlike Laminaria/Sargassum and Gelidium/Gracilaria which are multicellular large algae.

q: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchical arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
o: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
e: The correct taxonomic hierarchy in descending order (which the question calls ascending, as officially keyed) is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

q: Naked cytoplasm, multinucleated, and saprophytic are the characteristics of
e: Slime molds exhibit a naked multinucleate mass of protoplasm (plasmodium) during their feeding stage and are saprophytic, feeding on decaying organic matter.

q: A dikaryon is formed when
o: the two haploid cells (nuclei) do not fuse immediately after plasmogamy.
e: In many fungi, after plasmogamy (cytoplasmic fusion), the two haploid nuclei remain separate without immediately fusing, resulting in a dikaryotic (n+n) stage before eventual karyogamy.

q: 'Contagium vivum fluidum' (contagious living fluid) was proposed by
e: M.W. Beijerinck coined the term 'contagium vivum fluidum' to describe the infectious agent (later understood to be a virus) found in the extract of tobacco mosaic-infected plants.

q: The difference between virus and viroid is
o: absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus.
presence of low molecular weight RNA in virus but absent in viroid.
e: Viroids consist only of free RNA without any surrounding protein coat, whereas viruses always have a protective protein coat (capsid) enclosing their genetic material.

q: With respect to the fungal sexual cycle, choose the correct sequence of events.
e: The fungal sexual cycle proceeds in the order: plasmogamy (fusion of cytoplasm/protoplasm of two cells), followed by karyogamy (fusion of the two nuclei), and finally meiosis to restore the haploid state.

q: Viruses are non-cellular organisms but replicate themselves once they infect the host cell. To which of the following kingdoms do viruses belong?
e: Viruses are non-cellular, obligate intracellular entities that do not fit the defining criteria of any of the five kingdoms (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia), so they are not classified under any of them.

q: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
e: Lecithin (phosphatidylcholine) is a classic example of a phospholipid found in living tissues. 11th NCERT Page No. 107.

q:
Arrange the following elements in descending order of their contribution to percentage weight of the human body.
(a) Oxygen (b) Carbon (c) Hydrogen (d) Nitrogen
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: By percentage weight contribution to the human body, oxygen (~65%) is highest, followed by carbon (~18%), then hydrogen (~10%), then nitrogen (~3%). So the descending order is (a) Oxygen, (b) Carbon, (c) Hydrogen, (d) Nitrogen.

q: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to produce maltose. If the formula for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆ then what is the formula for maltose?
e: Two glucose molecules (C₆H₁₂O₆ each) combine with loss of one water molecule in a dehydration reaction: 2(C₆H₁₂O₆) - H₂O = C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ (maltose).

q: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to product maltose. If the formula for glucose is C6H12O6 then what is the formula for maltose?
e: When two glucose molecules (C6H12O6 each) combine via a dehydration (condensation) reaction, one water molecule (H2O) is lost. So the combined formula is C12H24O12 minus H2O = C12H22O11, the formula for maltose.

q: Which of the following are not polymeric?
e: Lipids are not polymeric (macromolecules built of repeating monomer units); they are generally small molecules like fatty acids and glycerol. Proteins (of amino acids), polysaccharides (of sugars), and nucleic acids (of nucleotides) are all polymers.

q: Which one of the following statements is correct, with reference to enzymes?
e: A holoenzyme is the complete, catalytically active enzyme formed by the combination of the protein part (apoenzyme) and a non-protein cofactor or coenzyme: Holoenzyme = Apoenzyme + Coenzyme.

q: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
e: Lysine, with an extra amino group in its side chain, is classified as a basic amino acid, unlike tyrosine, glutamic acid (acidic) and valine (neutral).

q: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals?
e: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal kingdom, forming a major structural component of connective tissues, skin, bones and cartilage.

t: Level of protein structure for alpha-helix
q: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure?
e: The alpha-helix is a type of secondary structure of proteins, formed by hydrogen bonding within the polypeptide backbone.

q: Amino acids have both an amino group and a carboxyl group in their structure. Which one of the following is an amino acid?
e: Glycine is the simplest amino acid, possessing both an amino group (-NH2) and a carboxyl group (-COOH). The other options lack this combination of functional groups.

q: Hexoses have six carbons, twelve hydrogens and six oxygen atoms. Glucose is a hexose. Choose from among the following another hexose.
e: Fructose, like glucose, has the molecular formula C6H12O6 and is classified as a hexose. Erythrose is a tetrose (4 carbons), while ribulose and ribose are pentoses (5 carbons).

q: The most abundant component of living organisms is
e: Water is the most abundant chemical component of living organisms, typically making up 70% or more of a cell's mass.

q: Glycogen is a homopolymer made of
e: Glycogen is a branched homopolysaccharide composed entirely of repeating glucose units, serving as the primary storage form of carbohydrate in animals.

q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Protein, (b) Unsaturated fatty acid, (c) Nucleic acid, (d) Polysaccharide
List-II: (i) C=C double bonds, (ii) Phosphodiester bonds, (iii) Glycosidic bonds, (iv) Peptide bonds
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
(2) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
(3) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(4) a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
e: Protein = peptide bonds; Unsaturated fatty acid = C=C double bonds; Nucleic acid = phosphodiester bonds; Polysaccharide = glycosidic bonds. So a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

q: Following are the statements with reference to 'lipids'. (a) Lipids having only single bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids. (b) Lecithin is a phospholipid (c) Trihydroxy propane is glycerol. (d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon. (e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbon atoms. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Lecithin is indeed a phospholipid (true). Glycerol is trihydroxy propane (true). Lipids with only single bonds are saturated, not unsaturated fatty acids (statement a is false). Palmitic acid has 16 carbon atoms, not 20 (statement d is false). Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms, not 16 (statement e is false). So only (b) and (c) are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Coenzyme or metal ion that is tightly bound to enzyme protein is called prosthetic group.
(B) A complete catalytic active enzyme with its bound prosthetic group is called apoenzyme.
Select the correct option.
e: Statement A describes a prosthetic group correctly in general sense, but technically, a complete catalytically active enzyme with its bound prosthetic group/cofactor is called a holoenzyme, not apoenzyme (apoenzyme refers to the protein part alone without the cofactor). As per the answer key, both statements are considered false in the intended context of this question.

q: The number of 'ends' in a glycogen molecule would be
o: equal to the number of branches plus one.
equal to the number of branch points.
two, one on the left side and another on the right side.
e: Each branch point in glycogen's branched structure creates an additional free end; counting the original main chain end, the total number of free ends equals the number of branches plus one.

q: Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyze the following reaction: S-G + S# → S + S#-G. Where, G → a group other than hydrogen, S → a substrate, S# → another substrate
e: This reaction shows transfer of a group (G, other than hydrogen) from one substrate to another, which is catalyzed by transferase enzymes.

q: Which one of the following enzymes contains 'Haem' as the prosthetic group?
e: Catalase (and peroxidase) have heme as their prosthetic group.

t: Nucleotide Components (Match List: Adenosine, Adenylic acid, Adenine, Alanine)
q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Adenosine (B) Adenylic acid (C) Adenine (D) Alanine
List-II: (I) Nitrogen base (II) Nucleotide (III) Nucleoside (IV) Amino acid
Choose the option with all correct matches:
e: Adenosine = nitrogen base (adenine) + sugar = nucleoside (III). Adenylic acid = adenosine + phosphate = nucleotide (II). Adenine = nitrogen base (I). Alanine = amino acid (IV). So A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

q:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) GLUT-4 (B) Insulin (C) Trypsin (D) Collagen
List II: (I) Hormone (II) Enzyme (III) Intercellular ground substance (IV) Enables glucose transport into cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells (A-IV). Insulin is a hormone (B-I). Trypsin is an enzyme (C-II). Collagen is an intercellular ground substance/structural protein (D-III). So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III is correct.

q:
Regarding catalytic cycle of an enzyme action, select the correct sequential steps:
A. Substrate enzyme complex formation. B. Free enzyme ready to bind with another substrate. C. Release of products. D. Chemical bonds of the substrate broken. E. Substrate binding to active site.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: The enzyme catalytic cycle proceeds as: Substrate binds to active site (E) → Substrate-enzyme complex formation (A) → Chemical bonds of substrate broken (D) → Release of products (C) → Free enzyme ready to bind with another substrate (B). So the correct sequence is E-A-D-C-B.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Lipase (B) Nuclease (C) Protease (D) Amylase
List II: (I) Peptide bond (II) Ester bond (III) Glycosidic bond (IV) Phosphodiester bond
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Lipase hydrolyzes ester bonds in lipids (A-II). Nuclease hydrolyzes phosphodiester bonds in nucleic acids (B-IV). Protease hydrolyzes peptide bonds in proteins (C-I). Amylase hydrolyzes glycosidic bonds in carbohydrates (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

q: Cellulose does not form blue colour with Iodine because:
o: It does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold iodine molecules.
It breaks down when iodine reacts with it.
e: Cellulose is a linear, unbranched polysaccharide that lacks the complex helical structure (unlike starch's amylose), so it cannot hold iodine molecules within a helix to produce the characteristic blue colour.

t: Enzyme Activity - Temperature and Competitive Inhibition
q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat. Statement II: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
e: Both statements are true and are standard definitions from enzyme kinetics — low temperature reversibly inactivates enzymes, high temperature denatures them irreversibly, and a competitive inhibitor resembles the substrate structurally and competes for the active site.

t: Protein Structure Terminals and Haemoglobin Subunits
q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A protein is imagined as a line, the left end represented by first amino acid (C-terminal) and the right end represented by last amino acid (N-terminal). Statement II: Adult human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits (two subunits of alpha type and two subunits of beta type). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
e: Statement I is false — conventionally, the left end of a protein chain is the N-terminal (first amino acid) and the right end is the C-terminal (last amino acid); the statement has them reversed. Statement II is true — adult human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits, two of alpha type and two of beta type.

q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Starch, B. Antibody, C. Concanavalin, D. Glut-4
List-II: I. Fights infection, II. Energy storage, III. Glucose transport, IV. Lectin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Starch functions in energy storage (II). Antibody fights infection (I). Concanavalin A is a lectin (IV). Glut-4 is a glucose transporter protein (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

q: A non-proteinaceous enzyme is:
e: Ribozymes are catalytic RNA molecules, making them non-proteinaceous enzymes, unlike the other options which are protein enzymes.

q: Which of the following is the least likely to be involved in stabilizing the three-dimensional folding of most proteins?
e: Ester bonds are not typically involved in protein folding; hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions are the main non-covalent forces stabilizing the 3D structure of proteins.

q: Which of the following are NOT secondary metabolites in plants?
e: Amino acids and glucose are primary metabolites (essential for basic metabolic processes), while rubber, gums, morphine, codeine, vinblastin and curcumin are secondary metabolites.

q: Identify the incorrect pair.
e: Ricin is a toxin (from castor bean), not classified as a drug, making this pairing incorrect. Codeine is an alkaloid, Abrin is a toxin, and Concanavalin A is a lectin, all correctly paired.

q: Concanavalin A is:
e: Concanavalin A is a lectin, a carbohydrate-binding protein found in jack beans.

q: Read the following statements on lipids and find out correct set of statements: (a) Lecithin found in the plasma membrane is a glycolipid (b) Saturated fatty acids possess one or more C=C bonds (c) Gingely oil has lower melting point, hence remains as oil in winter (d) Lipids are generally insoluble in water but soluble in some organic solvents (e) When fatty acid is esterified with glycerol, monoglycerides are formed. Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
e: (c) is correct: gingely (sesame) oil has a lower melting point, remaining liquid in winter. (d) is correct: lipids are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents. (e) is correct: esterification of fatty acid with glycerol can form monoglycerides (partial esterification). (a) is incorrect as lecithin is a phospholipid, not a glycolipid. (b) is incorrect as saturated fatty acids lack C=C double bonds by definition.

q: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Biological Molecules): (a) Glycogen (b) Globulin (c) Steroids (d) Thrombin. List-II (Biological functions): (i) Hormone (ii) Biocatalyst (iii) Antibody (iv) Storage product. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Glycogen is a storage polysaccharide, Globulin is an antibody (immunoglobulin), Steroids like cholesterol derivatives act as hormones, and Thrombin is an enzyme (biocatalyst) involved in blood clotting. This matches (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

q: The two functional groups characteristic of sugars are
e: Sugars (monosaccharides) are characterised by the presence of a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone) along with multiple hydroxyl groups.

q: Floridean starch has structure similar to:
e: Floridean starch, found in red algae, is structurally similar to amylopectin and glycogen, being a branched glucose polymer.

t: Glycosidic and peptide bonds in biomolecules
q: Identify the substances having glycosidic bond and peptide bond, respectively in their structure:
e: Inulin (a polysaccharide of fructose) has glycosidic bonds linking its sugar units, and insulin (a protein hormone) has peptide bonds linking its amino acids.

q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding amino acids? A. They are substituted methanes. B. Serine is an aromatic amino acid. C. Valine is a neutral amino acid. D. Lysine is an acidic amino acid.
e: Amino acids are substituted methanes (A, true — general structure based on methane). Valine is a neutral (non-polar) amino acid (C, true). Serine is not aromatic (B false); Lysine is basic, not acidic (D false). A and C only.

q: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Trypsin, B. Morphine, C. Concanavalin A, D. Collagen. List II — I. Intercellular ground substance, II. Lectin, III. Enzyme, IV. Alkaloid.
e: Trypsin is an enzyme (III); Morphine is an alkaloid (IV); Concanavalin A is a lectin (II); Collagen is intercellular ground substance/structural protein (I). A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

q: Identify the correct statements about biomolecules. A. Lipids are generally water soluble. B. Proteins are polypeptides. C. Polysaccharides are long chains of sugars. D. Adenine and guanine are substituted pyrimidines. E. Almost all enzymes are proteins.
e: B (proteins are polypeptides), C (polysaccharides are sugar chains), and E (most enzymes are proteins) are true. A is false (lipids are generally water-insoluble); D is false (adenine/guanine are purines, not pyrimidines). B, C and E only.

q: Match List I with List II: List I (Bioactive molecules) — A. Streptokinase, B. Statins, C. Lipases, D. Cyclosporin A. List II (Importance) — I. Immunosuppressive agent, II. Removal of clots from blood vessels, III. Blood cholesterol-lowering agent, IV. Detergent formulations.
e: Streptokinase removes clots from blood vessels (II); Statins lower blood cholesterol (III); Lipases used in detergent formulations (IV); Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressive agent (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

q: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Cortisol, B. Aldosterone, C. Cholecystokinin, D. Progesterone. List II — I. Stimulates the formation of alveoli in mammary glands, II. Produces anti-inflammatory reactions, III. Stimulates reabsorption of Na+ and water from renal tubule, IV. Stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice.
e: Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions (II); Aldosterone stimulates Na+/water reabsorption (III); Cholecystokinin stimulates pancreatic enzyme/bile secretion (IV); Progesterone stimulates alveoli formation in mammary glands (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.
