t: Hormone Source Organs (Match List: Progesterone, Relaxin, MSH, Catecholamines)
q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Progesterone (B) Relaxin (C) Melanocyte stimulating hormone (D) Catecholamines
List-II: (I) Pars intermedia (II) Ovary (III) Adrenal medulla (IV) Corpus luteum
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Progesterone is secreted by the corpus luteum (and placenta) - IV. Relaxin is secreted by the ovary (and placenta) - II. Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH) is secreted by the pars intermedia of the pituitary - I. Catecholamines (adrenaline + noradrenaline) are secreted by the adrenal medulla - III. So A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III. 11th NCERT, Page No. - 242, 244, 246.

q: Which of the following glucose transporters is insulin-dependent?
e: GLUT4 is the insulin-dependent glucose transporter, primarily found in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, which translocates to the cell membrane in response to insulin signaling.

q: During a prolonged stress response, the adrenal cortex secretes glucocorticoids such as cortisol. Which of the following correctly describes the combined metabolic effects of cortisol during such stress?
o: Stimulates glycogenesis in the liver, promotes protein anabolism in muscles, and suppresses gluconeogenesis
Promotes gluconeogenesis in the liver, stimulates lipolysis in adipose tissue, and causes protein catabolism in muscles
Inhibits gluconeogenesis, promotes insulin secretion from pancreas, and increases glycogen storage
Promotes glycolysis in muscles, inhibits lipolysis, and stimulates amino acid uptake by hepatocytes
e: Cortisol, a glucocorticoid secreted by the adrenal cortex (zona fasciculata), has several metabolic effects aimed at raising blood glucose during stress: (1) It stimulates gluconeogenesis in the liver, converting amino acids and glycerol into glucose. (2) It promotes protein catabolism in peripheral tissues like muscles, releasing amino acids as gluconeogenic substrates. (3) It stimulates lipolysis in adipose tissue, providing fatty acids for energy and glycerol for gluconeogenesis. It also has anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. Option A is incorrect because cortisol promotes protein catabolism, not anabolism, and stimulates rather than suppresses gluconeogenesis.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding function of adrenal medullary hormones:
A. It causes pupilary constriction
B. It is a hyperglycemic hormone
C. It causes piloerection
D. It increases strength of heart contraction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline/noradrenaline) cause pupillary dilation (not constriction), so A is false. They are hyperglycemic (increase blood glucose, B true), cause piloerection (hair standing, C true), and increase the strength and rate of heart contraction (D true). So B, C and D Only.

q: Why can't insulin be given orally to diabetic patients?
o: Human body will elicit strong immune response
It will be digested in Gastro-Intestinal (GI) tract
e: Insulin is a peptide hormone, so if given orally it would be digested by proteolytic enzymes in the alimentary canal (GI tract) before it could act, hence it must be administered by injection. 11th NCERT, Page No. - 245, 246.

t: Hypothalamic Hormones Released by Posterior Pituitary (ADH)
q: Which of the following hormones released from the pituitary is actually synthesized in the hypothalamus?
e: ADH (vasopressin) and oxytocin are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are only stored and released from the posterior pituitary. LH, FSH and ACTH are synthesized and released by the anterior pituitary itself. 11th NCERT, Page No. - 242.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Exophthalmic goiter (B) Acromegaly (C) Cushing's syndrome (D) Cretinism
List II: (I) Excess secretion of cortisol, moon face & hyperglycemia (II) Hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth. (III) Hyper secretion of thyroid hormone & protruding eye balls. (IV) Excessive secretion of growth hormone.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Exophthalmic goiter involves hyper secretion of thyroid hormone and protruding eye balls (A-III). Acromegaly results from excessive secretion of growth hormone (B-IV). Cushing's syndrome involves excess cortisol, moon face, and hyperglycemia (C-I). Cretinism involves hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

q: Match List I with List II: A. CCK, B. GIP, C. ANF, D. ADH. List II: I. Kidney, II. Heart, III. Gastric gland, IV. Pancreas. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: CCK (Cholecystokinin) acts on the pancreas (A-IV). GIP (Gastric Inhibitory Peptide) inhibits gastric gland secretion (B-III). ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor) is released from the heart (C-II). ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) acts on the kidney (D-I). So the correct match is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

q: Which of the following are NOT under the control of thyroid hormone? A. Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance. B. Regulation of basal metabolic rate. C. Normal rhythm of sleep-wake cycle. D. Development of immune system. E. Support the process of R.B.C. formation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Normal rhythm of the sleep-wake cycle (C) and development of the immune system (D) are not primarily controlled by thyroid hormone. Thyroid hormone does control water/electrolyte balance (A), basal metabolic rate (B), and supports RBC formation (E), per NCERT.

q:
Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct?
(a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone
(c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(d) It does not secrete prolactin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: The pituitary gland is anatomically divided into adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) and neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) -- (a) correct. It secretes follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) -- (b) correct. It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) from the pars intermedia -- (c) correct. It DOES secrete prolactin (from the anterior pituitary), so (d) is incorrect. Hence (a), (b) and (c) only.

t: Hormone Functions and Associated Conditions - Matching
q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Excess growth hormone, (B) Luteinizing hormone, (C) Vasopressin, (D) Oxytocin
List-II: (I) Reabsorption of water and electrolytes in kidney, (II) Contraction of uterus during child birth, (III) Acromegaly, (IV) Ovulation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Excess growth hormone causes acromegaly (III) in adults. Luteinizing hormone triggers ovulation (IV). Vasopressin (ADH) promotes reabsorption of water and electrolytes in the kidney (I). Oxytocin causes contraction of the uterus during childbirth (II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

q: Graves' disease is caused due to:
e: Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hypersecretion (hyperthyroidism) of the thyroid gland.

q: Name a peptide hormone which acts mainly on hepatocytes, adipocytes and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilization.
e: Insulin, a peptide hormone from pancreatic beta cells, acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes to enhance cellular glucose uptake and utilization, lowering blood glucose.

q: The posterior pituitary gland is not a 'true' endocrine gland because:
o: It is provided with a duct
It only stores and releases hormones
It is under the regulation of hypothalamus
e: The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) does not synthesize hormones itself; it only stores and releases hormones (oxytocin and vasopressin) that are synthesized by the hypothalamus, so it is not a 'true' endocrine gland.

q: How does steroid hormone influence the cellular activities?
o: Activating cyclic AMP located on the cell membrane
Using aquaporin channels as second messenger
Changing the permeability of the cell membrane
Binding to DNA and forming a gene-hormone complex
e: Steroid hormones, being lipophilic, pass through the cell membrane and bind to intracellular/nuclear receptors, forming a hormone-receptor complex that binds to DNA to influence gene expression.

q:
Match the following hormones with the respective disease:
(1) Insulin (2) Thyroxin (3) Corticoids (4) Growth Hormone
(i) Addison's disease (ii) Diabetes insipidus (iii) Acromegaly (iv) Goitre (v) Diabetes mellitus
Select the correct option.
e: Insulin deficiency causes Diabetes mellitus (v); Thyroxin deficiency causes Goitre (iv); Corticoid deficiency causes Addison's disease (i); Growth Hormone excess causes Acromegaly (iii).

q: Which of the following are not the effects of Parathyroid hormone? (a) Stimulates the process of bone resorption (b) Decreases Ca2+ level in blood (c) Reabsorption of Ca2+ by renal tubules (d) Decreases the absorption of Ca2+ from digested food (e) Increases metabolism of carbohydrates. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
e: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) actually increases blood calcium level (not decreases), increases calcium absorption from digested food (not decreases it), and does not primarily regulate carbohydrate metabolism, so statements (b), (d) and (e) are NOT true effects of PTH.

q: A temporary endocrine gland in the human body is:
e: The corpus luteum, formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation, is a temporary endocrine gland that secretes progesterone and degenerates if pregnancy does not occur.

q: Hypersecretion of Growth Hormone in adults does not cause further increase in height, because:
o: Bones loose their sensitivity to Growth Hormone in adults.
Muscle fibres do not grow in size after birth.
Growth Hormone becomes inactive in adults.
e: After adolescence, the epiphyseal (growth) plates of long bones fuse and close, so even excess growth hormone in adults cannot cause further increase in height (though it can cause other effects like acromegaly).

q: Which of the following is an amino acid derived hormone?
e: Epinephrine (adrenaline) is derived from the amino acid tyrosine, making it an amino acid-derived hormone, unlike the steroid hormones estriol, estradiol and ecdysone.

q: Which of the following hormones can play a significant role in osteoporosis?
e: Estrogen deficiency (common after menopause) and parathyroid hormone imbalance (which regulates calcium mobilisation from bone) are both significantly linked to the development of osteoporosis.

q: A patient presents with an enlarged thyroid gland (goitre) along with low levels of T3 and T4 in the blood. Which of the following best explains this condition?
o: Excess iodine in diet leading to suppression of TSH secretion
Deficiency of iodine causing continuous TSH stimulation of the thyroid gland
Hypersecretion of calcitonin leading to negative feedback on the anterior pituitary
Autoimmune destruction of TSH receptors on thyroid follicular cells
e: Iodine is essential for the synthesis of thyroid hormones T3 and T4. When dietary iodine is deficient, T3 and T4 levels fall. This fall removes the negative feedback on the anterior pituitary and hypothalamus, causing increased secretion of TSH. Chronically elevated TSH continuously stimulates the thyroid gland, leading to its enlargement (goitre). Thus, the condition is simple/endemic goitre due to iodine deficiency.

q: Which of the following hormones is not secreted by the anterior pituitary?
e: Oxytocin is synthesised in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary, unlike growth hormone, FSH, and ACTH, which are secreted by the anterior pituitary.

q: Mary is about to face an interview. During the five minutes before the interview, she experiences sweating, increased heart rate, and increased respiration rate. Which of the following hormones are responsible for her restlessness?
e: Adrenaline and noradrenaline, released by the adrenal medulla in response to stress, trigger the 'fight-or-flight' physiological changes described, including sweating and increased heart/respiration rate.

q: The steroid responsible for the balance of water and electrolytes in our body is
e: Aldosterone, a mineralocorticoid secreted by the adrenal cortex, regulates sodium and water reabsorption in the kidney, maintaining electrolyte and fluid balance.

q: Thymosin is responsible for
e: Thymosin, secreted by the thymus gland, plays a key role in the differentiation and maturation of T-lymphocytes, essential for cell-mediated immunity.

q: In the mechanism of action of a protein hormone, one of the second messengers is
e: Cyclic AMP (cAMP) is a widely used intracellular second messenger that mediates the effects of many protein hormones binding to plasma membrane receptors.

q: Hormones are called chemical signals that stimulate specific target tissues. Which of the following is the correct location of the receptors in the case of protein hormones?
e: Protein hormones, being large and unable to cross the lipid bilayer, bind to receptors located on the plasma membrane of target cells, unlike steroid/thyroid hormones, which have intracellular or nuclear receptors.

t: Disorders Linked to Thyroid Hormone Levels
q: Which of the following conditions is not linked to deficiency of thyroid hormones?
e: Exophthalmia (bulging of the eyes) is associated with hyperthyroidism (excess thyroid hormone, as in Graves' disease), not with thyroid hormone deficiency, unlike cretinism, goitre, and myxedema, which are all linked to hypothyroidism.

q: Once the undigested and unabsorbed substances enter the caecum, their backflow is prevented by:
e: The ileo-caecal valve, located between the ileum and caecum, prevents the backflow of undigested and unabsorbed substances from the caecum into the ileum.

q: Succus entericus is referred to as:
e: Succus entericus is the Latin term for intestinal juice, secreted by glands in the small intestine.

q: The dental formula in human beings is
e: The human dental formula is 2123/2123 per quadrant — 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars, and 3 molars in each half of the upper and lower jaw.

t: Gastric Gland Cell Types and Secretions
q: Match List I (Cells) with List II (Secretion): A. Peptic cells, B. Goblet Cells, C. Oxyntic cells, D. Hepatic cells. List II: I. Mucus, II. Bile juice, III. Proenzyme pepsinogen, IV. HCl and intrinsic factor for absorption of vitamin B12. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Peptic (chief) cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen (A-III). Goblet cells secrete mucus (B-I). Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption (C-IV). Hepatic cells secrete bile juice (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

q: Which hormones stimulate the production of pancreatic juice and bicarbonate?
e: Secretin stimulates the pancreas to release bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice, while cholecystokinin (CCK) stimulates the release of pancreatic enzymes and bile.

q: Sphincter of oddi is present at:
o: Junction of hepato-pancreatic duct and duodenum
e: The Sphincter of Oddi is located at the junction where the hepato-pancreatic duct opens into the duodenum, regulating flow of bile and pancreatic juice.

q:
Match the following structures with their respective location in organs:
(a) Crypts of Lieberkuhn (b) Glisson's Capsule (c) Islets of Langerhans (d) Brunner's Glands
(i) Pancreas (ii) Duodenum (iii) Small intestine (iv) Liver
Select the correct option from the following:
e: Crypts of Lieberkuhn are found in small intestine (iii); Glisson's Capsule covers the liver (iv); Islets of Langerhans are in the pancreas (i); Brunner's Glands are in the duodenum (ii).

q: Identify the cells whose secretion protects the lining of gastro-intestinal tract from various enzymes.
e: Goblet cells secrete mucus, which protects the lining of the gastrointestinal tract from the digestive action of various enzymes.

q: Select the correct sequence of organs in the alimentary canal of cockroach starting from mouth:
o: Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Gizzard -> Ileum -> Crop -> Colon -> Rectum
Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Ileum -> Crop -> Gizzard -> Colon -> Rectum
Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Crop -> Gizzard -> Ileum -> Colon -> Rectum
Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Gizzard -> Crop -> Ileum -> Colon -> Rectum
e: The correct sequence in cockroach alimentary canal is: Mouth -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Crop -> Gizzard -> Ileum -> Colon -> Rectum.

q: In which of the following animals, digestive tract has additional chambers like crop and gizzard?
e: Crop and gizzard are characteristic additional digestive chambers found in birds. Pavo (peacock), Psittacula (parakeet), and Corvus (crow) are all birds and possess these structures.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Fatty acids and glycerols cannot be absorbed into the blood. Statement II: Specialized lymphatic capillaries called lacteals carry chylomicrons into lymphatic vessels and ultimately into the blood. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Both statements are correct: fatty acids and glycerol (reformed into triglycerides/chylomicrons) cannot be directly absorbed into blood capillaries; instead, they enter via lacteals (specialized lymphatic capillaries) as chylomicrons, which eventually reach the blood through the lymphatic system.

q: Which of the following functions is not performed by secretions from salivary glands?
e: Saliva contains salivary amylase, which digests complex carbohydrates (starch) into simpler sugars, but it does not digest disaccharides. Saliva also lubricates the oral cavity and controls bacterial population via lysozyme.

q: A baby boy aged two years is admitted to play school and passes through a dental check-up. The dentist observed that the boy had twenty teeth. Which teeth were absent?
e: The deciduous (milk) dentition in humans has a total of 20 teeth (8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 molars), with no premolars present at all in the milk teeth set; premolars only appear with the permanent dentition.

q: Which cells of 'Crypts of Lieberkuhn' secrete antibacterial lysozyme?
e: Paneth cells, located in the crypts of Lieberkuhn of the small intestine, secrete the antibacterial enzyme lysozyme, which helps regulate the intestinal microbial environment.

q: Which of the following options best represents the enzyme composition of pancreatic juice?
e: Pancreatic juice contains lipase (for fats), amylase (for starch), trypsinogen (inactive precursor of trypsin, for proteins), and procarboxypeptidase (inactive precursor of carboxypeptidase). Pepsin and rennin are gastric enzymes, not pancreatic.

q: Which of the following terms describe human dentition?
e: Human dentition is thecodont (teeth embedded in sockets of the jawbone), diphyodont (two sets of teeth in a lifetime - milk and permanent), and heterodont (different types of teeth - incisors, canines, premolars, molars).

t: Location of cuboidal epithelium with brush border
q: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in:
e: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron is lined with cuboidal epithelium bearing a brush border of microvilli, which increases the surface area for reabsorption.

t: Anatomy of the human digestive system
q: Identify the correct statement with reference to human digestive system.
o: Serosa is the innermost layer of the alimentary canal.
Ileum is a highly coiled part.
e: The ileum, the last part of the small intestine, is a highly coiled structure; the other statements are incorrect (ileum opens into the large intestine, serosa is the outermost layer, and the vermiform appendix arises from the caecum, not duodenum).

q: Goblet cells of alimentary canal are modified from:
e: Goblet cells, which secrete mucus in the alimentary canal, are modified (specialised) columnar epithelial cells.

q: The enzyme enterokinase helps in conversion of:
e: Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, activates the inactive trypsinogen (secreted by the pancreas) into its active form, trypsin.

q: Which of the following correctly matches the enzyme with its substrate and the organ that secretes it?
e: Nuclease (specifically pancreatic nuclease) is secreted by the pancreas and acts on nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), breaking them down into nucleotides. Sucrase acts on sucrose (not maltose), gastric lipase acts on fats (not proteins) in the stomach, and salivary amylase acts on starch (not fats).

q: Which of the following is not true of intestinal villi?
o: They are supplied with capillaries and lacteal vessels.
They only participate in digestion of fats.
e: Villi primarily serve absorption of all digested nutrients (not just fats) into the blood (via capillaries) and lymph (via lacteals), and bear microvilli to increase surface area — they are not limited to fat digestion.

q: The hepatopancreatic duct opens into the duodenum and carries
e: The hepatopancreatic duct is formed by the union of the common bile duct and the pancreatic duct, so it carries both bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum.

q: Which of the following is not a common disorder associated with the digestive system?
e: Tetanus is a bacterial infection (caused by Clostridium tetani) affecting the nervous system and muscles, unrelated to digestion, unlike diarrhoea, jaundice, and dysentery, which are digestive system disorders.

t: Glands Associated with the Alimentary Canal
q: A gland not associated with the alimentary canal is the
e: The adrenal gland is an endocrine gland located near the kidney and is not part of the digestive system, unlike the pancreas, liver, and salivary glands, which are all accessory digestive glands.

q: The liver is the largest gland in the body and performs several functions. Choose the function that is not correct.
o: Secretion of a hormone called gasotrin.
e: The liver is involved in carbohydrate metabolism, bile formation (which aids fat digestion/emulsification), but it does not secrete a hormone called 'gasotrin' — gastrin is actually secreted by the stomach, not the liver, and 'gasotrin' is not a recognised hormone at all.

q: Mark the right statement among the following.
o: Trypsinogen is secreted by the intestinal mucosa.
Enterokinase is secreted by the pancreas.
e: Trypsinogen is the inactive zymogen form secreted by the pancreas, later activated into active trypsin by enterokinase, which is secreted by the intestinal mucosa (not the pancreas) — bile does not contain trypsin.

q: Who is known as the father of Ecology in India?
e: Ramdeo Misra is revered as the Father of Ecology in India.

q: Which of the following is the unit of productivity of an Ecosystem?
e: The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm⁻² yr⁻¹ or (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹ to compare the productivity of different ecosystems.

q: In the equation GPP - R = NPP, where GPP is Gross Primary Productivity and NPP is Net Primary Productivity, R here is ______.
e: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) minus respiratory losses (R) by plants. So R stands for respiratory loss.

q: Detritivores breakdown detritus into smaller particles. This process is called:
e: Fragmentation is the process by which detritivores (e.g., earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles, which is the first step of decomposition.

q: In the equation GPP-R=NPP, R represents:
e: R in this equation stands for respiration losses, with GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) minus respiration giving NPP (Net Primary Productivity).

q: A climax community is in a state of
e: A climax community represents the final, relatively stable stage of ecological succession, in a state of dynamic equilibrium with its environment, persisting until disturbed by some external change.

q:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Robert May (B) Alexander von Humboldt (C) Paul Ehrlich (D) David Tilman
List II: (I) Species-Area relationship (II) Long term ecosystem experiment using outdoor plots (III) Global species diversity at about 7 million (IV) Rivet popper hypothesis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Robert May estimated global species diversity at about 7 million (A-III). Alexander von Humboldt described the species-area relationship (B-I). Paul Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis (C-IV). David Tilman conducted long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

q: In an ecosystem the Net Primary productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is 100x (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹, what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem.
e: Using the 10% law of energy transfer across trophic levels: NPP of first trophic level (producers) = 100x. Energy reaching second trophic level = 10x. Energy reaching third trophic level (GPP, taken as equal to energy received) = x (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹.

q:
Match column-I with column-II:
Column-I: (a) Nitrococcus, (b) Rhizobium, (c) Thiobacillus, (d) Nitrobacter
Column-II: (i) Denitrification, (ii) Conversion of ammonia to nitrite, (iii) Conversion of nitrite to nitrate, (iv) Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia
Choose the correct answer from options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(2) a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
(3) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
(4) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
e: Nitrococcus = conversion of ammonia to nitrite; Rhizobium = conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia (nitrogen fixation); Thiobacillus = denitrification; Nitrobacter = conversion of nitrite to nitrate. So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

q: Match the items given in Column I (a. Eutrophication, b. Sanitary landfill, c. Snow blindness, d. Jhum cultivation) with those in Column II (i. UV-B radiation, ii. Deforestation, iii. Nutrient enrichment, iv. Waste disposal) and select the correct option given below.
e: Eutrophication is caused by nutrient enrichment (iii), sanitary landfill is a method of waste disposal (iv), snow blindness is caused by UV-B radiation (i), and Jhum cultivation (shifting cultivation) is associated with deforestation (ii). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

q: What type of ecological pyramid would be obtained with the following data? Secondary consumer: 120 g, Primary consumer: 60 g, Primary producer: 10 g
e: Since the biomass increases from the primary producer (10g) to primary consumer (60g) to secondary consumer (120g), the pyramid of biomass is inverted (narrow base, wider top), typical of aquatic ecosystems.

t: Trophic levels and examples in grassland ecosystem
q: Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem: (a) Fourth trophic level, (b) Second trophic level, (c) First trophic level, (d) Third trophic level with (i) Crow, (ii) Vulture, (iii) Rabbit, (iv) Grass
e: In the grassland food chain (Grass→Rabbit→Snake/Crow→Vulture/Hawk type), grass is the first trophic level (iv), rabbit (herbivore) is the second (iii)... per official key, fourth trophic level is vulture (ii), second trophic level is rabbit (iii), first trophic level is grass (iv), third trophic level is crow (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

q: The process of mineralisation by microorganisms helps in the release of
o: both organic and inorganic nutrients from detritus.
inorganic nutrients from detritus and the formation of humus.
e: Decomposition proceeds through fragmentation of detritus, then humification (forming humus, a dark, resistant organic matter), and finally mineralisation, in which microorganisms further break down humus to release inorganic nutrients back into the soil.

q: Productivity is the rate of production of biomass, expressed in terms of: (i) (kcal m⁻³) yr⁻¹, (ii) (g m⁻²) yr⁻¹, (iii) (g m⁻¹) yr⁻¹, (iv) (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹. Choose the correct combination.
e: Productivity is correctly expressed per unit area per unit time, either as dry matter mass (g m⁻² yr⁻¹) or as energy content (kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹) — matching (ii) and (iv). Expressions using volume (m⁻³) or linear measure (m⁻¹) are dimensionally inappropriate for productivity.

t: Determining Trophic Level from Carbon Transfer
q: If the carbon atoms fixed by producers have already passed through three (consumer) species, the trophic level of the last species would be a
e: Carbon fixed by the producer passes sequentially through the primary consumer, then the secondary consumer, and then the tertiary consumer — so after passing through three consumer species, the carbon has reached the tertiary consumer's trophic level.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy. Statement II : The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP). In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
e: Statement I is correct: solar energy is the primary source of energy in an ecosystem. Statement II is incorrect: the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is called Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), not Net Primary Productivity (NPP, which is GPP minus respiratory losses).

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Fig fruit is a non-vegetarian fruit as it has enclosed fig wasps in it.
Statement II: Fig wasp and fig tree exhibit mutual relationship as fig wasp completes its life cycle in fig fruit and fig fruit gets pollinated by fig wasp.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both statement I and Statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
e: Both statements are incorrect. Statement I is debatable/considered incorrect as fig fruit is used during religious fasting and not strictly classified as non-vegetarian in this context. Statement II is incorrect because pollination occurs in the fig inflorescence (syconium), not the fig fruit itself - the fruit develops after pollination.

t: Unidirectional Energy Flow and Second Law of Thermodynamics
q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In ecosystem, there is unidirectional flow of energy of sun from producers to consumers.
Statement II: Ecosystems are exempted from 2nd law of thermodynamics.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
e: Statement I is correct - energy flows unidirectionally from the sun to producers to consumers in an ecosystem. Statement II is incorrect - ecosystems are NOT exempt from the 2nd law of thermodynamics; they require a constant supply of energy to synthesize the molecules needed to maintain structure and function.

q: Identify the correct statements: A. Detrivores perform fragmentation. B. The humus is further degraded by some microbes during mineralization. C. Water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil and get precipitated by a process called leaching. D. The detritus food chain begins with living organisms. E. Earthworms break down detritus into smaller particles by a process called catabolism. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Statement A is correct — detritivores (like earthworms) perform fragmentation of detritus into smaller particles. Statement B is correct — humus is further degraded by microbes during mineralization, releasing inorganic nutrients. Statement C is correct — water-soluble inorganic nutrients leach down into the soil. Statement D is incorrect — the detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter, not living organisms. Statement E is incorrect — earthworms break down detritus by fragmentation, not 'catabolism' as a named process. So A, B, C only are correct.

q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(a) Energy flow from producers to consumers is unidirectional
(b) Energy pyramid can never be inverted
(c) Transfer of energy follows the 1% law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional, moving from producers to consumers (unlike nutrient cycling, which is cyclic) -- (a) is correct. Only about 1% of the solar energy incident on producers is typically captured and converted into chemical (net primary productive) energy, sometimes referred to as the 'one percent law' of energy capture efficiency by autotrophs -- (c) is correct in this sense. (Note: pyramid of energy is generally taught as always upright, but per this question's answer key, (b) is not included among the correct statements.)

q: The primary producers of the deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystem are:
e: In deep-sea hydrothermal vents (no sunlight), chemosynthetic bacteria are the primary producers, using chemical energy instead of light energy.

q: Which of the following is correctly matched?
e: Parthenium hysterophorus is a well-known invasive weed that poses a threat to biodiversity. Stratification relates to communities (not population), aerenchyma relates to hydrophytes (not Opuntia, a xerophyte), age pyramid relates to populations (not biomes).

q: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorous and calcium present in the soil at any given time, is referred as:
e: The 'standing state' refers to the amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time, as part of nutrient cycling studies in ecosystems.

q: Which of the following ecological pyramids is generally inverted?
o: Pyramid of biomass in a forest
Pyramid of biomass in a sea
e: The pyramid of biomass in a sea/pond ecosystem is generally inverted because the biomass of phytoplankton (producers) at any time is less than the biomass of zooplankton/fish (consumers) that feed on them.

q: Thiobacillus is a group of bacteria helpful in carrying out:
e: Thiobacillus denitrificans is involved in denitrification, converting nitrates back to nitrogen gas.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Decomposition is a process in which the detritus is degraded into simpler substances by microbes. Statement II: Decomposition is faster if the detritus is rich in lignin and chitin. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Statement I is correct: decomposition is the microbial breakdown of detritus into simpler substances. Statement II is incorrect: decomposition is actually slower (not faster) when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, as these are resistant to microbial breakdown.

q: Which one of the following will accelerate phosphorus cycle?
e: Phosphorus, unlike nitrogen and carbon, does not have a significant atmospheric component. Its cycle is primarily driven by weathering of phosphorus-containing rocks, which releases phosphate into the soil and water, accelerating the cycle.

q: Which ecosystem has the maximum biomass?
e: Forest ecosystems, with large, long-lived trees and dense vegetation accumulated over long periods, have the maximum standing biomass among the given ecosystem types.

q: Presence of plants arranged into well defined vertical layers depending on their height can be seen best in:
e: Tropical rain forests show the most pronounced vertical stratification (layering), with distinct emergent, canopy, understorey, shrub, and herb layers, due to their high plant diversity and dense growth competing for light.

q: All of the following are included in 'Ex-situ conservation' except
e: Sacred groves are examples of in-situ conservation (protecting species within their natural habitat), whereas wildlife safari parks, seed banks and botanical gardens are all forms of ex-situ conservation (conservation outside the natural habitat).

q: Which of the following organisms are known as chief producers in the oceans?
e: Diatoms are the chief primary producers in oceans, forming the base of the marine food chain due to their enormous abundance in phytoplankton.

t: Obligate mutualism between plants and pollinators
q: Which one of the following plants shows a very close relationship with a species of moth, where none of the two can complete its life cycle without the other?
e: Yucca plants and the Yucca moth have an obligate mutualistic relationship: the moth is the sole pollinator of Yucca flowers, and in turn lays its eggs in the ovary, with larvae feeding on some developing seeds; neither species can complete its life cycle without the other.

t: Relationship between gross and net primary productivity
q: In relation to Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity of an ecosystem, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Gross primary productivity is always less than net primary productivity.
Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity.
Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity are one and same.
There is no relationship between Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity.
e: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) = Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) - Respiratory losses (R). Since respiratory losses are always positive, GPP is always greater than NPP.

q: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for further sewage treatment?
e: Activated sludge (which includes settled bacterial flocs from the secondary treatment process) is transferred into anaerobic sludge digesters, where anaerobic bacteria further digest the organic matter, producing biogas.

q: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Decomposition, B. Detritus, C. Mineralisation, D. Humification. List II — I. Accumulation of dark coloured amorphous colloidal substance, II. Release of inorganic nutrients by the activity of microbes in soil, III. Breaking down of complex organic matter into inorganic substances, IV. Dead remains of plants and animals including fecal matter.
e: Decomposition is the breaking down of complex organic matter (III); detritus is dead remains (IV); mineralisation is release of inorganic nutrients (II); humification is accumulation of dark amorphous colloidal substance (I). A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

q: The main criteria used for Five Kingdom Classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969) included: A. Cell structure, B. Body organization, C. Presence of flagellum, D. Reproduction, E. Phylogenetic relationships.
o: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, D and E only
e: Whittaker's five-kingdom classification used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships — but not specifically 'presence of flagellum' as a primary criterion, so A, B, D and E only.

q: Ecological pyramids represent the relationship between the organisms at different trophic levels and they are generally inverted for:
o: Pyramid of energy in pond ecosystem
e: In a pond/sea ecosystem, pyramid of biomass is generally inverted since the biomass of phytoplankton (producers) is less than that of zooplankton/fish at higher trophic levels.

t: Term for nutrient amount in soil at a given time
q: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium at a given time, is referred to as:
e: The amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time is called the standing state (or standing state of nutrients).

q: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria are: (i) autotrophs, (ii) heterotrophs, (iii) saprotrophs, (iv) chemo-autotrophs. Choose the correct combination.
e: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria are heterotrophs that obtain nutrition by breaking down dead organic matter, which makes them saprotrophs — matching (ii) and (iii). They are not autotrophic or chemo-autotrophic.

q: Which of the following is NOT a producer?
e: Spirogyra, Volvox, and Nostoc are all photosynthetic (algae/cyanobacteria) and act as producers, whereas Agaricus is a mushroom-forming fungus that is a saprotrophic decomposer, not a producer.

q: Approximately how much of the solar energy falling on the leaves of a plant is converted to chemical energy by photosynthesis?
e: Only a small fraction, roughly 2 to 10 percent, of the solar radiation incident on a plant's leaves is actually captured and converted into chemical energy via photosynthesis; the rest is reflected, transmitted, or lost as heat.

t: Herbivore Consumption of Net Primary Productivity
q: How much of the net primary productivity of a terrestrial ecosystem is eaten and digested by herbivores?
e: In most terrestrial ecosystems, herbivores consume and digest only a relatively small fraction, roughly about 10%, of the net primary productivity available to them.

t: Pattern of Change During Ecological Succession
q: During the process of ecological succession, the changes that take place in communities are
o: not influenced by the physical environment.
e: Ecological succession follows a predictable, orderly, and sequential pattern of community change over time, progressing from pioneer communities toward a stable climax community, and is strongly influenced by the physical environment.

t: Reservoir of a Gaseous Biogeochemical Cycle
q: The reservoir for the gaseous type of biogeochemical cycle exists in the
e: Gaseous biogeochemical cycles (such as the carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen cycles) have their main reservoir in the atmosphere, from which the gaseous nutrients are drawn into living systems and eventually returned.

q: The thickness of ozone in a column of air in the atmosphere is measured in terms of:
e: The thickness of the ozone layer (total ozone in a column of air) is measured in Dobson units (DU).

q: The Earth summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 was called:
o: to assess threat posed to native species by invasive weed species
for immediate steps to discontinue use of CFCs that were damaging the ozone layer
to reduce CO2 emissions and global warming.
for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilization of its benefits.
e: The Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 was held for the conservation of biological diversity and sustainable utilization of its benefits, leading to the Convention on Biological Diversity.

q: Which of the following protocols did aim for reducing emission of chlorofluorocarbons into the atmosphere?
e: The Montreal Protocol (1987) specifically aimed at reducing and phasing out emissions of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) that deplete the ozone layer.

q: Which of the following pairs of gases is mainly responsible for green house effect.
e: Carbon dioxide and Methane are major greenhouse gases mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect and global warming.

q: The device which can remove particulate matter present in the exhaust from a thermal power plant is:
e: An Electrostatic Precipitator uses electrical charges to remove particulate matter (ash, dust) from the exhaust gases of thermal power plants, trapping over 99% of particulates.

q: World Ozone Day is celebrated on
e: World Ozone Day is observed on 16th September every year, commemorating the signing of the Montreal Protocol to protect the ozone layer.

q: Montreal protocol was signed in 1987 for control of:
o: Transport of Genetically modified organisms from one country to another
e: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty designed to phase out the production and use of substances responsible for ozone layer depletion.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Electrostatic precipitator is most widely used in thermal power plant. Statement II: Electrostatic precipitator in thermal power plant removes ionising radiations. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
e: Statement I is correct — electrostatic precipitators are widely used in thermal power plants to control particulate emissions. Statement II is incorrect — electrostatic precipitators remove particulate matter (ash, dust particles) from flue gases, not ionising radiations.

q: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) may not be a good index for pollution for water bodies receiving effluents from:
e: BOD measures oxygen consumed by microbial degradation of biodegradable organic matter; petroleum industry effluents contain largely non-biodegradable toxic pollutants, so BOD is not a good pollution index for them.

q: A lake which is rich in organic waste may result in:
o: Mortality of fish due to lack of oxygen
Increased population of aquatic organisms due to minerals
Drying of the lake due to algal bloom
Increased population of fish due to lots of nutrients
e: Organic waste enrichment causes eutrophication — excessive microbial decomposition depletes dissolved oxygen, leading to fish mortality.

q: The highest DDT concentration in aquatic food chain shall occur in:
e: Due to biomagnification, DDT concentration increases at each successive trophic level; the seagull, being a top predator/highest trophic level among the options, accumulates the highest concentration.

q: Which of these following methods is the most suitable for disposal of nuclear waste?
o: Dump the waste within rocks under deep ocean
Bury the waste within rocks deep below the Earth's surface
Bury the waste under antarctic ice-over
e: The most suitable and widely practiced method for disposal of nuclear waste is burying it deep within rock formations below the Earth's surface in secure geological repositories.

q: Polyblend, a fine powder of recycled modified plastic, has proved to be a good material for
e: Polyblend, a fine powder of recycled modified plastic, is mixed with bitumen for construction of roads, improving their durability.

q: The entire fleet of buses in Delhi were converted to CNG from diesel. In reference to this, which one of the following statements is false?
o: CNG burns more efficiently than diesel
The same diesel engine is used in CNG buses making the cost of conversion low
It cannot be adulterated like diesel
e: CNG buses require modified/different engines (not the same diesel engine), so this statement is false. CNG does burn more efficiently, is generally cheaper than diesel, and cannot be adulterated as easily as diesel, making these statements true.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles. Statement II: Particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Passing exhaust through electric wires to charge dust particles describes the working of an electrostatic precipitator, not a scrubber, making Statement I incorrect. Statement II is correct: fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) is effectively removed by an electrostatic precipitator rather than a scrubber.

q: Which one of the following statements is not valid for aerosols?
o: They alter rainfall and monsoon patterns
They have negative impact on agricultural land
They are harmful to human health
e: Aerosols generally have harmful effects: they alter rainfall and monsoon patterns, negatively impact agricultural land and productivity (by blocking sunlight and depositing pollutants), and are harmful to human health, so the claim of 'increased agricultural productivity' is not valid.

q: Which of the following in sewage treatment removes suspended solids?
e: Primary treatment of sewage involves physical processes (filtration and sedimentation) that remove floating debris and suspended solids like grit and sand, before the sewage moves on to secondary (biological) treatment.

q: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?
e: Ozone (O3) at ground level is a secondary pollutant, formed through photochemical reactions between primary pollutants (like NOx and hydrocarbons) in the presence of sunlight, unlike CO, SO2 and CO2 which are primary pollutants released directly.

q: In stratosphere, which of the following elements acts as a catalyst in degradation of ozone and release of molecular oxygen?
e: Chlorine atoms (released from CFCs) act as catalysts in the stratosphere, breaking down ozone molecules into molecular oxygen through a chain reaction, without being consumed themselves.

q: Snow-blindness in Antarctic region is due to:
o: Freezing of fluids in the eye by low temperature
Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
High reflection of light from snow
Damage to retina caused by infra-red rays
e: Snow blindness is caused by inflammation of the cornea (photokeratitis) due to excessive exposure to UV-B radiation, which is intensified by reflection off snow in regions with a depleted ozone layer, like Antarctica.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statements I: In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles.
Statement II: Particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Statement I is incorrect — charging dust particles with electric wires describes an electrostatic precipitator, not a scrubber. Statement II is correct — PM2.5 is removed by electrostatic precipitators, not scrubbers.

q: The flippers of the Penguins and Dolphins are the example of the:
e: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated species independently evolve similar structures due to adapting to similar environments/functions. Penguin flippers (modified wings) and Dolphin flippers (modified limbs) are structurally different in origin but functionally similar, making this an example of convergent evolution.

q: The theory of spontaneous generation stated that
o: life arose from living forms only.
life can arise from both living and non-living matter.
life can arise from non-living things only.
life arises spontaneously, neither from living nor from non-living matter.
e: The theory of spontaneous generation (abiogenesis) proposed that living organisms could arise directly from non-living matter, a view later disproved by experiments such as those of Louis Pasteur.

t: Animal Husbandry and Plant Breeding as Selection
q: Animal husbandry and plant breeding programmes are examples of
e: In animal husbandry and plant breeding, humans deliberately select and breed organisms with desirable traits, which is the defining feature of artificial selection, as opposed to natural selection driven by the environment.

t: General Trend in the Evolution of Life
q: The evolution of life shows that life forms had a trend of moving from
e: The fossil and evolutionary record shows that life originated in water and gradually colonised land over evolutionary time, i.e. a trend from water to land.

t: Geological Eras and Dominant Life Forms
q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Mesozoic Era (B) Proterozoic Era (C) Cenozoic Era (D) Paleozoic Era
List II: (I) Lower invertebrates (II) Fish & Amphibia (III) Birds & Reptiles (IV) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Mesozoic Era is associated with Birds & Reptiles (A-III). Proterozoic Era is associated with lower invertebrates (B-I). Cenozoic Era is associated with Mammals (C-IV). Paleozoic Era is associated with Fish & Amphibia (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

q: A gene locus has two alleles A, a. If the frequency of dominant allele A is 0.4, then what will be the frequency of homozygous dominant, heterozygous and homozygous recessive individuals in the population?

t: Type of Selection in Industrial Melanism
q: Industrial melanism observed in the moth Biston betularia is an example of which type of selection?
e: In polluted, soot-covered industrial areas, the frequency of the dark (melanic) form of the moth increased over time at the expense of the light form, shifting the population's phenotype progressively in one direction — the hallmark of directional (natural) selection.

q: Miller-Urey experiment showed synthesis of organic molecules from:
e: Miller and Urey (1953) simulated primitive Earth using CH4, NH3, H2 and H2O with electrical sparks (lightning), producing amino acids — proving abiotic synthesis of organic molecules.

t: Analogous Organs - Convergent Evolution (Sweet Potato & Potato)
q: Sweet potato and potato represent a certain type of evolution. Select the correct combination of terms to explain the evolution
e: Sweet potato (modified root) and potato (modified stem) perform a similar function (storage) but have different origins - this is analogy, resulting from convergent evolution. Class 11th NCERT Page No.115.

q: Which one of the following factors will not affect the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?
e: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium requires a constant gene pool with no change in allele frequencies. A constant gene pool is actually a condition for maintaining equilibrium, not a disturbing factor. Gene migration, genetic recombination, and genetic drift are all factors that can disturb the equilibrium.

q:
Given below are some stages of human evolution. Arrange them in correct sequence. (Past to Recent)
A. Homo habilis B. Homo sapiens C. Homo neanderthalensis D. Homo erectus
Choose the correct sequence of human evolution from the options given below:
e: The correct chronological sequence of human evolution from past to recent is: Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo neanderthalensis → Homo sapiens, giving the sequence A-D-C-B.

q: Select the correct group/set of Australian Marsupials exhibiting adaptive radiation.
o: Mole, Flying squirrel, Tasmanian tiger cat
e: Numbat, Spotted cuscus, and Flying phalanger are all Australian marsupials that are classic examples of adaptive radiation, having diversified from a common ancestral marsupial stock to occupy different ecological niches.

q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Forelimbs of human and bats are homologous.
Reason R: Forelimbs of humans and bats have similar anatomical structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
e: The forelimbs of humans and bats are homologous organs -- they evolved from a common ancestral structure but are adapted to perform different functions (grasping vs. flying) -- Assertion A is correct. Homology is defined by similar anatomical (structural) origin despite different functions, so forelimbs having similar underlying anatomical structure (bone arrangement) is indeed the basis for them being called homologous -- Reason R is correct and correctly explains A.

q: A population of diploid organisms is at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. If the frequency of allele A is 0.1, the frequency of AA is ____________.
e: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, genotype frequencies follow p² + 2pq + q² = 1, where p is the frequency of allele A. Frequency of AA genotype = p² = (0.1)² = 0.01.

q: Adaptive radiation in placental mammals and Australian Marsupials leading to similarity between distant species is an example of
e: When unrelated species (placental mammals and Australian marsupials) independently evolve similar body forms/adaptations due to similar environmental pressures (analogous structures, not from a common recent ancestor), it is called convergent evolution.

q:
Natural selection can lead to__________.
(a) stabilisation (b) genetic drift (c) directional change (d) disruption
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Natural selection can produce three types of outcomes: stabilising selection (a), directional selection/change (c), and disruptive selection (d). Genetic drift (b) is a separate, random evolutionary mechanism independent of natural selection (it involves random changes in allele frequencies, especially in small populations), not a result of natural selection itself.

q: Which of the following is not evidence for evolution?
o: Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
e: Ernst Haeckel's embryological recapitulation theory ('ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny', i.e., that embryonic development of an organism repeats its evolutionary history) has been scientifically discredited/discounted and is not considered valid evidence for evolution. Fossil records, divergent evolution of homologous structures (like forelimbs), and convergent evolution of analogous structures (like wings) are all valid, accepted lines of evidence for evolution.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Modern Homo sapiens arose in Australia and moved across continents.
Statement II: Homo sapiens arose around 75000 to 10000 years ago.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
e: Modern Homo sapiens arose in AFRICA (not Australia) and then spread/moved across other continents (the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis) -- Statement I is incorrect. As per the standard NCERT account, Homo sapiens arose approximately 75,000 to 10,000 years ago -- Statement II is correct as per this textbook figure.

q: Genetic drift operates in:
e: Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies that has a pronounced effect in small, isolated populations, where chance events can significantly alter gene pool composition.

q: In Hardy-Weinberg equation, the frequency of heterozygous individual is represented by:
e: In the Hardy-Weinberg equation p² + 2pq + q² = 1, the term 2pq represents the frequency of heterozygous individuals.

q: The chronological order of human evolution from early to the recent is:
o: Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Ramapithecus → Homo erectus
Australopithecus → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus
Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus
Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Australopithecus → Homo erectus
e: The chronological order of human evolution is: Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus (followed by Homo sapiens).

q:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of events in the origin of life?
I. Formation of protobionts
II. Synthesis of organic monomers
III. Synthesis of organic polymers
IV. Formation of DNA-based genetic systems
e: The correct sequence in the origin of life (chemical evolution) is: synthesis of organic monomers → synthesis of organic polymers → formation of protobionts → formation of DNA-based genetic systems, i.e., II, III, I, IV.

q: The factor that leads to Founder effect in a population is:
e: The Founder effect occurs when a small group (founders) colonizes a new habitat, carrying only a fraction of the genetic variation of the original population — this is a form of genetic drift.

q:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I: (a) Adaptive radiation (b) Convergent evolution (c) Divergent evolution (d) Evolution by anthropogenic action
List - II: (i) Selection of resistant varieties due to excessive use of herbicides and pesticides (ii) Bones of forelimbs in Man and Whale (iii) Wings of Butterfly and Bird (iv) Darwin Finches
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Adaptive radiation is exemplified by Darwin's Finches; Convergent evolution by wings of Butterfly and Bird (similar function, different origin); Divergent evolution by bones of forelimbs in Man and Whale (homologous structures); Evolution by anthropogenic action by selection of resistant varieties due to excessive herbicide/pesticide use.

q:
Match the hominids with their correct brain size.
(a) Homo habilis (b) Homo neanderthalensis (c) Homo erectus (d) Homo sapiens
(i) 900cc (ii) 1350cc (iii) 650-800 cc (iv) 1400 cc
Select the correct option.
e: Homo habilis had a brain capacity of about 650-800 cc (iii); Homo erectus about 900 cc (i); Homo neanderthalensis about 1350 cc (ii); Homo sapiens about 1400 cc (iv).

q: Variations caused by mutation, as proposed by Hugo de Vries, are:
e: According to Hugo de Vries' mutation theory, variations caused by mutations are random (occur by chance) and directionless (not oriented towards any particular goal).

q: In a species the weight of newborn ranges from 2 to 5 kg. 97% of the newborn with weight from 2 to 2.5 kg or 4.5 to 5 kg die. Which type of selection process is taking place?
e: Stabilizing selection favors the intermediate/average phenotype (middle weight range) while selecting against the extreme phenotypes (very low and very high weight), as described in this scenario.

q: Natural selection where more individuals acquire specific character value other than the mean character value, leads to
e: When natural selection favours individuals with a character value shifted away from the population mean (towards one extreme), it results in directional selection/change.

q: Which of the following represents order of 'Horse'?
e: In the taxonomic hierarchy of the horse (Equus caballus), Perissodactyla is the order (odd-toed ungulates), while Equidae is the family, Equus is the genus, and caballus/ferus are species epithets.

q: Artificial selection to obtain cows yielding higher milk output represents:
o: directional as it pushes the mean of the character in one direction.
disruptive as it splits the population into two, one yielding higher output and the other lower output.
stabilizing followed by disruptive as it stabilizes the population to produce higher yielding cows.
stabilizing selection as it stabilizes this character in the population.
e: Selecting cows for higher milk output consistently pushes the population mean towards higher yield over generations, which is the defining feature of directional selection.

t: Theories of evolution (de Vries' mutation theory)
q: According to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is
e: Hugo de Vries proposed the mutation theory of evolution, suggesting that evolution occurs through sudden, large, discontinuous variations called saltations, rather than gradual small changes.

q: Among the following sets of examples for divergent evolution, select the incorrect option.
o: Forelimbs of man, bat and cheetah
Eye of octopus, bat and man
Brain of bat, man and cheetah
Heart of bat, man and cheetah
e: The eye of the octopus (cephalopod mollusc) evolved independently from the eyes of bats and humans (vertebrates) through convergent evolution (analogous structures), not divergent evolution from a common ancestral structure, making this pairing incorrect for divergent evolution.

q: The similarity in bone structure of the forelimbs of many vertebrates is an example of
e: Similar bone structure arising from a common ancestor but modified for different functions (as in vertebrate forelimbs) is the classic example of homology.

q: Which of the following refer to correct example(s) of organisms which have evolved due to changes in environment brought about by anthropogenic action? (a) Darwin's Finches of Galapagos islands. (b) Herbicide resistant weeds. (c) Drug resistant eukaryotes. (d) Man-created breeds of domesticated animals like dogs.
e: Herbicide-resistant weeds, drug-resistant eukaryotes (pathogens) and man-created dog breeds have all evolved due to human (anthropogenic) activity; Darwin's finches evolved through natural environmental pressures, not direct anthropogenic action.

q: Embryological support for evolution was disapproved by:
e: Karl Ernst von Baer disputed and criticised Ernst Haeckel's recapitulation theory (that embryological development mirrors evolutionary history), opposing this embryological support for evolution.

t: Example that is not convergent evolution
q: Which of the following is not an example of convergent evolution?
o: Fore limbs of whales and bats
e: Forelimbs of whales and bats are homologous structures (common ancestry, divergent evolution), not an example of convergent evolution.

t: Matching evolutionary chronology of life forms
q: Match List I with List II with respect to chronology of evolution of life forms: List I — A. About 65 mya, B. About 500 mya, C. About 350 mya, D. About 320 mya. List II — I. Jawless fish probably evolved, II. The dinosaurs suddenly disappeared from the earth, III. Seaweeds and few plants probably existed, IV. Invertebrates were formed and became active.
e: About 65 mya dinosaurs disappeared (II); about 500 mya jawless fish evolved (I); about 350 mya seaweeds/plants existed (III); about 320 mya invertebrates became active (IV). A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

t: Sequence of evolution of human/brain and language parallel species
q: Evolution of human appears parallel to the progressive development of brain and language skills. As such, the evolution of individual species in the sequence of their appearance is:
o: Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
Neanderthal → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens
Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Ramapithecus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
Homo sapiens → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Neanderthal → Homo erectus
e: Correct evolutionary sequence: Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens.

q: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Adaptive radiation, (b) Convergent evolution, (c) Divergent evolution, (d) Evolution by anthropogenic action with (i) Selection of resistant varieties due to excessive use of herbicides and pesticides, (ii) Bones of forelimbs in Man and Whale, (iii) Wings of Butterfly and Bird, (iv) Darwin Finches.
e: Adaptive radiation is exemplified by Darwin's finches (iv); Convergent evolution by wings of butterfly and bird (iii); Divergent evolution by bones of forelimbs in man and whale (ii); Evolution by anthropogenic action by selection of resistant varieties (i). (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

q: Which of the following statements is not true?
o: Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
Sweet potato and potato is an example of analogy
Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
e: Flippers of penguins (modified wings) and dolphins (modified forelimbs) are analogous structures (similar function, different origin, convergent evolution), not homologous. Statement (4) is false/not true.

q: The equation (p+q)² = p² + 2pq + q² = 1 is used in
e: This is the Hardy-Weinberg equation, used in population genetics to describe allele and genotype frequencies in a population that is in genetic equilibrium (not undergoing evolutionary change).

q: The appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of
e: Antibiotic resistance is not induced by the antibiotic itself; rather, resistant variants already exist at low frequency within the bacterial population due to pre-existing genetic variation, and the antibiotic simply selects for and increases the proportion of these resistant individuals.

t: Why Viviparity is Considered More Evolved
q: Viviparity is considered to be more evolved because
o: the young ones are left on their own after birth.
the young ones are protected by a thick shell.
the young ones are protected inside the mother's body and are looked after once born, leading to a greater chance of survival.
the embryo takes a long time to develop.
e: In viviparous organisms, the developing young are protected and nourished inside the mother's body and are typically cared for after birth too, which significantly increases their chances of survival compared to oviparous (egg-laying) strategies.

t: Nature of Mutational and Recombinational Variation
q: Variations arising during mutations and meiotic recombinations are
e: Mutations and recombinations introduce variation randomly, with no inherent direction or bias toward being advantageous; it is natural selection acting afterward on this random variation that produces directional change in a population.

q: In which disease does mosquito transmitted pathogen cause chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels?
e: Elephantiasis (filariasis) is caused by filarial worms transmitted by mosquitoes, which cause chronic inflammation and blockage of lymph vessels, leading to gross enlargement of affected body parts.

q: The JGA (Juxta Glomerular Apparatus) is a special sensitive region formed by cellular modifications in ___________ related to the same nephron.
o: Proximal convoluted tubule and efferent renal arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and efferent renal arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and afferent renal arteriole
Proximal convoluted tubule and afferent renal arteriole
e: JGA is formed by cellular modifications of the distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole of the same nephron.

q: Animals that excrete ammonia as the primary nitrogenous waste are called:
e: Ammonotelic animals excrete ammonia as the primary nitrogenous waste. This mode of excretion is common in aquatic animals like bony fishes and aquatic amphibians, as water helps dilute and expel the toxic ammonia.

q: Which part of the nephron is NOT present in juxtaglomerular nephrons but is present in cortical nephrons?
o: Loop of Henle with long descending limb
e: Juxtaglomerular nephrons have a very long loop of Henle that extends deep into the medulla, whereas cortical nephrons have a short loop of Henle. All nephrons possess PCT, Bowman's capsule, and DCT.

q: Which of the following is removed from our body by the lungs?
e: The lungs eliminate both carbon dioxide and water vapour during exhalation, in addition to their primary role in gas exchange.

q: The pH of human urine is approximately
e: Human urine is typically slightly acidic, with a pH of approximately 6.5.

q: The condition of accumulation of urea in the blood is termed
e: Uremia refers to the abnormal accumulation of urea in the blood, usually due to impaired kidney function.

q: Which one of the following is also known as antidiuretic hormone (ADH)?
e: Vasopressin is also known as antidiuretic hormone (ADH); it promotes water reabsorption in the kidneys, reducing urine output.

q: Animals that excrete nitrogenous waste primarily as uric acid are called:
e: Uricotelic animals excrete uric acid as the main nitrogenous waste. Examples include reptiles, birds, and insects. Ammonotelic animals excrete ammonia, and ureotelic animals excrete urea.

q: The process of glomerular filtration produces a filtrate that is similar to plasma but lacks:
e: Glomerular filtrate is essentially blood plasma without large proteins. Proteins like albumin are too large to pass through the glomerular filtration membrane. Glucose, amino acids, urea, and inorganic salts are all present in the filtrate.

q: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs found in:
e: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects and other arthropods like cockroaches. They absorb nitrogenous wastes from the haemolymph and convert them to uric acid. Earthworms use nephridia, Planaria uses flame cells, and Pila uses kidneys.

q: Animals that excrete ammonia as their primary nitrogenous waste are called:
e: Ammonotelic animals (e.g., most aquatic invertebrates, bony fishes) excrete ammonia as the primary nitrogenous waste. Ammonia is highly toxic and highly soluble, so it requires large amounts of water for excretion. Ureotelic animals excrete urea, and uricotelic animals excrete uric acid.

q: Which of the following diagrams is correct with regard to the proximal (P) and distal (D) tubule of the Nephron?
o: PCT: HCO3−,NaCl reabsorbed, H2O reabsorbed, H+ secreted; DCT: NaCl,H2O reabsorbed, HCO3− reabsorbed, K+,H+ secreted — but PCT shown without NH3
PCT: HCO3−,NaCl,H2O reabsorbed, H+,NH3 secreted; DCT: NaCl,H2O reabsorbed, HCO3− reabsorbed, K+,H+ secreted
PCT: HCO3−,NaCl,H2O reabsorbed, H+,NH3 secreted; DCT: H2O reabsorbed, HCO3− reabsorbed, NaCl,H+ secreted
PCT: NaCl,HCO3− reabsorbed, H+,H2O secreted; DCT: NaCl,NH3 reabsorbed, K+,H2O secreted
e: PCT reabsorbs HCO3−, NaCl, H2O and nutrients, while secreting H+ and NH3 to maintain pH balance. DCT reabsorbs NaCl, H2O conditionally and HCO3−, while secreting K+ and H+ to maintain sodium-potassium and pH balance. This matches option (2).

q: In humans, the liver plays a role in excretion by converting which toxic substance into a less harmful form that is eventually excreted?
o: Ammonia into urea via the ornithine cycle
Biliverdin into bilirubin for excretion via urine
e: The liver is a vital excretory organ. It converts toxic ammonia (produced from amino acid catabolism) into urea through the ornithine cycle (urea cycle). This urea is then transported to the kidneys and excreted in urine.

q: The stretch receptors in the urinary bladder wall send signals to the micturition centre located in which part of the nervous system?
e: When the urinary bladder fills (about 300-400 mL), stretch receptors on the bladder wall send signals to the micturition centre in the spinal cord. This initiates a reflex causing the urethral sphincter to relax and the bladder to contract. The cerebral cortex provides voluntary control over this reflex.

q: Which of the following substances is actively secreted into the tubular filtrate during tubular secretion and helps in maintaining ionic balance?
e: Tubular secretion involves the active transport of substances from the peritubular blood into the tubular filtrate. Potassium ions (K⁺), hydrogen ions (H⁺), and ammonia are secreted into the filtrate in the DCT and collecting duct to maintain ionic and acid-base balance. Glucose is normally completely reabsorbed, not secreted.

q: Malpighian tubules, the excretory organs of insects, open into which part of the alimentary canal?
o: Hindgut at the junction of midgut and hindgut
e: Malpighian tubules are excretory structures found in insects. They arise from the junction of the midgut and hindgut (ileum region) and open into the alimentary canal at this junction. They absorb nitrogenous wastes and ions from haemolymph and transfer them into the intestine for excretion.

q: We can produce concentrated or dilute urine. This is facilitated by a special mechanism. Identify the mechanism.
o: Counter-current mechanism in the loop of Henle/vasa recta
e: The counter-current mechanism operating in the loop of Henle and the vasa recta maintains an osmotic gradient in the medulla, which allows the kidney to produce urine of varying concentration depending on the body's water needs.

q: In the countercurrent mechanism of urine concentration, which segment of the nephron is impermeable to water but actively transports NaCl into the interstitium?
o: Descending limb of loop of Henle
Ascending limb of loop of Henle
e: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water but actively transports NaCl out into the medullary interstitium. This creates a hyperosmotic environment in the medulla. The descending limb is permeable to water but not to solutes.

q: Approximately what fraction of the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT)?
e: The PCT reabsorbs approximately 70–80% of the glomerular filtrate. This includes almost all glucose, amino acids, a large portion of water, Na⁺, K⁺, and other essential substances. The PCT is the primary site of reabsorption in the nephron.

q: In the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), aldosterone acts primarily to:
o: Increase glomerular filtration rate by dilating afferent arterioles
Promote Na⁺ reabsorption and K⁺ secretion in the distal tubule
Increase water permeability of the collecting duct directly
Stimulate renin secretion from juxtaglomerular cells
e: Aldosterone, secreted by the adrenal cortex in response to angiotensin II, acts on the DCT and collecting duct to promote Na⁺ reabsorption and K⁺ secretion. This increases blood volume and pressure. ADH (not aldosterone) increases water permeability of the collecting duct.

q: In a patient with severe glomerulonephritis, which combination of clinical findings would most likely be observed?
o: Polyuria, low blood pressure, high urine specific gravity, and hyperkalemia
Haematuria, proteinuria, decreased GFR, and hypertension
Glycosuria, aminoaciduria, normal GFR, and low plasma creatinine
Oliguria, alkalosis, decreased plasma urea, and low blood pressure
e: Glomerulonephritis involves inflammation of the glomeruli, which damages the filtration membrane. This leads to: haematuria (RBCs in urine) and proteinuria (proteins leak through damaged membrane), decreased GFR (inflamed capillaries filter less), and hypertension (reduced filtration causes fluid retention). Glycosuria and aminoaciduria are features of tubular disorders, not glomerular disease.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the nephron, the descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water and permeable to electrolytes.
Statement II: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple columnar brush border epithelium and increases the surface area for reabsorption.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
e: The descending limb of loop of Henle is actually permeable to water and impermeable to electrolytes (the reverse of what Statement I says, so it is false). While the PCT is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium (not columnar), making Statement II also false. So both statements are false.

q: Choose the correct statement given below regarding juxta medullary nephron.
o: Loop of Henle of juxta medullary nephron runs deep into medulla.
Juxta medullary nephrons outnumber the cortical nephrons.
Juxta medullary nephrons are located in the columns of Bertini.
Renal corpuscle of juxta medullary nephron lies in the outer portion of the renal medulla
e: Juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops of Henle that run deep into the medulla, important for producing concentrated urine. They are far fewer in number than cortical nephrons (about 15%), and their renal corpuscles lie in the cortex close to the medulla, not within the medulla or columns of Bertini.
