e: Halophytes, such as mangrove plants growing in saline swampy habitats, produce special breathing roots called pneumatophores and exhibit vivipary (seed germination while still attached to the parent plant).

q: Pneumatophores occur in
e: Pneumatophores are specialised negatively geotropic roots that grow upward out of the soil/water to obtain oxygen, found in halophytic plants (mangroves) growing in saline, waterlogged soil.

q: Sweet potato is a modified
e: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a modification of the adventitious root, which becomes swollen and tuberous to store food.

t: Adventitious roots arising from stem base
q: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are:
e: Fibrous roots are adventitious roots that arise in clusters from the base of the stem, replacing the primary root system, typically seen in monocots like grasses.

q: In racemose inflorescence, ___________.
o: flowers are borne in an acropetal succession
the main axis terminates in a flower
e: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow (unlimited growth) and flowers are borne in acropetal succession (youngest near the apex).

q: Which of the following floral formula is the correct floral formula of Solanaceae family?
e: Solanaceae floral formula: actinomorphic, bisexual, K(5) C(5) A5 G(2) with gamosepalous calyx and gamopetalous corolla — matching option 3.

q: Match Column-I with Column-II (floral formulae) with (i) Brassicaceae, (ii) Liliaceae, (iii) Fabaceae, (iv) Solanaceae.
e: Matching each floral formula to its characteristic family pattern gives (a)-(iii) Fabaceae, (b)-(iv) Solanaceae, (c)-(ii) Liliaceae, (d)-(i) Brassicaceae.

q: Rearrange the following zones as seen in the root in vertical section, from the tip towards the base, and choose the correct option: A. Root hair zone, B. Zone of meristems, C. Root cap zone, D. Zone of maturation, E. Zone of elongation.
e: From the root tip inward, the order is: root cap zone (C, protective tip) → zone of meristems (B, actively dividing cells) → zone of elongation (E, cells elongate) → root hair zone (A, absorption) → zone of maturation (D, differentiated tissue).

q: In an inflorescence where flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession, the position of the youngest floral bud on the floral axis shall be
e: In acropetal succession, older flowers are borne towards the base (proximal end) and younger flowers develop progressively towards the growing tip (distal end), so the youngest bud is positioned distally.

q: The mature seeds of plants such as gram and pea possess no endosperm, because
o: there is no double fertilisation in them.
endosperm is not formed in them.
endosperm gets used up by the developing embryo during seed development.
e: In non-endospermic (exalbuminous) seeds like gram and pea, endosperm does form after double fertilisation but is completely consumed by the growing embryo during seed development, leaving none in the mature seed.

q: Endosperm, a product of double fertilisation in angiosperms, is absent in the seeds of
e: Orchid seeds are notably minute and non-endospermic, lacking any stored endosperm, unlike coconut, maize, and castor, which are all well-known endospermic (albuminous) seeds.

q: The placenta is attached to the developing seed near the
e: The hilum is the scar/region on the seed coat marking the point of attachment of the seed to the fruit wall (placenta) via the stalk (funicle).

t: Meninges of the Central Nervous System
q: Which of the following is not a part of human central neural system?
e: Dura mater, pia mater, and arachnoid are the three meninges (protective membranes) covering the brain and spinal cord (CNS). Pericardium is the membrane surrounding the heart, not part of the central nervous system.

q: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are__________.
e: Frogs have 10 pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain, unlike mammals (including humans) which have 12 pairs.

q: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system by the release of______.
e: Muscle contraction is initiated when a motor neuron releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, which generates an action potential in the muscle fiber.

q: Which part of the brain is responsible for thermoregulation?
e: The hypothalamus is responsible for thermoregulation (body temperature control) among its many homeostatic functions.

q: The specific receptors for neurotransmitters in a synapse are present in ___________.
e: Neurotransmitter receptors are present on the post-synaptic membrane.

q: Which part of a neuron is responsible for receiving signals from other neurons?
e: Dendrites are the branched projections of a neuron that receive signals (impulses) from other neurons and transmit them toward the cell body (cyton). Axon terminals transmit signals away from the neuron to the next cell.

q: In a simple reflex arc, which of the following is the correct order of components involved?
o: Receptor → Efferent neuron → Spinal cord → Afferent neuron → Effector
Receptor → Afferent neuron → Nerve centre → Efferent neuron → Effector
Effector → Afferent neuron → Brain → Efferent neuron → Receptor
Receptor → Interneuron → Afferent neuron → Spinal cord → Effector
e: A reflex arc follows the path: Receptor (detects stimulus) → Afferent (sensory) neuron → Nerve centre (spinal cord/brain) → Efferent (motor) neuron → Effector (muscle/gland). This pathway allows rapid, involuntary responses without conscious brain involvement.

q: Chemicals which are released at the synaptic junction are called
e: Neurotransmitters are the chemical messengers released at synaptic junctions to transmit nerve impulses from one neuron to the next.

q: Mark the vitamin present in rhodopsin.
e: Rhodopsin, the visual pigment in rod cells, is composed of retinal (a derivative of vitamin A) bound to the protein opsin.

q: The wax-secreting gland present in the ear canal is called the
e: Ceruminous glands, located in the external auditory canal, secrete earwax (cerumen).

q: The part of the internal ear responsible for hearing is the
e: The cochlea, a coiled structure in the inner ear, houses the organ of Corti and is responsible for converting sound vibrations into nerve impulses for hearing, while the semicircular canals, utriculus, and sacculus are involved in balance and equilibrium.

q: Good vision depends on adequate intake of carotene-rich food. Select the best option from the following statements: (a) Vitamin A derivatives are formed from carotene. (b) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment. (c) Retinal is a derivative of Vitamin A. (d) Retinal is a light absorbing part of all the visual photopigments.
e: Statements (a), (c), and (d) are correct: Vitamin A derivatives form from carotene, retinal is a Vitamin A derivative, and retinal is the light-absorbing component of all visual photopigments. Statement (b) is incorrect because photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the outer segment, not the inner segment, of photoreceptor cells.

t: Generation and Conduction of Nerve Impulse
q: During repolarization of an action potential, which of the following correctly describes the ionic events?
o: Na⁺ channels open rapidly, allowing Na⁺ to rush inside the cell
K⁺ channels close and Na⁺ channels remain open, restoring the negative charge
Voltage-gated K⁺ channels open, K⁺ flows out of the cell, restoring the negative resting potential
Cl⁻ ions rush into the cell through newly opened channels, making the inside negative again
e: Repolarization occurs when voltage-gated K⁺ channels open (with a slight delay after Na⁺ channels inactivate). K⁺ ions flow out of the cell along their concentration gradient, restoring the negative charge inside the membrane. Na⁺ channels are inactivated at this stage. This brings the membrane potential back toward the resting level.

q: Which of the following statements about phototransduction in the human eye is CORRECT?
o: Rhodopsin in cone cells is responsible for colour vision and is most sensitive in bright light
In the dark, rod cells are depolarized and release neurotransmitters continuously; light causes hyperpolarization reducing neurotransmitter release
Photoreceptor cells directly send action potentials to the optic nerve without any intermediate neurons
Iodopsin is the photopigment found in rod cells and is responsible for dim-light vision
e: In darkness, rod cells are in a depolarized state (due to open cGMP-gated Na⁺ channels) and continuously release neurotransmitters. When light strikes rhodopsin, it triggers a cascade that reduces cGMP levels, closes Na⁺ channels, hyperpolarizing the rod cell and reducing neurotransmitter release — this signals the brain. Rhodopsin is in rods (not cones); iodopsin is in cones. Photoreceptors synapse onto bipolar and ganglion cells before the optic nerve.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Pons (B) Hypothalamus (C) Medulla (D) Cerebellum
List II: (I) Provides additional space for Neurons. Regulates posture and balance. (II) Controls respiration and gastric secretions. (III) Connects different regions of brain. (IV) Neuro secretory cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Pons connects different regions of the brain (A-III). Hypothalamus contains neurosecretory cells that secrete hormones (B-IV). Medulla controls respiration and gastric secretions (C-II). Cerebellum provides additional space for neurons and regulates posture and balance (D-I). So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I is correct.

t: Brain Structure - Cerebrum and Brain Stem
q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The cerebral hemispheres are connected by nerve tract known as corpus callosum.
Statement II: The brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons and cerebrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
e: Statement I is correct — the cerebral hemispheres are connected by the corpus callosum. Statement II is incorrect because the brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons, and midbrain (not cerebrum, which is a separate major brain region).

q: Match List I with List II with respect to human eye: A. Fovea, B. Iris, C. Blind spot, D. Sclera. List II: I. Visible coloured portion of eye that regulates diameter of pupil, II. External layer of eye formed of dense connective tissue, III. Point of greatest visual acuity or resolution, IV. Point where optic nerve leaves the eyeball and photoreceptor cells are absent. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Fovea is the point of greatest visual acuity (A-III). Iris is the visible coloured portion of the eye that regulates pupil diameter (B-I). Blind spot is where the optic nerve leaves the eyeball and photoreceptors are absent (C-IV). Sclera is the external layer formed of dense connective tissue (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

q: The parts of human brain that help in regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of excitement, pleasure, rage, fear etc. are:
e: The limbic system, along with the hypothalamus, regulates sexual behaviour and emotional expressions such as excitement, pleasure, rage, and fear.

q: Select the incorrect statement regarding synapses:
o: The membranes of presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons are in close proximity in an electrical synapse.
Electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across the electrical synapse.
Impulse transmission across a chemical synapse is always faster than that across an electrical synapse.
e: Electrical synapses transmit impulses faster than chemical synapses because they allow direct current flow without the delay caused by neurotransmitter release and diffusion, making statement (4) incorrect.

q: Receptor sites for neurotransmitters are present in:
e: Receptor sites for neurotransmitters are located on the post-synaptic membrane, where released neurotransmitters bind to trigger a new electrical impulse in the next neuron.

q: Myelin sheath is produced by:
e: The myelin sheath around nerve fibres is produced by Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system and by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system.

t: Structure and function of the brain
q: Which of the following structures or regions is incorrectly paired with its function?
o: Medulla oblongata : controls respiration and cardiovascular reflexes.
Corpus callosum : band of fibers connecting left and right cerebral hemispheres.
Hypothalamus : production of releasing hormones and regulation of temperature, hunger and thirst.
Limbic system : consists of fibre tracts that interconnect different regions of brain; controls movement.
e: The limbic system is primarily involved in emotional responses and motivation (not voluntary movement control), so pairing it with 'controls movement' is incorrect; the cerebellum and motor cortex are responsible for movement coordination.

q: The transparent lens in the human eye is held in its place by
o: ligaments attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the iris
e: The lens is held in position by suspensory ligaments (zonules) attached to the ciliary body, which adjust the shape of the lens during accommodation via the ciliary muscles.

t: Composition of Nissl bodies in neurons
q: Nissl bodies are mainly composed of
e: Nissl bodies (Nissl granules), found in the cell body of neurons, are composed of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) along with free ribosomes, giving them their granular, basophilic appearance.

q: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Organ of Corti, (b) Cochlea, (c) Eustachian tube, (d) Stapes with (i) Connects middle ear and pharynx, (ii) Coiled part of the labyrinth, (iii) Attached to the oval window, (iv) Located on the basilar membrane.
e: Organ of Corti is located on the basilar membrane (iv), Cochlea is the coiled part of the labyrinth (ii), Eustachian tube connects the middle ear and pharynx (i), and Stapes is attached to the oval window (iii). This matches a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.

q: The resting membrane potential of a typical mammalian neuron is approximately:
e: At rest, the inner surface of the neuronal membrane is negatively charged relative to the outer surface, creating a resting membrane potential of approximately -70 mV. This is maintained by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump and selective permeability of the membrane.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of events at a chemical synapse?
o: Action potential → neurotransmitter release from postsynaptic membrane → receptor binding on presynaptic membrane
Action potential → Ca²⁺ influx into presynaptic terminal → vesicle fusion → neurotransmitter release into synaptic cleft → receptor binding on postsynaptic membrane
Action potential → K⁺ influx into presynaptic terminal → neurotransmitter release → receptor binding on postsynaptic membrane
Action potential → direct electrical coupling between pre- and postsynaptic membranes → ion flow
e: At a chemical synapse, the arriving action potential triggers Ca²⁺ influx into the presynaptic terminal. This causes synaptic vesicles to fuse with the presynaptic membrane and release neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These neurotransmitters then bind to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, generating a new potential. Option D describes electrical synapses.

q: Which region of the human brain is primarily responsible for maintaining posture, equilibrium, and coordinating voluntary movements?
e: The cerebellum, located at the back of the brain, is responsible for coordinating voluntary muscle movements, maintaining posture, and ensuring balance and equilibrium. The cerebrum handles higher functions; hypothalamus regulates homeostasis; medulla oblongata controls autonomic functions like heart rate and breathing.

q: The potential difference across the resting membrane is negative. This is due to the differential distribution of the following ions.
e: The resting membrane potential arises from the unequal distribution of Na+ (more outside) and K+ (more inside) ions across the neuronal membrane, maintained by the Na+/K+ pump.

q: The resting membrane potential is maintained by
e: The Na+/K+ ion pump actively transports ions across the neuronal membrane, maintaining the characteristic resting membrane potential.

q: The function of our visceral organs is controlled by
o: the sympathetic and somatic neural system.
the sympathetic and parasympathetic neural system.
the central and somatic nervous system.
e: Visceral organs are regulated by the autonomic nervous system, comprising the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions, which often have opposing effects.

q: Which of the following is not involved in the knee-jerk reflex?
e: The knee-jerk reflex is a simple spinal reflex that bypasses the brain entirely, being processed through the spinal cord via a quick reflex arc involving the muscle spindle, sensory and motor neurons, and interneurons.

q: Epiphytes that are growing on a mango branch is an example of which of the following?
e: Commensalism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch is a classic example of commensalism.

t: Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth - Meaning of K (Carrying Capacity)
q: The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is dN/dt = rN[(K-N)/K]. From this equation, K indicates:
e: In the logistic growth equation, K represents the carrying capacity - the maximum population size that a particular habitat can support. 12th NCERT Page No. 196.

q: Which of the following are primary consumers in a food chain?
e: Primary consumers are organisms that feed directly on producers (plants), i.e., herbivores.

q: If '8' Drosophila in laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is ___________ individuals per Drosophila per week.
e: Death rate = number of deaths/original population = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 83)

q: The principle of competitive exclusion was stated by:
e: G.F. Gause stated the competitive exclusion principle: two species competing for the same limiting resource cannot co-exist indefinitely.

q: If '8' Drosophila in a laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is ______ individuals per Drosophila per week.
e: Death rate = number of deaths / population size = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week.

q: Mycorrhizae are the example of:
e: Mycorrhizae represent a mutualistic association between fungi and plant roots, where the fungus helps the plant absorb water/nutrients and receives photosynthates in return, benefiting both partners.

q: Which of the following regions of the globe exhibits highest species diversity?
e: The Amazon rainforest is renowned for having the highest species diversity of any region on Earth, due to its vast size, stable climate and high rainfall.

q: Which of the following is not an attribute of a population?
e: Sex ratio, natality and mortality are all intrinsic attributes/characteristics of a population itself, while species interaction refers to relationships between different populations/species, not an attribute of a single population.

t: Meaning of 'e' in exponential growth equation
q: In the exponential growth equation Nt=N0ert, e represents:
e: In the exponential growth equation, 'e' represents the base of natural logarithms (≈2.718).

q: Autecology is the
o: relation of a population to its environment.
relation of an individual (species) to its environment.
relation of a community to its environment.
relation of a biome to its environment.
e: Autecology is the branch of ecology that studies the relationship of an individual organism or single species to its environment, as opposed to synecology, which studies communities.

q: The biosphere is
o: composed of the plants present in the soil.
composed of all living organisms present on earth which interact with the physical environment.
e: The biosphere encompasses all living organisms on Earth together with their interactions with the physical (abiotic) environment, forming the global sum of all ecosystems.

q: The salt concentration (salinity) of the sea, measured in parts per thousand, is
e: The average salinity of open ocean sea water is approximately 30 to 35 parts per thousand.

q: Lichens are the association of
e: Lichens are a symbiotic association between a fungus and a photosynthetic alga (or cyanobacterium), where the fungus provides structure and protection while the alga provides nutrients through photosynthesis.

q: Which growth model does NOT show carrying capacity?
e: Exponential (J-shaped) growth: dN/dt=rN has no upper limit. Logistic (S-shaped) includes K (carrying capacity): dN/dt=rN(K-N)/K. Carrying capacity = max sustainable population.

q: Which one of the following equations represents the Verhulst-pearl Logistic Growth of population?
e: The Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth of population is described by the equation dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, where N is population size, r is intrinsic rate of natural increase, K is carrying capacity.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that two closely related species competing for different resources cannot exist indefinitely.
Statement II: According to Gause's principle, during competition, the inferior will be eliminated. This may be true if resources are limiting.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
e: Statement I is false because Gause's principle actually applies to species competing for the SAME limiting resources (not different resources) — two species competing for identical resources cannot coexist indefinitely. Statement II is true as it correctly describes the outcome of such competition when resources are limiting.

q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct? (1) Algal blooms caused by excess of organic matter in water improve water quality and promote fisheries. (2) Water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and leads to an imbalance in the ecosystem dynamics of the water body. (3) The amount of some toxic substance of industrial waste water increases in the organisms at successive trophic levels. (4) The micro-organisms involved in biodegradation of organic matter in a sewage polluted water body consume a lot of oxygen causing the death of aquatic organisms.
o: Algal blooms caused by excess of organic matter in water improve water quality and promote fisheries.
Water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and leads to an imbalance in the ecosystem dynamics of the water body.
The amount of some toxic substance of industrial waste water increases in the organisms at successive trophic levels.
The micro-organisms involved in biodegradation of organic matter in a sewage polluted water body consume a lot of oxygen causing the death of aquatic organisms.
e: Statement 1 is NOT correct — algal blooms caused by excess organic matter (eutrophication) actually deteriorate water quality and cause large-scale fish mortality, not improve water quality or promote fisheries. The other statements correctly describe effects of water hyacinth, biomagnification, and biodegradation.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle states that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually. Statement II: In general, carnivores are more adversely affected by competition than herbivores. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
e: Statement I is correct — this is the accurate statement of Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle. Statement II is false — it is generally herbivores (not carnivores) that are shown to be more adversely affected by interspecific competition in several studies cited in NCERT.

q: Match List I (Interaction) with List II (Species A and B effects): A. Mutualism, B. Commensalism, C. Amensalism, D. Parasitism. List II: I. +(A), 0(B), II. -(A), 0(B), III. +(A), -(B), IV. +(A), +(B). Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Mutualism benefits both species: +(A), +(B) (A-IV). Commensalism benefits one species while the other is unaffected: +(A), 0(B) (B-I). Amensalism harms one species while the other is unaffected: -(A), 0(B) (C-II). Parasitism benefits one species (parasite) while harming the other (host): +(A), -(B) (D-III). So the correct match is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

q: Match List I with List II: (Interacting species) A. A Leopard and a Lion in a forest/grassland, B. A Cuckoo laying egg in a Crow's nest, C. Fungi and root of a higher plant in Mycorrhizae, D. A cattle egret and a Cattle in a field. (Name of Interaction) I. Competition, II. Brood parasitism, III. Mutualism, IV. Commensalism. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Leopard and Lion competing for the same prey/territory represents competition (A-I). Cuckoo laying eggs in a crow's nest is brood parasitism (B-II). Fungi and plant roots in mycorrhizae represent mutualism (C-III). Cattle egret and cattle represent commensalism (D-IV). So the correct match is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

t: Population Growth Models and Age Pyramids
q: Match List I with List II: A. Logistic growth, B. Exponential growth, C. Expanding age pyramid, D. Stable age pyramid. List II: I. Unlimited resource availability condition, II. Limited resource availability condition, III. The percent individuals of pre-reproductive age is largest followed by reproductive and post-reproductive age groups, IV. The percent individuals of pre-reproductive and reproductive age group are same. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Logistic growth occurs under limited resource availability (A-II). Exponential growth occurs under unlimited resource availability (B-I). Expanding age pyramid has the largest percentage of pre-reproductive individuals, followed by reproductive and post-reproductive (C-III). Stable age pyramid has roughly equal percentages of pre-reproductive and reproductive age groups (D-IV). So the correct match is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Both species are harmed, (B) One species is harmed and the other is benefited, (C) Both species are benefited, (D) One is benefited while the other has no effect
List-II: (I) Predation, (II) Mutualism, (III) Competition, (IV) Commensalism
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: When both species are harmed, it is competition (III). When one species is harmed and the other benefited, it is predation (I) (predator benefits, prey harmed). When both species are benefited, it is mutualism (II). When one is benefited while the other has no effect, it is commensalism (IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

q: Consider a population of 10 million cells. Given the per-capita birth rate of 0.002 (per unit time) and the per-capita death rate of 0.002 (per unit time), the expected number of cells after 10 generations is________.
e: The net growth rate r = birth rate - death rate = 0.002 - 0.002 = 0. With a net growth rate of zero, the population size remains constant (neither growing nor declining) over successive generations, so after 10 generations the population remains 10 million.

q: Which of the following is correct for r-selected species?
o: Small number of progeny with large size
Large number of progeny with small size
Large number of progeny with large size
Small number of progeny with small size
e: r-selected species produce a large number of progeny, each of small size, with high reproductive rate and little parental care.

q: If '+' sign is assigned to beneficial interaction, '-' sign to detrimental and '0' sign to neutral interaction, then the population interaction represented by '+' '-' refers to:
e: Parasitism is represented by (+,-): the parasite benefits (+) while the host is harmed (-)

q:
Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
(1) Water hyacinth, growing in the standing water, drains oxygen from water that leads to the death of fishes.
(2) Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are called clone.
(3) Microscopic, motile asexual reproductive structures are called zoospores.
(4) In potato, banana and ginger, the plantlets arise from the internodes present in the modified stem.
e: Plantlets in potato, banana and ginger arise from nodes (buds/eyes) of the modified stem, not internodes, making statement 4 incorrect.

q: Inspite of interspecific competition in nature, which mechanism the competing species might have evolved for their survival?
e: Resource partitioning allows competing species to coexist by differentiating their niches (e.g., different feeding times, microhabitats) to avoid direct competition for the same resources.

q: Amensalism can be represented as:
e: In amensalism, one species (A) is harmed (-) while the other (B) is unaffected (0), e.g., Penicillium secreting penicillin that harms bacteria without benefiting itself.

q:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I: (a) Allen's Rule (b) Physiological adaptation (c) Behavioural adaptation (d) Biochemical adaptation
List - II: (i) Kangaroo rat (ii) Desert lizard (iii) Marine fish at depth (iv) Polar seal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
e: Allen's Rule is exemplified by Polar seal (body proportions adapted to cold); Physiological adaptation by Kangaroo rat (concentrated urine); Behavioural adaptation by Desert lizard (basking behaviour); Biochemical adaptation by Marine fish at depth (pressure-resistant proteins).

q: Which one of the following statements cannot be connected to Predation?
o: It helps in maintaining species diversity in a community
It might lead to extinction of a species
Both the interacting species are negatively impacted
It is necessitated by nature to maintain the ecological balance
e: In predation, one species (predator) benefits while the other (prey) is harmed (+/- interaction), not both negatively impacted (which would describe competition, a -/- interaction). So statement 3 cannot be connected to predation.

q: While explaining interspecific interaction of population, (+) sign is assigned for beneficial interaction, (-) sign is assigned for detrimental interaction and (0) for neutral interaction. Which of the following interactions can be assigned (+) for one species and (-) for another species involved in the interaction?
e: Predation is a (+/-) interaction: the predator benefits (+) while the prey is harmed (-). Amensalism is (0/-), commensalism is (+/0), and competition is (-/-), none of which match the (+) for one and (-) for the other pattern.

q: Alexander Von Humbolt described for the first time:
e: Alexander von Humboldt was the first to describe the species-area relationship, observing that within a region, species richness increased with explored area, following a roughly rectangular hyperbola.

q: Asymptote in a logistic growth curve is obtained when:
e: In the logistic growth model, dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, population growth slows and plateaus (asymptote) as the population size N approaches the carrying capacity K, i.e., when K = N.

q: Which one of the following population interactions is widely used in medical science for the production of antibiotics?
e: Amensalism, where one species is harmed and the other remains unaffected, is exemplified by the Penicillium fungus producing penicillin that inhibits bacterial growth, a principle widely used in antibiotic production.

q: In a growing population of a country,
o: pre-reproductive individuals are more than the reproductive individuals.
pre-reproductive individuals are less than the reproductive individuals.
reproductive and pre-reproductive individuals are equal in number.
reproductive individuals are less than the post-reproductive individuals.
e: In a growing (expanding) population, the age pyramid is broad at the base, meaning the pre-reproductive (young) age group outnumbers the reproductive age group, driving future population growth.

q: According to Robert May, the global species diversity is about:
e: According to Robert May's estimate, the total global species diversity is approximately 7 million species.

q: Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are examples of:
e: Flippers in penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) evolved independently in unrelated lineages to serve the similar function of swimming, which is a classic example of convergent evolution (analogous structures).

q: Choose the correct statements regarding population interactions between two species. A. In both parasitism and commensalism, only one species benefits and the other species is harmed. B. Both species benefit in mutualism. C. Both species benefit in commensalism. D. In parasitism, only one species benefits and the other is harmed. E. In amensalism, one species is harmed and the other is unaffected.
e: B (mutualism, both benefit), D (parasitism, one benefits one harmed), and E (amensalism, one harmed one unaffected) are correct. A is false since in commensalism, the other species is unaffected, not harmed; C is false since only one species benefits in commensalism. B, D and E only.

q: An ecological niche is
o: the surface area of the ocean.
the physical position and functional role of a species within the community.
formed of all plants and animals living at the bottom of a lake.
e: An ecological niche describes both the physical habitat a species occupies and the functional role (e.g. its feeding relationships, resource use) it plays within its community.

q: According to Allen's Rule, mammals from colder climates have
e: Allen's Rule states that mammals in colder climates tend to have shorter, more compact extremities (ears, limbs, tails), which reduces surface area relative to body volume and minimises heat loss.

t: Climatic Conditions for Tropical Forest Formation
q: The formation of tropical forests requires a mean annual temperature and mean annual precipitation of approximately
e: Tropical forests develop under warm (about 18–25°C mean annual temperature) and very wet (about 150–400 cm mean annual precipitation) climatic conditions.

q: Which of the following forest plants controls the light conditions at the ground level?
e: The tall trees forming the forest's upper canopy intercept most of the incoming sunlight, thereby controlling how much light filters down to reach the ground-level vegetation beneath them.

t: Survival of a Transplanted Forest Herb
q: What will happen to a well-growing herbaceous plant from the forest if it is transplanted outside the forest into a park?
o: It will grow well because it is planted in the same general locality.
It may not survive because of the change in its microclimate.
It will grow very well because the plant gets more sunlight.
e: Forest-floor herbs are adapted to the specific microclimate (shade, humidity, temperature) created by the forest canopy; moving such a plant to an open park drastically changes these conditions, and it may fail to survive.

q: Amensalism is an association between two species where
o: one species is harmed and the other is benefitted.
one species is harmed and the other is unaffected.
one species is benefitted and the other is unaffected.
e: In amensalism, one species is negatively affected (harmed or inhibited) by the interaction, while the other species involved remains completely unaffected.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List – I: A. Chlorophyll a, B. Chlorophyll b, C. Xanthophylls, D. Carotenoids. List – II: I. Yellow-green, II. Yellow, III. Blue-green, IV. Yellow to yellow orange. Choose the option with all correct matches.
e: Chlorophyll a is blue-green (III). Chlorophyll b is yellow-green (I). Xanthophylls are yellow (II). Carotenoids are yellow to yellow-orange (IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

q: Which pigment has absorption peak at 700 nm in the photosynthetic reaction centre PS I (P700)?
e: The reaction centre pigment of Photosystem I, designated P700 (absorption peak at 700 nm), is a special form of chlorophyll a.

t: Enzyme for carboxylation in Calvin cycle
q: The enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle is:
e: RuBisCO (RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase) catalyses the carboxylation of RuBP, the first step of the Calvin cycle.

q: Which metal ion is a constituent of chlorophyll?
e: Chlorophyll's porphyrin ring holds a central magnesium ion, essential for its light-absorbing function.

q: Which range of wavelength (in nm) is called photosynthetically active radiation (PAR)?
e: The 400-700 nm range of visible light is referred to as photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum usable by plants for photosynthesis.

q: With reference to factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis, which of the following statements is not correct?
o: Increasing atmospheric CO2 concentration up to 0.05% can enhance CO2 fixation rate
C3 plants respond to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis while C4 plants have much lower temperature optimum
Tomato is a greenhouse crop which can be grown in CO2-enriched atmosphere for higher yield
Light saturation for CO2 fixation occurs at 10% of full sunlight
e: In reality, C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum for photosynthesis than C3 plants (C4 plants perform better at higher temperatures due to their CO2-concentrating mechanism), the reverse of what statement (2) claims, making it the incorrect statement.

q: The oxygenation activity of RuBisCo enzyme in photorespiration leads to the formation of:
o: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
e: In photorespiration, the oxygenase activity of RuBisCO acts on RuBP with O2 to produce one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate (3-C compound) and one molecule of phosphoglycolate (2-C compound), with the key product counted here being 1 molecule of the 3-C compound.

t: Electron transport chain in light reactions (plastoquinone)
q: In light reaction, plastoquinone facilitates the transfer of electrons from:
e: Plastoquinone (PQ) is a mobile electron carrier that transfers electrons from Photosystem II (PS-II) to the cytochrome b6f complex in the light reaction electron transport chain.

q: Energy required for ATP synthesis associated with Photosystem II comes from
e: ATP synthesis during the light reaction occurs by chemiosmosis, driven by the proton (H+) gradient built up across the thylakoid membrane, which powers ATP synthase.

q: Splitting of water is associated with
o: the inner surface of the thylakoid membrane.
e: The splitting (photolysis) of water, associated with the water-splitting complex of Photosystem II, occurs on the lumenal side of the thylakoid membrane, releasing O2, protons, and electrons into the thylakoid lumen.

t: Electron Transport Chain in Light Reaction
q: The correct sequence of flow of electrons in the light reaction is
e: In the light reaction's electron transport chain, electrons flow from Photosystem II through plastoquinone and the cytochrome complex to Photosystem I, and finally to ferredoxin.

q: Which pigment is responsible for red and blue light absorption in plants?
e: Chlorophyll a (primary pigment) absorbs mainly red (680nm) and blue-violet (430nm) light. It is the only pigment that directly takes part in the light reactions of photosynthesis.

q: Which of the following statements about RuBisCO is true?
o: It is active only in the dark
It has higher affinity for oxygen than carbon dioxide.
it is an enzyme involved in the photolysis of water
It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP.
e: RuBisCO (Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase) is active both in light and dark, has a higher affinity for CO2 than O2 when both are at equal concentration, and catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP (ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate) in the Calvin cycle, not the photolysis of water.

t: Calvin Cycle - ATP and NADPH Requirement per CO2
q: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of CO2 fixed in the Calvin cycle?
o: 3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
e: For every CO2 molecule fixed in the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH are utilized. 11th NCERT Page No. 145.

q:
Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis?
(A) Light (B) Chlorophyll (C) CO2 (D) ATP (E) NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: The dark reaction (Calvin cycle/biosynthetic phase) requires CO2, ATP and NADPH (produced from the light reaction) but does not directly require light or chlorophyll. So C, D and E only. 11th NCERT Page No. 142.

t: Photorespiration in C3 and C4 Plants
q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: In C3 plants, some O2 binds to RuBisCO, hence CO2 fixation is decreased.
Statement-II: In C4 plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.
In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
e: In C3 plants, RuBisCO's oxygenase activity causes O2 to bind instead of CO2, reducing CO2 fixation (Statement-I is true). In C4 plants, it is actually the reverse of Statement-II: mesophyll cells show no photorespiration while bundle sheath cells (which lack PSII and have high CO2 concentration) show negligible photorespiration too — the statement as given mismatches the actual biology, making Statement-II false.

t: Calvin Cycle - ATP and NADPH Requirement
q: How many ATP and NADPH2 are required for the synthesis of one molecule of Glucose during the Calvin cycle?
e: The Calvin cycle requires 18 ATP and 12 NADPH2 to synthesize one molecule of glucose (for 6 turns of the cycle fixing 6 CO2 molecules).

q: Which micronutrient is required for splitting of water molecule during photosynthesis?
e: Manganese is a required micronutrient for the photolysis (splitting) of water during the light reactions of photosynthesis, as part of the oxygen-evolving complex.

q: The reaction centre in PS II has its absorption maxima at:
e: The reaction centre chlorophyll a molecule of Photosystem II (PS II) has an absorption maxima at 680 nm, hence it is called P680.

q: Which of the following combinations is required for chemiosmosis?
o: membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, NADP synthase
proton pump, electron gradient, ATP synthase
proton pump, electron gradient, NADP synthase
membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, ATP synthase
e: Chemiosmosis requires a membrane (to maintain the gradient), a proton pump (to pump protons across the membrane), a proton gradient (built up across the membrane), and ATP synthase (which uses the proton gradient to synthesize ATP).

q:
Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct?
(a) Does not occur in C3 plants
(b) CO2 is consumed and O2 is generated
(c) Phosphoglycolate is formed
(d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Photorespiration DOES occur in C3 plants (it is a characteristic wasteful pathway in C3 plants, largely absent in C4 plants due to the CO2-concentrating mechanism), so (a) is false. Photorespiration consumes O2 and releases CO2 (opposite of what (b) states), so (b) is false. RuBisCO's oxygenase activity on RuBP produces phosphoglycolate, which is then metabolized -- (c) is correct. Unlike photosynthesis, photorespiration does not result in net synthesis of ATP or NADPH -- (d) is correct. So (c) and (d) only.

t: Calvin Cycle - Turns Required for Glucose Formation
q: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose?
e: Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes 1 molecule of CO2. Formation of 1 molecule of glucose (6 carbons) requires 6 turns of the Calvin cycle (fixing 6 CO2 molecules). For 3 molecules of glucose, 3 × 6 = 18 turns are required.

q: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
o: Role of air → release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → role of air
Production of glucose → role of air → release of oxygen → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → production of glucose → release of oxygen → role of air
e: Historically, photosynthesis research progressed in this order: first the role of air was established (Joseph Priestley, Jan Ingenhousz), then the release of oxygen was discovered, followed by the demonstration of glucose (carbohydrate) production, and later the study of the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b (T.W. Engelmann and others) in relation to photosynthetic activity.

q: The process which makes the major difference between C3 and C4 plants is:
e: C4 plants minimize photorespiration due to their bundle sheath cells and CO2-concentrating mechanism, unlike C3 plants where photorespiration significantly reduces photosynthetic efficiency — this is the major functional difference.

q: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in sorghum is:
e: Sorghum is a C4 plant; the first stable product of CO2 fixation via PEP carboxylase in C4 plants is oxaloacetic acid (OAA), a 4-carbon compound.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The primary CO2 acceptor in C4 plants is phosphoenolpyruvate and is found in the mesophyll cells. Statement II: Mesophyll cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCo enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Both statements are correct: in C4 plants, PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) is the primary CO2 acceptor present in mesophyll cells (catalyzed by PEP carboxylase), and RuBisCo is absent from mesophyll cells, being present only in bundle sheath cells.

q: Which one of the following is not true regarding the release of energy during ATP synthesis through chemiosmosis? It involves:
o: Movement of protons across the membrane to the stroma
Reduction of NADP to NADPH2 on the stroma side of the membrane
e: Chemiosmosis involves the breakdown of the proton gradient (not an 'electron gradient', which is not a standard term in this context) as protons flow through ATP synthase, driving ATP synthesis. The other statements about proton movement to stroma and NADPH formation on the stroma side are correct aspects of the process.

t: Bundle Sheath Cells in C4 Plants
q: What is the role of large bundle sheath cells found around the vascular bundles in C4 plants?
o: To provide the site for photorespiratory pathway
To increase the number of chloroplast for the operation of Calvin cycle
To enable the plant to tolerate high temperature
To protect the vascular tissue from high light intensity
e: Bundle sheath cells in C4 plants contain numerous chloroplasts (often agranal) where the Calvin cycle (C3 pathway/CO2 fixation via RuBisCo) operates, isolated from atmospheric oxygen to minimize photorespiration.

q: Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) is the primary CO2 acceptor in:
e: In C4 plants, PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) acts as the primary CO2 acceptor in mesophyll cells, fixing CO2 via the enzyme PEP carboxylase to form the 4-carbon compound oxaloacetate, before CO2 is released again in the bundle sheath cells for the Calvin cycle.

q: Which of the following is not a product of light reaction of photosynthesis?
e: The light reactions of photosynthesis produce ATP, NADPH and oxygen (from the splitting of water); NADH is not a product of the light reactions (it is primarily associated with respiration).

q: Oxygen is not produced during photosynthesis by
e: Green sulphur bacteria perform anoxygenic photosynthesis, using H2S instead of H2O as the electron donor, and therefore do not produce oxygen, unlike Chara, Cycas and Nostoc which perform oxygenic photosynthesis.

q: Find the incorrect statement(s) about photosynthesis from the following: A. The water splitting complex is associated with PS I. B. C4 plants use the C3 pathway of CO2 fixation as the main biosynthetic pathway. C. In C4 plants, photorespiration does not occur. D. C3 plants exhibit 'Kranz' anatomy. E. ATP synthesis in chloroplast occurs through chemiosmosis.
e: A is false (water-splitting complex is with PS II, not PS I); D is false (Kranz anatomy is a feature of C4, not C3, plants). B, C, E are true. So A and D only are incorrect.

t: ATP and NADPH required for one glucose via Calvin pathway
q: How many ATP and NADPH molecules are required to make one molecule of glucose through the Calvin pathway?
e: The Calvin cycle requires 18 ATP and 12 NADPH to synthesize one molecule of glucose.

q: Which pigment acts directly to convert light energy into chemical energy?
e: Chlorophyll a is the primary pigment at the reaction centre that directly participates in converting absorbed light energy into chemical energy; other pigments act as accessory pigments that pass energy to it.

q: Which light range is least effective in photosynthesis?
e: Green light is largely reflected (not absorbed) by chlorophyll pigments, making it the least effective wavelength range for driving photosynthesis, as shown by the dip in the action spectrum around green light.

q: Chemosynthetic bacteria obtain energy from
e: Chemosynthetic (chemoautotrophic) bacteria derive energy from the oxidation of inorganic chemicals (such as H2S, NH3, or Fe2+), rather than from light.

q: During the light reaction in photosynthesis, the following are formed:
o: ATP, hydrogen and an O2 donor.
e: The light reaction produces ATP (via chemiosmosis), reduced NADPH (the 'hydrogen' carrier), and O2 (released from the splitting of water) — sugar is formed later in the dark reaction, not the light reaction.

q: The dark reaction in photosynthesis is called so because
o: it can occur in the dark also.
it does not depend on light energy.
it occurs more rapidly at night.
e: The 'dark reaction' (carbon fixation/Calvin cycle) does not itself require light directly and can proceed in the dark (using ATP and NADPH already produced), though in practice it usually occurs during the day alongside the light reaction.

t: Primary CO2 Acceptor in C4 Plants
q: PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) is the primary CO2 acceptor in
e: In C4 plants, CO2 is first fixed by combining with PEP (catalysed by PEP carboxylase) to form oxaloacetate, before being passed on to the Calvin cycle in bundle sheath cells.

q: The enzyme that is not found in a C3 plant is
e: PEP carboxylase is the enzyme specific to C4 plants (and CAM plants) for primary CO2 fixation into oxaloacetate; it is not present in C3 plants, which rely solely on RuBP carboxylase for CO2 fixation.

q: The reaction responsible for the primary fixation of CO2 is catalysed by
o: both RuBP carboxylase and PEP carboxylase.
e: Primary CO2 fixation is catalysed by RuBP carboxylase (Rubisco) in C3 plants and by PEP carboxylase in C4 plants — both enzymes serve this role depending on the plant type.

t: First Stable Product of C4 Pathway
q: When CO2 is added to PEP, the first stable product synthesised is
e: The carboxylation of PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) by PEP carboxylase, with the addition of CO2, directly yields oxaloacetate (OAA), a 4-carbon compound, as the first stable product in the C4 pathway.

q: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called:
e: Totipotency is the inherent capacity of a plant cell to generate a whole plant/organism, given appropriate conditions. 12th NCERT Page No. 178.

q: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus, increasing the yield?
e: Gibberellins promote stem elongation. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, which directly increases the commercial yield of sugarcane as the stem is the harvested product.

q: In tissue culture experiments, leaf mesophyll cells are put in a culture medium to form callus. This phenomenon may be called as:
e: Dedifferentiation is the phenomenon where living differentiated cells (like leaf mesophyll cells) regain the capacity to divide under appropriate conditions, forming a mass of undifferentiated cells (callus).

q: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the 7th day?
e: For arithmetic growth, Length at time t = L0 + (growth rate × t) = 20 + (30 × 7) = 20 + 210 = 230 cm.

q: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage?
e: Gibberellins are well known for causing a marked increase in internode elongation (bolting) prior to flowering in rosette plants such as cabbage.

q: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide?
e: 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective herbicide to kill broad-leaved weeds (dicots) without affecting monocot crops like cereals.

q: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called:
e: Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different developmental pathways in response to environmental conditions or life phases, forming different structures (e.g., heterophylly).

q: The plant hormone used to destroy weeds in a field:
e: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective herbicide to destroy dicot weeds in cereal crop fields.

q: Growth can be measured in various ways. Which of these can be used as parameters to measure growth?
e: Plant growth can be quantified by increase in cell number (via division), increase in cell size, or overall increase in length/weight — all are valid growth parameters.

q: Monocarpic plants are those which
e: Monocarpic plants (e.g., bamboo, agave) flower only once in their lifetime and die shortly after, having completed their reproductive cycle.

q:
Read the following statements on plant growth and development.
A. Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins.
B. Plant growth regulators can be involved in promotion as well as inhibition of growth.
C. Dedifferentiation is a pre-requisite for re-differentiation.
D. Abscisic acid is a plant growth promoter.
E. Apical dominance promotes the growth of lateral buds.
Choose the options with all correct statements.
e: Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins (A, correct). Growth regulators like auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins are promoters, while ABA is an inhibitor - so PGRs are involved in both promotion and inhibition (B, correct). Dedifferentiation (cell division forming new cells) is a pre-requisite for redifferentiation into permanent tissues (C, correct). Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor, not promoter (D, incorrect). Apical dominance suppresses (not promotes) the growth of lateral buds (E, incorrect). So A, B, C Only.

q: Which one of the following phytohormones promotes nutrient mobilization which helps in the delay of leaf senescence in plants?
e: Cytokinins help overcome apical dominance and promote nutrient mobilization, which helps delay leaf senescence.

t: Auxin Herbicide - Selective Action on Dicot Weeds
q: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin
o: Does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
Can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth
Promotes abscission of mature leaves only
e: Synthetic auxins like 2,4-D are used as selective herbicides because they do not affect mature monocotyledonous plants (grasses) but kill broad-leaved dicot weeds. 11th NCERT Page No. 176.

q: Which hormone promotes internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice?
e: Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants, helping them keep pace with rising flood water levels.

q: Spraying of which of the following phytohormone on juvenile conifers helps in hastening the maturity period, that leads to early seed production?
e: Spraying gibberellic acid (GA3) on juvenile conifers hastens maturity and leads to early seed production, a well-documented commercial application of gibberellins.

q: You are given a tissue with its potential for differentiation in an artificial culture. Which of the following pairs of hormones would you add to the medium to secure shoots as well as roots?
e: Auxin and cytokinin in appropriate ratios control shoot and root differentiation in tissue culture (high cytokinin:auxin → shoots, high auxin:cytokinin → roots)

q: Phytochrome is a:
e: Phytochrome is a chromoprotein pigment involved in photoperiodism and other light-regulated plant responses.

q: In plant tissue culture, which combination of hormones is used to induce shoot and root formation respectively from a callus?
o: Cytokinin for shoots, Auxin for roots
Auxin for shoots, Cytokinin for roots
Gibberellin for shoots, Auxin for roots
Ethylene for shoots, Cytokinin for roots
e: A high cytokinin:auxin ratio induces shoot formation from callus, while a high auxin:cytokinin ratio induces root formation — the basis of organogenesis in micropropagation.

q: Phytochrome, the pigment involved in photoperiodism, is chemically a:
e: Phytochrome is a chromoprotein — a protein (apoprotein) covalently linked to a chromophore (phycocyanobilin-like pigment) that senses red/far-red light.

q: The site of perception of light in plants during photoperiodism is:
e: The leaf is the site of perception of photoperiodic stimulus (light duration) in plants, which then triggers a signal that induces flowering at the shoot apex.

q: It takes very long time for pineapple plants to produce flowers. Which combination of hormones can be applied to artificially induce flowering in pineapple plants throughout the year to increase yield?
e: Auxin and ethylene are used together to artificially induce flowering in pineapple plants throughout the year, increasing commercial yield.

q: What is the site of perception of photoperiod necessary for induction of flowering in plants?
e: Leaves are the site of perception of photoperiod for induction of flowering; the signal (florigen) is then transmitted to the shoot apex where flowering is induced.

q: The gaseous plant growth regulator is used in plants to:
o: promote root growth and root hair formation to increase the absorption surface
kill dicotyledonous weeds in the fields
e: Ethylene (the gaseous plant growth regulator) promotes root growth and root hair formation, increasing the absorptive surface area, among its other effects like fruit ripening and senescence promotion.

q: Production of Cucumber has increased manifold in recent years. Application of which of the following phytohormones has resulted in this increased yield as the hormone is known to produce female flowers in the plants:
e: Ethylene promotes femaleness (production of female flowers) in cucumber plants, which increases fruit yield since cucumber fruits develop from female flowers.

q: Fruit and leaf drop at early stages can be prevented by the application of:
e: Auxins prevent premature fruit and leaf drop (abscission) by inhibiting the formation of the abscission layer, while ethylene actually promotes abscission.

t: Gibberellins and stem elongation in sugarcane
q: Name the plant growth regulator which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane crop.
e: Gibberellins promote stem elongation (internode elongation), and spraying them on sugarcane crops increases stem length, thereby increasing the sugar yield per plant.

q: The process of growth is maximum during:
e: During the log (exponential) phase, growth rate is at its maximum, as cells/organisms divide and grow rapidly under favourable conditions, unlike the lag phase (initial slow growth), senescence (decline) or dormancy (no growth).

q: Which of the following is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy?
e: Gibberellic acid is a growth-promoting hormone that actually breaks seed dormancy (promotes germination), unlike abscisic acid, phenolic acid and para-ascorbic acid, which inhibit germination and maintain dormancy.

t: Role of Ethylene in Fruit Ripening
q: Ethylene is used for
e: Ethylene is a ripening hormone that promotes (hastens) fruit ripening; it does not retard or slow down ripening in tomatoes or apples, making option (b) the sole correct choice.

q: Coconut water contains
e: Coconut water (liquid endosperm) is a well-known natural source of cytokinins, historically used to promote cell division in plant tissue culture.

q: The effect of apical dominance can be overcome by which of the following hormones?
e: Cytokinins promote lateral (axillary) bud growth, counteracting the auxin-driven apical dominance that normally suppresses lateral bud development.

q: Apples are generally wrapped in waxed paper to
o: prevent sunlight from changing their colour.
prevent aerobic respiration by checking O2 entry.
prevent ethylene formation due to injury.
e: Wrapping apples in waxed paper limits oxygen entry, slowing aerobic respiration and thereby delaying the ripening and spoilage process.

q: The term 'synergistic action' of hormones refers to
o: when two hormones act together but bring about opposite effects.
when two hormones act together and contribute to the same function.
when one hormone affects more than one function.
when many hormones bring about any one function.
e: Synergism refers to two (or more) hormones acting together to enhance or contribute towards the same physiological function, as opposed to antagonism, where hormones act in opposite directions.

q: Plasticity in plant growth means that
o: plant development is dependent on the environment.
e: Plasticity refers to the ability of plants to follow different growth/developmental pathways in response to the environment (e.g., heterophylly), rather than a fixed, rigid developmental path.

q: To increase sugar production in sugarcane, plants are sprayed with
e: Spraying sugarcane crops with gibberellins increases internode length and stem growth, which enhances overall sugar yield.

q: ABA (abscisic acid) acts antagonistic to
e: Abscisic acid (ABA), the stress/dormancy-promoting hormone, acts antagonistically to gibberellic acid (GA), which promotes growth and germination — their opposing actions regulate processes like seed dormancy.

q: The photoperiod in plants is perceived at
e: The photoperiod (day length) is perceived by phytochrome pigments located in the leaves, which then signal the plant to initiate flowering when appropriate.

q: Bryophytes are called amphibians of plant kingdom because:
o: They need water for fertilization but live on land
They have both roots and leaves
e: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) grow on land but require water for fertilization since male gametes are motile (swim to archegonium). Similar to amphibians needing water to reproduce.

q: Which is NOT a gymnosperm?
e: Eucalyptus is an angiosperm (dicot, family Myrtaceae). Pinus, Cycas and Gnetum are all gymnosperms (naked seed plants — seeds not enclosed in fruit). Gymnosperm: naked seed.

q: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
e: Gymnosperms (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed/naked, both before and after fertilization. Class 11th NCERT Page No 34.

q: In bryophytes, the gemmae help in which one of the following?
e: Asexual reproduction in liverworts (bryophytes) takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialised structures called gemmae (singular: gemma). Class 11th NCERT Page No 29.

q: Sphenopsida class belongs to__________.
e: Sphenopsida (e.g., Equisetum) is one of the classes within Pteridophytes.

q: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. Such plants are known as:
e: Plants producing two kinds of spores (microspores and megaspores) like Selaginella and Salvinia are called heterosporous.

q: Cyanobacteria are classified under
e: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are prokaryotic organisms and are classified under kingdom Monera, not under the (eukaryotic) algae of Plantae.

t: Classification features of algae and fungi
q: Which one is wrongly matched?
e: Chlorella is correctly a unicellular green alga, so this pairing is actually correct; per the official answer key, the pairing marked as wrong among the options is 'Unicellular organism - Chlorella'.

q: The embryo sac of an angiosperm is made up of
e: The mature angiosperm embryo sac typically has 7 cells but 8 nuclei in total, because the central cell contains two polar nuclei within a single cell.

q: If the diploid chromosome number of a flowering plant is 36, what would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
e: The endosperm of angiosperms is typically triploid (3n), formed by fusion of a male gamete (n) with the diploid (2n) central cell. With 2n = 36, n = 18, so the endosperm (3n) = 3 × 18 = 54.

q: Given below are the stages in the life cycle of pteridophytes. Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence. A. Prothallus stage. B. Meiosis in spore mother cells. C. Fertilisation. D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte. E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
e: Life cycle sequence: Meiosis in spore mother cells produces spores (B) → spores germinate to form the prothallus/gametophyte (A) → formation of archegonia and antheridia on the gametophyte (D) → transfer of antherozoids to archegonia via water (E) → fertilisation occurs (C). So B, A, D, E, C.

q: The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of bryophytes is: A. Fusion of antherozoid with egg. B. Attachment of gametophyte to substratum. C. Reduction division to produce haploid spores. D. Formation of sporophyte. E. Release of antherozoids into water. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Sequence: gametophyte attaches to substratum (B) → antherozoids released into water (E) → antherozoid fuses with egg (A) → sporophyte forms after fertilization (D) → reduction division (meiosis) in sporophyte produces haploid spores (C). So B, E, A, D, C.

t: Plant Group Examples (Match List: Pteridophyte, Bryophyte, Angiosperm, Gymnosperm)
q:
Match List I with List II.
List-I: (A) Pteridophyte (B) Bryophyte (C) Angiosperm (D) Gymnosperm
List-II: (I) Salvia (II) Ginkgo (III) Polytrichum (IV) Salvinia
Choose the option with all correct matches.
e: Salvinia is a Pteridophyte (IV). Polytrichum is a Bryophyte (III). Salvia is an Angiosperm (I). Ginkgo is a Gymnosperm (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II. Class 11th NCERT Page No 30, 32.

q: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
e: Fungi are classified based on mode of spore formation, fruiting body structure, and morphology of mycelium. Mode of nutrition is not a primary criterion used for fungal classification. 11th NCERT Page No. 16.

q:
Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements: In the members of Phaeophyceae,
A. Asexual reproduction occurs usually by biflagellate zoospores.
B. Sexual reproduction is by oogamous method only.
C. Stored food is in the form of carbohydrates which is either mannitol or laminarin.
D. The major pigments found are chlorophyll a, c and carotenoids and xanthophyll.
E. Vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall, usually covered on the outside by gelatinous coating of algin.
Choose the correct answer from the option given below.
o: A, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
e: In Phaeophyceae, sexual reproduction ranges from isogamous to oogamous (not oogamous only), so statement B is incorrect. The other statements — biflagellate zoospores for asexual reproduction, mannitol/laminarin as stored food, chlorophyll a and c with carotenoids and xanthophyll as pigments, and cellulosic walls coated with algin — are all correct, giving A, C, D and E only.

q: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: The first stage of gametophyte in the life cycle of moss is protonema stage. Reason R: Protonema develops directly from spores produced in capsule. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
o: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
e: Assertion A is correct — the protonema is the first (juvenile, filamentous) stage of the gametophyte generation in mosses. Reason R is correct and explains A — the protonema develops directly by germination of spores produced inside the capsule (sporangium).

q: Family Fabaceae differs from Solanaceae and Liliaceae. With respect to the stamens, pick out the characteristics specific to family Fabaceae but not found in Solanaceae or Liliaceae.
e: Fabaceae typically shows diadelphous stamens (9+1 arrangement, filaments united in two bundles) with dithecous anthers, a characteristic not found in Solanaceae or Liliaceae.

q: Identify the pair of heterosporous pteridophytes among the following:
e: Selaginella and Salvinia are both heterosporous pteridophytes, producing two kinds of spores (microspores and megaspores). Psilotum, Equisetum, and Lycopodium are homosporous.

q: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: In gymnosperms the pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents. Reason R: Air currents carry the pollen grains to the mouth of the archegonia where the male gametes are discharged and pollen tube is not formed. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
e: Assertion A is true — in gymnosperms, pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents to the ovule. Reason R is false — in gymnosperms, pollen tubes ARE typically formed (except in a few cases like Cycas and Ginkgo with motile sperm), and the air currents carry pollen to the micropyle, not directly to discharge male gametes at the mouth of the archegonia without a pollen tube in most gymnosperms.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes remain within the sporangia.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, seeds are not covered.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
e: In gymnosperms, the male gametophyte (pollen grain) and female gametophyte both develop and remain retained within their respective sporangia rather than becoming free-living -- Statement I is correct. Gymnosperm seeds are 'naked', not enclosed within a fruit (ovary wall), which is a defining characteristic of this group -- Statement II is correct. Both statements are correct.

q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Fusion of protoplasms between gametes, B. Fusion of two nuclei, C. Generation of haploid spores
List-II: I. Meiosis, II. Plasmogamy, III. Karyogamy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Fusion of protoplasms between two gametes/cells is called plasmogamy (II). Fusion of two nuclei (following plasmogamy) is called karyogamy (III). Generation of haploid spores from a diploid cell occurs through meiosis (I). So A-II, B-III, C-I.

q: Gemmae are present in:
e: Gemmae are multicellular, asexual reproductive structures found in some liverworts (like Marchantia), produced in gemma cups.

q: Which of the following plants is monoecious?
e: Chara is monoecious, bearing both male (antheridia) and female (oogonia) reproductive structures on the same plant. Cycas, papaya and Marchantia are dioecious.

q: Pinus seed cannot germinate and establish without fungal association. This is because:
o: It has very hard seed coat
Its seeds contain inhibitors that prevent germination.
It has obligate association with mycorrhizae.
e: Pinus has an obligate association with mycorrhizal fungi, which is necessary for seed germination and establishment of the seedling.

t: Life Cycles of Plant Groups - Matching
q: Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits: (a) Spirogyra (b) Fern (c) Funaria (d) Cycas -- List-II: (i) Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte (ii) Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (iii) Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus (iv) Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Spirogyra (alga) has a dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (ii). Fern has a dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte prothallus (iii). Funaria (moss) has a dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent sporophyte (iv). Cycas (gymnosperm) has dominant diploid sporophyte with highly reduced gametophyte (i). So a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

q: Strobili or cones are found in:
e: Equisetum (a pteridophyte, horsetail) bears strobili (cone-like reproductive structures) at the tip of its stems, unlike Salvinia, Pteris (ferns without true cones) or Marchantia (a bryophyte).

q:
Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits:
List-I: (a) Spirogyra (b) Fern (c) Funaria (d) Cycas
List-II: (i) Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte (ii) Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (iii) Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus (iv) Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e: Spirogyra has dominant haploid free-living gametophyte(ii), Fern has dominant sporophyte with reduced prothallus gametophyte(iii), Funaria has dominant haploid leafy gametophyte(iv), Cycas has dominant diploid sporophyte with reduced gametophyte(i). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

q: Fusion of two motile gametes which are dissimilar in size is termed as
e: Anisogamy refers to the fusion of two motile (flagellated) gametes that differ in size. Isogamy involves gametes of similar size and motility, while oogamy involves fusion of a large, non-motile female gamete with a small, motile male gamete.

q: Holdfast, stipe and frond constitute the plant body in the case of
e: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) have a differentiated plant body consisting of a holdfast (for attachment), stipe (stalk), and frond (leaf-like blade), unlike the simpler bodies of red or green algae.

q: A plant group showing thallus organisation, presence of rhizoids, a dominant haploid phase, and requiring water for the motile male gametes to reach the egg best identifies which group?
e: Bryophytes have a thallus-like or simple plant body, rhizoids instead of true roots, a dominant gametophytic (haploid) generation, and depend on water for the motile male gametes to swim to the egg for fertilisation.

q: A prothallus is
o: a structure in pteridophytes formed before the thallus develops.
a sporophytic free-living structure formed in pteridophytes.
a gametophytic free-living structure formed in pteridophytes.
a primitive structure formed after fertilisation in pteridophytes.
e: The prothallus is the small, free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte generation of pteridophytes (ferns), developing from a germinated spore before producing gametes.

q: Plants of a certain group are diploid and well adapted to extreme conditions, bearing sporophylls arranged in compact structures called cones. This group is
e: Gymnosperms are typically perennial, woody, diploid plants well adapted to extreme environments, with sporophylls (spore-bearing leaves) organised into compact cones (strobili).

q: The giant Redwood tree (Sequoia sempervirens) is a/an
e: Sequoia sempervirens (coast redwood) is a conifer, placed within the Gymnosperms, which include some of the tallest and most massive living trees.

q: Phenotypic ratio in F2 of monohybrid cross (Tt × Tt) is:
e: F2 of Tt × Tt = TT:Tt:tt = 1:2:1 genotypically. Since T is dominant, TT and Tt appear tall. Phenotypic ratio = 3 Tall:1 Dwarf = 3:1.

q: What is the pattern of inheritance for polygenic trait?
e: Polygenic traits are controlled by multiple genes contributing additively to the phenotype, showing continuous variation (e.g., height, skin colour) — this is a non-Mendelian inheritance pattern, unlike the clear-cut dominant/recessive patterns of Mendelian inheritance.

t: Dihybrid Cross - Phenotypic Ratio in F2
q: Genes R and Y follow independent assortment. If RRYY produce round yellow seeds and rryy produce wrinkled green seeds, what will be the phenotypic ratio of the F2 generation?
e: In a dihybrid cross following independent assortment, the F2 generation shows round-yellow : round-green : wrinkled-yellow : wrinkled-green phenotypes in the ratio 9:3:3:1. Class 12th NCERT Page No.64.

q: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms of chromosomes, the chromosome is referred as:
e: A metacentric chromosome has the centromere at the middle, dividing it into two equal arms.

q: XO type of sex determination can be found in:
e: Grasshoppers show the XO type of sex determination, in which males have only one X-chromosome (XO) besides the autosomes, while females have a pair of X-chromosomes (XX).

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting traits in pea plants and proposed the Laws of Inheritance. Statement II: Seven characters examined by Mendel in his experiment on pea plants were seed shape and colour, flower colour, pod shape and colour, flower position and stem height. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
