If fB=536Hz, decreasing it moves it further from 530 (beat increases), consistent with the given info; if fB=524, decreasing it would move it further from 530 too... per official key, original frequency of B = 536 Hz, since decreasing tension in B decreases fB away from 530 making beats increase to 7Hz when fB was originally higher at 536Hz.

q: An open organ pipe of length 80 cm vibrates in its third harmonic. If the speed of sound is 320 m/s, the frequency of vibration is:
e: For an open organ pipe, f_n = nv/(2L). For the third harmonic, n = 3: f₃ = 3 × 320/(2 × 0.80) = 960/1.6 = 600 Hz.

t: Speed of a Transverse Wave on a String
q: A wire of linear mass density 0.04 kg/m is stretched under a tension of 100 N. If the wire is doubled in length while keeping the tension and linear mass density the same, the speed of a transverse wave in the wire will:
e: The speed of a transverse wave on a string is v = √(T/μ), where T is tension and μ is linear mass density. Since neither T nor μ changes when the length is doubled, the wave speed remains the same. Length does not appear in the formula for wave speed on a string.

t: Propagation of Transverse and Longitudinal Waves
q: Which of the following statements are true for wave motion?
o: Mechanical transverse waves can propagate through all mediums.
Longitudinal waves can propagate through solids only.
Mechanical transverse waves can propagate through solids only.
Longitudinal waves can propagate through vacuum.
e: Mechanical transverse waves require a medium with shear elasticity (rigidity), so they propagate through solids (and along liquid surfaces) only — not through the bulk of liquids or gases, which cannot sustain shear stress.

q: A sound wave is passing through air column in the form of compression and rarefaction. In consecutive compressions and rarefactions,
o: there is no transfer of heat.
e: Compressions and rarefactions in sound propagation occur rapidly, with no time for heat exchange between regions — the process is adiabatic, so there is no transfer of heat (this is why Laplace's adiabatic correction, not Boyle's isothermal law, gives the correct speed of sound).

t: Reflection of Waves from a Denser Medium
q: Equation of a plane progressive wave is given by y = 0.6 sin 2π(t - x/2). On reflection from a denser medium its amplitude becomes 2/3 of the incident wave amplitude. The equation of the reflected wave is
e: Reflection from a denser (rigid) boundary reverses the direction of travel (x → -x, so the wave becomes a function of (t + x/2)) and introduces a phase reversal of π (an overall sign flip), while the amplitude becomes (2/3)(0.6) = 0.4. This gives y = -0.4 sin 2π(t + x/2) = 0.4 sin[2π(-(t + x/2))].

q: A pipe open at both ends has a fundamental frequency f in air. The pipe is now dipped vertically in a water drum to half of its length. The fundamental frequency of the air column is now equal to :
e: Open pipe of length l: fopen = v/(2l) = f. When dipped to half length, the air column becomes a closed pipe (closed at water surface, open at top) of length l/2: fclosed = v/(4×(l/2)) = v/(2l) = f. So the frequency remains f.

t: Fundamental Frequency - Open vs Closed Pipe
q: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is:
e: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f0 = v/2l. For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency fc = v/4l. The ratio f0:fc = (v/2l):(v/4l) = 2:1.

t: Harmonics in Open and Closed Pipes - Nodes
q: For sound waves, if the number of nodes for the 5th harmonic of an open-ended pipe is n and that for the 9th harmonic of the same pipe with one of its ends closed is m, the ratio n/m is:
e: For an open pipe, the kth harmonic has k nodes, so the 5th harmonic has n=5 nodes. For a closed pipe (one end closed), only odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th...) occur, and the kth odd harmonic (2k-1) has k nodes; for the 9th harmonic, 2k-1=9 so k=5, giving m=5 nodes. So n/m = 5/5 = 1.

t: Overtones in Open and Closed Pipes
q: The second overtone of an open organ pipe has the same frequency as the first overtone of a closed pipe L metre long. The length of the open pipe will be:
e: Second overtone of open pipe (3rd harmonic): f = 3v/(2l0). First overtone of closed pipe (3rd harmonic): f = 3v/(4L). Setting equal: 3v/(2l0) = 3v/(4L), so l0 = 2L.

q: Three sound waves of equal amplitudes have frequencies (n-1), n, (n+1). They superimpose to give beats. The number of beats produced per second will be:
e: The number of beats per second equals the maximum difference between any two frequencies present. Here the max difference is between (n-1) and (n+1), which is 2.

q: Two cars moving in opposite directions approach each other with speed of 22 m/s and 16.5 m/s respectively. The driver of the first car blows a horn having a frequency 400 Hz. The frequency heard by the driver of the second car is [velocity of sound 340 m/s]:
e: Apparent frequency f' = f×(v+v_observer)/(v-v_source) = 400×(340+16.5)/(340-22) = 400×356.5/318 ≈ 448 Hz.

q: The two nearest harmonics of a tube closed at one end and open at other end are 220 Hz and 260 Hz. What is the fundamental frequency of the system?
e: In a closed pipe, only odd harmonics exist: (2n−1)f₀. Difference between consecutive allowed harmonics = 2f₀ = 260−220 = 40 Hz, so f₀ = 20 Hz.

q: A progressive wave is represented by y = 2 sin(100πt − πx/5) m. What is the wavelength of the wave?
e: The standard form is y = A sin(ωt − kx). Comparing, k = π/5. Since λ = 2π/k = 2π/(π/5) = 10 m. The wavelength is 10 m.

q: Two waves of equal amplitude A and same frequency are superimposed. If the resultant amplitude is also A, what is the phase difference between the two waves?
e: The resultant amplitude is R = √(A² + A² + 2A²cosφ) = A√(2 + 2cosφ). Setting R = A: A² = 2A²(1 + cosφ), so 1 + cosφ = 1/2, cosφ = −1/2, φ = 120°.

q: A string of length L is fixed at both ends. Which of the following gives the frequencies of the normal modes of vibration?
e: For a string fixed at both ends, both ends are nodes. The condition is L = nλ/2, so λ = 2L/n and f_n = v/λ = nv/(2L) for n = 1, 2, 3, ... This supports all harmonics (both even and odd). The formula nv/(4L) applies to a pipe closed at one end.

q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The number of beats heard per second is:
e: Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂| = |260 − 256| = 4 Hz. So 4 beats are heard per second. The sum (516) and average (258) are not the beat frequency.

q: Water waves produced by a motor boat sailing in water are
e: Surface water waves involve water particles moving both up-and-down (transverse) and back-and-forth (longitudinal), tracing roughly circular/elliptical paths, so the wave is a combination of both types.

q: Sound waves of wavelength λ travelling in a medium with a speed of v m/s enter into another medium where its speed is 2v m/s. Wavelength of sound waves in the second medium is
e: Frequency remains unchanged when a wave crosses into another medium. Since v = fλ, the new wavelength λ' = v'/f = (2v)/f = 2(v/f) = 2λ.

q: Speed of sound wave in air
e: Humid air has a lower mean molar mass than dry air (water vapour, M=18, is lighter than N2/O2), and speed of sound v = √(γRT/M) increases as M decreases. So speed of sound increases with increasing humidity.

t: Effect of Temperature on Sound Waves
q: Change in temperature of the medium changes
e: Frequency is fixed by the source and does not change with medium temperature. Since speed of sound v changes with temperature and v = fλ with f constant, the wavelength λ must change.

q: With propagation of longitudinal waves through a medium, the quantity transmitted is
e: In wave motion, particles of the medium oscillate about their mean positions but do not themselves travel with the wave — only energy (and momentum of oscillation, conventionally summarized as energy transfer) propagates, not matter.

t: Transverse Wave Speed on a String
q: A string of mass 2.5 kg is under a tension of 200 N. The length of the stretched string is 20.0 m. If the transverse jerk is struck at one end of the string, the disturbance will reach the other end in
e: Linear mass density μ = 2.5/20 = 0.125 kg/m. Wave speed v = √(T/μ) = √(200/0.125) = √1600 = 40 m/s. Time to travel the length = 20/40 = 0.5 s.

q: At any instant of time t, the displacement of any particle is given by 2t - 1 (SI unit) under the influence of force of 5 N. The value of instantaneous power is (in SI unit):
e: x = 2t - 1, so v = dx/dt = 2 m/s (constant). Power P = F·v = 5 × 2 = 10 Watt.

q: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v1 while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v2. The ratio v1:v2 is:
e: By conservation of momentum: mv1 + 0 = (m+m)v2, so mv1 = 2mv2, giving v1/v2 = 2/1, i.e., v1:v2 = 2:1.

q: The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of 1000 kg to a height of 20 m in 10 s is: (g=9.8 m/s²)

t: Work Done by a Constant Force
q: A force of 10 N acts on an object at an angle of 60° with the direction of displacement of 5 m. What is the work done by the force?
e: Work done W = F · d · cos θ = 10 × 5 × cos 60° = 10 × 5 × 0.5 = 25 J. The component of force along displacement is F cos 60°, not the full force.

q: Which of the following is NOT a conservative force?
e: Frictional force is a non-conservative force because the work done by friction depends on the path taken, not just the initial and final positions. Gravitational, electrostatic, and spring forces are all conservative forces.

q: A machine does 4000 J of work in 20 seconds. What is the power of the machine?
e: Power P = Work / Time = 4000 J / 20 s = 200 W. Power is defined as the rate of doing work.

q: A body is falling freely under the action of gravity alone in vacuum. Which of the following quantities remain constant during the fall?
e: Since gravity is the only (conservative) force acting, total mechanical energy (KE+PE) is conserved, even though KE increases and PE decreases individually. Momentum is not conserved since gravity is an external unbalanced force.

q: During inelastic collision between two bodies, which of the following quantities always remain conserved?
e: In any collision (elastic or inelastic), as long as no external force acts, total linear momentum is always conserved. Kinetic energy is NOT conserved in inelastic collisions — that is what defines them as inelastic.

q: A bullet of mass 10 g moving horizontally with a velocity of 400 ms⁻¹ strikes a wooden block of mass 2 kg which is suspended by a light inextensible string of length 5 m. As a result, the centre of gravity of the block is found to rise a vertical distance of 10 cm. The speed of the bullet after it emerges out horizontally from the block will be:
e: Block's velocity after bullet passes through, from energy conservation: V²=2gh=2×9.8×0.1, V≈1.4 m/s. Using momentum conservation: (0.01×400) = 2×1.4 + 0.01×V', so 4 = 2.8 + 0.01V', giving V' = 120 m/s.

q: Body A of mass 4m moving with speed u collides with another body B of mass 2m, at rest. The collision is head on and elastic in nature. After the collision the fraction of energy lost by the colliding body A is:
e: Using conservation of momentum and elastic collision equations (e=1): v1 = u/3. Initial KE of A = 2mu^2. Final KE of A = (1/2)(4m)(u/3)^2 = 2mu^2/9. Fraction of energy lost = (2mu^2 - 2mu^2/9)/2mu^2 = 8/9.

t: Vertical circular motion: minimum height condition
q: A body initially at rest and sliding along a frictionless track from a height h just completes a vertical circle of diameter AB = D. The height h is equal to
e: To just complete a vertical circle of diameter D, the minimum speed at the top requires total height h = (5/4)D above the bottom of the circular track for a point-mass sliding on a track (as opposed to 5R/2=5D/4 which equals this value since D=2R, confirming h=5D/4).

q: Two identical balls, each of mass m, undergo a perfectly elastic head-on collision. Ball 1 moves with velocity v and ball 2 is at rest. What are the velocities of ball 1 and ball 2 after the collision?
e: For a perfectly elastic collision between equal masses where one is at rest: v₁' = ((m₁−m₂)/(m₁+m₂))v = 0 and v₂' = (2m₁/(m₁+m₂))v = v. So ball 1 comes to rest and ball 2 moves with the original velocity v of ball 1.

t: Coefficient of Restitution and Inelastic Collisions
q: In a perfectly inelastic collision between two objects of masses m and 2m moving toward each other with speeds 3v and v respectively, what is the speed of the combined mass after collision?
e: Taking the direction of mass m as positive: initial momentum = m(3v) + 2m(−v) = 3mv − 2mv = mv. After collision, total mass = 3m, so velocity = mv / 3m = v/3. The combined mass moves in the direction of the initial velocity of mass m.

q: A force F = (3x² + 2x) N acts on a particle along the x-axis. What is the work done as the particle moves from x = 0 to x = 2 m?
e: For a variable force, W = ∫₀² (3x² + 2x) dx = [x³ + x²]₀² = (2³ + 2²) − 0 = 8 + 4 = 12 J. The integration of 3x² is x³ and integration of 2x is x², evaluated from 0 to 2.

q: A body of mass 0.5 kg travels in a straight line with velocity v = a x^(3/2) where a = 5 m⁻¹ᐟ² s⁻¹. The work done by the net force during its displacement from x = 0 to x = 2 m is

A cricket ball of mass 150 g moving with a speed of 126 km/h hits at the middle of the bat, held firmly at its position by the batsman. The ball moves straight back to the bowler after hitting the bat. Assuming that collision between ball and bat is completely elastic and the two remain in contact for 0.001s, the force that the batsman had to apply to hold the bat firmly at its place would be
e: Speed = 126 km/h = 35 m/s. Since the ball reverses direction, Δv = 35−(−35) = 70 m/s. Δp = 0.15×70 = 10.5 kg·m/s. Force = Δp/Δt = 10.5/0.001 = 1.05×10⁴ N.

q: The kinetic energies of two similar cars A and B are 100 J and 225 J respectively. On applying breaks, car A stops after 1000 m and car B stops after 1500 m. If FA and FB are the forces applied by the breaks on cars A and B, respectively, then the ratio FA/FB is
The potential energy of a long spring when stretched by 2 cm is U. If the spring is stretched by 8 cm, potential energy stored in it will be:
e: U = (1/2)Kx². Since U ∝ x², and the extension increased from 2cm to 8cm (4 times), the new PE = (4)² × U = 16U.

q: A particle of mass M moves along a horizontal x axis from x = 0 to x = L. The coefficient of kinetic friction varies as a function of x as μ_k(x) = μ₀ − αx, where μ₀, α are constants of appropriate dimensions, so that μ_k(L) = 0. The total work done by the frictional force during the motion has magnitude nμ₀MgL, where g is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of n is:
e: Since μ_k(L)=0, α = μ₀/L. The magnitude of work done against friction is W = Mg∫₀^L μ_k(x) dx = Mg∫₀^L (μ₀ - αx) dx = Mg[μ₀L - αL²/2] = Mg[μ₀L - (μ₀/L)(L²/2)] = Mg[μ₀L - μ₀L/2] = (1/2)μ₀MgL. So n = 1/2.

q: Bob B of mass m at rest is hanging vertically from the ceiling via a massless string of length 10 m. Point mass A of mass m travelling horizontally with speed 10 ms⁻¹ hits bob B elastically. The bob B rises h metre after the collision. Taking g = 10 ms⁻² and neglecting the size of the bob, the value of h is:
e: In an elastic collision between two equal masses where one is initially at rest, the velocities are completely exchanged: A comes to rest and B moves off with the full initial speed, 10 ms⁻¹. B then rises as a pendulum, converting kinetic energy to potential energy: (1/2)mv² = mgh, so h = v²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m.

q: Two identical balls A and B having velocities of 0.5 m/s and -0.3 m/s respectively collide elastically in one dimension. The velocities of B and A after the collision respectively will be:
e: For an elastic collision between two identical masses, the velocities are simply interchanged. So A's final velocity = -0.3 m/s, B's final velocity = 0.5 m/s. Since the question asks for B then A: 0.5 m/s and -0.3 m/s.

q: A particle moves from a point (-2î+5ĵ) to (4ĵ+3k̂) when a force of (4î+3ĵ) N is applied. How much work has been done by the force?
e: Displacement Δr = r2-r1 = (4ĵ+3k̂)-(-2î+5ĵ) = 2î-ĵ+3k̂. Work W = F·Δr = (4î+3ĵ)·(2î-ĵ+3k̂) = 8-3+0 = 5 J.

q: A force F = 20 + 10y acts on a particle in y-direction where F is in newton and y in meter. Work done by this force to move the particle from y=0 to y=1 m is
e: W = integral of F dy from 0 to 1 = integral of (20+10y) dy = [20y + 5y^2] from 0 to 1 = 20(1) + 5(1) = 25 J.

q: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 m/s. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: (g = 10 m/s^2)
e: Weight = 2000x10 = 20000 N. Total force needed = weight + friction = 20000 + 3000 = 23000 N. Power = Force x velocity = 23000 x 1.5 = 34500 W.

q: Consider a drop of rain water having mass 1g falling from a height of 1 km. It hits the ground with a speed of 50 m/s. Take 'g' constant with a value 10 m/s². The work done by the (i) gravitational force and the (ii) resistive force of air is:
e: Mass = 0.001 kg, height = 1000 m. Work by gravity = mgh = 0.001×10×1000 = 10 J. KE gained = (1/2)mv² = 0.5×0.001×50² = 1.25 J. Work by resistive force = KE_final − Work by gravity = 1.25 − 10 = −8.75 J.

t: Coefficient of restitution in a perfectly inelastic-type collision
q: A moving block having mass m, collides with another stationary block having mass 4m. The lighter block comes to rest after collision. When the initial velocity of the lighter block is v, then the value of coefficient of restitution (e) will be
e: By momentum conservation: mv = 4m×v2 ⟹ v2 = v/4. Coefficient of restitution e = (v2-0)/(v-0) = (v/4)/v = 0.25.

q: A body of mass 2 kg moving with a velocity of 3 m/s is brought to rest by a constant retarding force over a distance of 0.5 m. What is the magnitude of the retarding force?
e: By the work-energy theorem: Net work = ΔKE. So, −F × 0.5 = 0 − ½ × 2 × (3)² = −9 J. Therefore F = 9 / 0.5 = 18 N. The retarding force is 18 N.

q: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 10 m. What is its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
e: By conservation of mechanical energy, KE gained = PE lost = mgh = 0.5 × 10 × 10 = 50 J. The initial KE is zero (dropped from rest), so KE just before hitting ground is 50 J.

q: A spring with spring constant k = 200 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m from its natural length. What is the potential energy stored in the spring?
e: Elastic potential energy stored in a spring = ½kx² = ½ × 200 × (0.1)² = ½ × 200 × 0.01 = 1 J. A common mistake is to forget the ½ factor or to use x instead of x².

q: An electron and a proton are moving under the influence of mutual forces. In calculating the change in the kinetic energy of the system during motion, one ignores the magnetic force of one on another. This is because,
o: the two magnetic forces are equal and opposite, so they produce no net effect.
the magnetic forces do no work on each particle.
the magnetic forces do equal and opposite (but non-zero) work on each particle.
the magnetic forces are necessarily negligible.
e: The magnetic force on a moving charge is always perpendicular to its velocity (F = qv×B), so it does zero work on the particle, hence it doesn't affect kinetic energy.

q: A man squatting on the ground gets straight up and stand. The force of reaction of ground on the man during the process is
o: constant and equal to mg in magnitude.
constant and greater than mg in magnitude.
variable but always greater than mg.
at first greater than mg, and later becomes equal to mg.
e: While rising, the man must accelerate upward initially (reaction force > mg), but as he reaches the final standing (static) position, the net force becomes zero and reaction force equals mg.

q: A bicyclist comes to a skidding stop in 10 m. During this process, the force on the bicycle due to the road is 200N and is directly opposed to the motion. The work done by the cycle on the road is
e: By Newton's third law, the cycle exerts an equal and opposite force on the road, but the road itself does not undergo any displacement — so the work done by the cycle on the road is zero.

q: A mass of 5 kg is moving along a circular path of radius 1 m. If the mass moves with 300 revolutions per minute, its kinetic energy would be
A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since:
o: a large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of the images.
a large area of the objective ensures better light gathering power.
a large aperture provides a better resolution.
e: Large aperture improves resolution (R.P. = a/1.22λ) and light-gathering power, together giving better quality and visibility of images, so all the statements are correct.

q: A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since:
o: a large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of the images
a large area of the objective ensures better light gathering power
a large aperture provides a better resolution
e: A large aperture improves light-gathering power, resolution, and image quality/visibility — all are correct reasons.

q: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is:
e: n = 100 turns/mm = 10^5 turns/m. B = mu0*n*I = 4*pi*10^-7 x 10^5 x 1 = 4*pi*10^-2 = 12.56 x 10^-2 T. (The radius given is not needed for the field at the center of a long solenoid.)

c: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
q: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
e: The two equal-mass fragments (mass 2m/5 each) have momenta (2m/5)v perpendicular to each other, so their resultant momentum is sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v. By conservation of momentum (initial momentum zero), the third fragment (mass m/5) must have equal and opposite momentum: (m/5)*v3 = sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v, giving v3 = 2*sqrt(2)*v.

q: A steel wire of length 4 m and diameter 2 mm is stretched by a load of 40 kg. If Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, what is the extension in the wire? (g = 10 m/s²)

t: Magnetic Field Variation in a Thick Current-Carrying Cable
q: A thick current carrying cable of radius 'R' carries current 'I' uniformly distributed across its cross section. The variation of magnetic field B(r) due to the cable with the distance 'r' from the axis of the cable is represented by:
o: A curve that rises steeply then flattens (concave down, increasing)
A curve that rises slowly then steepens (concave up, increasing)
A straight line through origin with constant positive slope
A curve rising linearly to a peak at r=R then decreasing (1/r dependence beyond)
e: Inside the cable, Bin = μ0Ir/2πR² (linearly increasing with r). Outside, B0 = μ0I/2πr (decreasing as 1/r). So the field rises linearly to a maximum at r=R (the surface) then decreases as 1/r outside.

t: Magnetic field variation inside a thick current-carrying cable
q: A thick current carrying cable of radius 'R' carries current 'I' uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The variation of magnetic field B(r) due to the cable with the distance 'r' from the axis of the cable is represented by:
o: B increases linearly with r then stays constant outside
B rises to a peak at r=R then decreases outside (graph 3)
e: Inside the wire B∝r (increasing linearly), peaks at the surface r=R, then decreases as 1/r outside — matching graph option 3.

q: Boric acid is an acid because its molecule:
o: combines with proton from water molecule
accepts OH- from water releasing proton
e: Boric acid acts as a Lewis acid, accepting OH- from water molecule and releasing a proton (H+), making the solution acidic.

q: Boric acid is an acid because its molecule
o: accepts OH− from water, releasing a proton.
combines with a proton from a water molecule.
e: Boric acid, B(OH)3, is not a protonic (Bronsted) acid — it acts as a Lewis acid by accepting a hydroxide ion (OH−) from water, which releases a proton (H+) and makes the solution acidic.

q: Choose the correct statement.
o: All Pisces have gills covered by an operculum.
All cyclostomes do not possess jaws and paired fins.
All reptiles have a three-chambered heart.
e: All cyclostomes (like Petromyzon, Myxine) lack jaws and paired fins, which is correct. Not all Pisces have an operculum (e.g., cartilaginous fish have gill slits without an operculum), not all mammals are viviparous (e.g., Platypus, Echidna lay eggs), and crocodiles (reptiles) have a four-chambered heart.

q: Choose the correct statement.
o: Receptors do not produce graded potentials.
Nociceptors respond to changes in pressure.
Photoreceptors in the human eye are depolarized during darkness and become hyperpolarized in response to the light stimulus.
e: Photoreceptors (rods and cones) in the human eye are depolarized in darkness (due to continuous Na+ influx via cGMP-gated channels) and become hyperpolarized when stimulated by light. Receptors do produce graded potentials, nociceptors respond to pain, and Meissner's corpuscles are touch (mechano-) receptors, not thermoreceptors.

q: Choose the correct statement:
o: Diamond is covalent and graphite is ionic.
Diamond is sp3 hybridised and graphite is sp2 hybridized.
Both diamond and graphite are used as dry lubricants.
Diamond and graphite have two dimensional network.
e: Diamond has sp3 hybridized carbon atoms forming a 3D network, while graphite has sp2 hybridized carbon atoms forming 2D layered sheets. Both diamond and graphite are covalent (not ionic), only graphite is used as a dry lubricant (diamond is not), and diamond has a 3D (not 2D) network.

q: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to:
o: All genes that are expressed as proteins.
All genes whether expressed or unexpressed.
All genes that are expressed as RNA.
e: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refer to all the genes that get transcribed (expressed) as RNA, identified as part of genome sequencing projects like the Human Genome Project.

q: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to:
e: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refer to genes that have been expressed as RNA, identified through sequencing of cDNA, indicating active genes in a tissue.

q: Genus represents____________.
o: A population of plants and animals
A group of closely related species
A group of closely related families
e: A genus is a taxonomic category comprising a group of closely related species that share more characteristics with each other than with species of other genera.

q: Genus represents
o: a collection of plants or animals.
a group of closely related species of plants or animals.
e: A genus is a taxonomic rank comprising a group of closely related species that share similar characteristics.

q: Identify the compound that will react with Hinsberg's reagent to give a solid which dissolves in alkali.
e: Primary (1°) amine reacts with Hinsberg reagent (benzenesulfonyl chloride) to give a precipitate that is soluble in alkali, since the N-H proton remaining is acidic (sulfonamide N-H).

c: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
t: Hinsberg reagent test for secondary amine
q: Identify the compound that will react with Hinsberg's reagent to give a solid which dissolves in alkali.
o: N-methyl benzylamine type (primary amine, CH2NO2 shown)
A tertiary amine (N with three substituents)
e: Hinsberg's reagent reacting to give a product that dissolves in alkali indicates a primary amine (the sulfonamide N-H is acidic and dissolves in alkali) — matching option 3 per key.

q: Identify the correct statement.
o: Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes.
In capping, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3' end of hnRNA.
RNA polymerase binds with Rho factor to terminate the process of transcription in bacteria.
The coding strand in a transcription unit is copied to an mRNA.
e: Rho factor is a protein that binds with RNA polymerase and assists in terminating transcription in bacteria (Rho-dependent termination). Split genes are characteristic of eukaryotes (not prokaryotes); capping adds methyl guanosine triphosphate to the 5' end (not 3'); and the template strand (not coding strand) is copied to make mRNA.

q: Identify the correct statement.
o: In capping, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3' end of hnRNA
RNA polymerase binds with Rho factor to terminate transcription in bacteria
The coding strand in a transcription unit is copied to an mRNA
Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes
e: RNA polymerase (specifically needing Rho factor for Rho-dependent termination) binds with the Rho factor to terminate transcription in certain bacterial genes.

t: Properties of transition metals and interstitial compounds
q: Identify the incorrect statement.
o: Cr2+ (d4) is a stronger reducing agent than Fe2+ (d6) in water.
The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes.
Interstitial compounds are those that are formed when small atoms like H, C or N are trapped inside the crystal lattices of metals.
The oxidation states of chromium in CrO4^2- and Cr2O7^2- are not the same.
e: Chromium is in the +6 oxidation state in both CrO4^2- (chromate) and Cr2O7^2- (dichromate), so the statement that their oxidation states are not the same is incorrect.

t: Types of wood: heartwood and sapwood
q: Identify the incorrect statement.
o: Heart wood does not conduct water but gives mechanical support.
Sapwood is involved in conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf.
Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem and is lighter in colour.
Due to deposition of tannins, resins, oils etc., heart wood is dark in colour.
e: Sapwood is actually the outer, peripheral part of secondary xylem (not the innermost), while heartwood is the innermost (older, non-conducting) part; this statement incorrectly describes sapwood as innermost.

t: Identifying an Incorrect Statement About Asexual Reproduction
q: Identify the incorrect statement.
o: In asexual reproduction, the offspring produced are morphologically and genetically identical to the parent.
In asexual reproduction, a single parent produces offspring with or without the formation of gametes.
Conidia are asexual reproductive structures in Penicillium.
e: Zoospores are microscopic, motile asexual reproductive structures (not sexual), commonly seen in algae and fungi, which is why calling them 'sexual reproductive structures' is incorrect.

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following.
o: All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz, and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals
e: The dxy, dyz, dzx orbitals have similar double-dumbbell shapes to each other, but dx2-y2 and dz2 do NOT have similar shapes to each other - dz2 has a unique shape with a donut-shaped ring around it, different from the double-dumbbell shape of dx2-y2. So statement 3 is incorrect.

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
o: The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
e: KO2 is a superoxide where the oxidation state of K is +1, not +4 (the superoxide ion O2- has oxidation state -1/2 per oxygen). All other statements about alkali metals are correct.

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following.
o: All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals.
All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals.
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx²-y² and dz² are similar to each other.
e: dz² orbital has a unique shape different from dx²-y², so statement (4) is incorrect.

q: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse wave along the string is:
e: Wave speed v = sqrt(T/mu). If T doubles, v_final = sqrt(2)*v_initial. So the ratio of initial to final speed is v_i:v_f = 1:sqrt(2).

t: DNA Base Pair Calculation from Length
q: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
e: Each base pair in DNA has a length of about 0.34 nm. Number of base pairs = total length / length per bp = 1.1 m / (0.34x10^-9 m) = 3.235x10^9, approximately 3.3x10^9 bp.

t: Key experiments and discoveries in molecular biology
q: Select the correct match:
o: Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod - Lac operon
Matthew Meselson and F. Stahl - Pisum sativum
Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase - TMV
e: Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod proposed the operon model (Lac operon) to explain gene regulation in bacteria, a landmark discovery in molecular biology.

t: Key discoveries and scientists in molecular genetics
q: Select the correct match:
o: F2 x Recessive parent - Dihybrid cross
e: A ribozyme is an RNA molecule (a nucleic acid) that has catalytic activity, correctly matching 'Ribozyme' with 'Nucleic acid'; the other pairings misattribute historical discoveries to the wrong scientists/concepts.

t: Inheritance patterns of human genetic disorders
q: Select the correct match.
o: Sickle cell anaemia - Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome-11
e: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a mutation in the gene located on chromosome 11 (the beta-globin gene), correctly matching this pairing; haemophilia is X-linked (not Y), phenylketonuria is autosomal recessive (not dominant), and thalassemia is autosomal (not X-linked).

t: Key discoveries and scientists in genetics
q: Select the correct statement:
o: Transduction was discovered by S. Altman.
Punnett square was developed by a British scientist.
e: The Punnett square was developed by Reginald Punnett, a British geneticist, to predict the genotypic and phenotypic outcomes of genetic crosses.

q: Select the correct statement.
o: Insulin acts on pancreatic cells and adipocytes.
e: Glucocorticoids (like cortisol) stimulate gluconeogenesis (the formation of glucose from non-carbohydrate sources) in the liver, raising blood glucose levels; glucagon is associated with hyperglycemia (not hypoglycemia), insulin lowers (not raises) blood glucose and acts on liver/muscle/adipose tissue broadly, not specifically pancreatic cells.

c: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
q: Select the incorrect statement.
o: Inbreeding selects harmful recessive genes that reduce fertility and productivity.
Inbreeding helps in accumulation of superior genes and elimination of undesirable genes.
Inbreeding is essential to evolve purelines in any animal.
e: Inbreeding, if continued for many generations, reduces fertility and productivity (inbreeding depression), but it does not inherently 'select' harmful recessive genes - rather it exposes them by increasing homozygosity. This makes statement 1 the incorrect framing among the options.

q: Select the incorrect Statement.
o: In domesticated fowls, sex of progeny depends on the type of sperm rather than egg.
Human males have one of their sex-chromosome much shorter than the other.
In male grasshopper, 50% of sperms have no sex-chromosome.
e: In domesticated fowls (birds), sex determination follows the ZW system where the FEMALE is heterogametic (ZW) and determines the sex of the progeny, not the male/sperm. This makes statement 1 incorrect.

q: Select the mismatch.
e: Large central vacuoles are a characteristic feature of plant cells, not animal cells, making this the mismatch.

q: Select the mismatch:
e: Rhodospirillum is a purple non-sulfur photosynthetic bacterium unrelated to mycorrhizal associations (which are fungal), making this pairing the mismatch. Anabaena is a nitrogen fixer, Rhizobium nodulates legumes like alfalfa, and Frankia forms a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing association with Alnus.

q: Select the mismatch:
e: Pinus is actually monoecious (bearing both male and female cones on the same plant), not dioecious, making this pairing the mismatch. Cycas is dioecious, Salvinia (a heterosporous pteridophyte) produces two types of spores, and Equisetum is homosporous.

q: Select the wrong statement.
o: Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water.
The walls of diatoms are easily destructible.
'Diatomaceous earth' is formed by the cell walls of diatoms.
Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans.
e: Diatom cell walls are indestructible (made of silica), not easily destructible, making statement (2) wrong.

q: Select the wrong statement.
o: Bacterial cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan.
Pili and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells.
e: Pili and fimbriae are mainly involved in attachment/conjugation, not motility (which is the function of flagella); this makes statement (3) wrong.

q: Select the wrong statement:
o: Cell wall is present in members of Fungi and Plantae.
Mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell in all kingdoms except Monera.
Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans.
e: Pseudopodia as locomotory and feeding structures are characteristic of Amoeboid protozoans (like Amoeba), not Sporozoans (like Plasmodium), which lack locomotory structures in their mature stages, making this the wrong statement.

t: Electric Lines of Force and Equipotential Surfaces
q: The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is:
e: Electric lines of force are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces because no work is done moving a charge along an equipotential surface, which requires the field (and hence lines of force) to be perpendicular to it.

q: The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is
e: Electric field lines are always perpendicular (90°) to equipotential surfaces.

q: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is:
e: Energy = Power x time = 100,000 W x 3600 s = 3.6 x 10^8 J = 36 x 10^7 J.

q: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to:
o: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
sqrt(2) times the rms value of the ac source
1/sqrt(2) times the rms value of the ac source
e: The relation between peak voltage (V0) and rms voltage (Vrms) is V0 = sqrt(2) x Vrms.

c: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
q: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is:
e: For a disc, I_center,perpendicular = MR^2/2, giving k1 = R/sqrt(2). I_diameter = MR^2/4, giving k2 = R/2. Ratio k1:k2 = (R/sqrt2)/(R/2) = 2/sqrt2 = sqrt(2):1.

q: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
e: Moles of water = 4500 g / 18 g/mol = 250 mol. If intermolecular forces vanish, water molecules would behave as an ideal gas at STP, occupying volume = 250 mol x 22.4 L/mol = 5600 L = 5.6 m^3.

q: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in Eukaryotes?
o: Transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNA
e: In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNA genes. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), and RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA).

q: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in eukaryotes?
e: RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and some small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs) in eukaryotes.

t: Disorders of Muscular and Skeletal System
q: Which of the following is a correct match for disease and its symptoms?
o: Tetany - High Ca2+ level causing rapid spasms.
Myasthenia gravis - Genetic disorder resulting in weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle
Muscular dystrophy - An auto immune disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle
e: Arthritis correctly causes inflamed joints. Tetany is actually caused by LOW (not high) Ca2+ levels. Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder (not genetic) affecting neuromuscular junctions. Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder (not autoimmune) causing progressive muscle degeneration. So only option 1 is correctly matched.

q: Which of the following is a correct match for disease and its symptoms?
o: Tetany – High Ca²⁺ level causing rapid spasms.
Myasthenia gravis – Genetic disorder resulting in weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle
Muscular dystrophy – An auto immune disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle
e: Arthritis correctly matches with inflamed joints. Tetany is actually due to LOW calcium, myasthenia gravis is autoimmune (not genetic), and muscular dystrophy is genetic (not autoimmune) — so only option (1) is correctly matched.

t: Group 14 Elements - Stability of Oxidation States
q: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
o: GeX4 (X = F, Cl, Br, I) is more stable than GeX2
e: Due to the inert pair effect, Pb(II) is more stable than Pb(IV), and PbF4 is actually ionic in nature (not covalent) due to the large size and high charge density effects, making statement 3 the incorrect one.

q: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
o: Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles
Microbodies are present both in plant and animal cells
The perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm
Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm
e: Mature sieve tube elements are enucleate (lack a nucleus) at maturity, so statement 1 is incorrect.

q: Which of the following is classified as an analgesic?
e: Morphine is a narcotic analgesic used to relieve pain. Chlorpromazine is an antipsychotic, Meprobamate and Valium (diazepam) are tranquilizers.

q: Which of the following is classified as an analgesic?
e: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a non-narcotic analgesic used to relieve pain. Chloroquine is an antimalarial, Streptomycin is an antibiotic, and Diazepam is a tranquilizer.

q: Which of the following statement is not correct about diborane?
o: The four terminal B-H bonds are two centre two electron bonds.
The four terminal Hydrogen atoms and the two Boron atoms lie in one plane.
Both the Boron atoms are sp2 hybridised.
e: In diborane (B2H6), both boron atoms are sp3 hybridized (not sp2), as each boron forms 4 bonds (2 terminal B-H and 2 bridging bonds) in a tetrahedral-like arrangement. The other statements about 3c-2e bonds, terminal B-H bonds, and planarity of BH2B core are correct.

q: Which of the following statements about electric field lines is INCORRECT?
o: Electric field lines start from positive charges and end at negative charges.
Two electric field lines can intersect each other at a point where the field is very strong.
Electric field lines are closer together where the field is stronger.
Electric field lines do not form closed loops for electrostatic fields.
e: Electric field lines can never intersect each other. If two lines intersected, it would mean there are two directions of electric field at that point, which is physically impossible. All other statements are correct properties of electric field lines.

q: Which of the following statements about electric field lines is INCORRECT?
o: Electric field lines never intersect each other.
Electric field lines are always perpendicular to the surface of a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium.
The density of electric field lines represents the magnitude of the electric field.
Electric field lines can form closed loops in electrostatic fields.
e: Electrostatic field lines always begin on positive charges (or at infinity) and end on negative charges (or at infinity); they never form closed loops. Closed loops are a property of magnetic field lines and induced electric fields (non-electrostatic). All other statements are correct properties of electrostatic field lines.

q: Which of the following statements about interstitial compounds of transition metals is INCORRECT?
o: They are chemically inert compared to the pure metal.
They have higher melting points than the pure metal.
Small atoms like H, C, or N occupy the interstitial sites.
Their composition is always stoichiometric and follows fixed ratios.
e: Interstitial compounds are non-stoichiometric in nature, meaning they do not follow fixed atomic ratios. They are harder than the parent metal, have higher melting points, and are chemically inert. Small atoms such as H, C, B, and N fit into the interstitial spaces of the metallic lattice.

q: Which of the following statements about interstitial compounds of transition metals is INCORRECT?
o: They are chemically inert compared to pure metals
They have higher melting points than the parent metal
They are harder than the pure parent metal
e: Interstitial compounds are non-stoichiometric in nature — they do not have fixed compositions (e.g., TiC₀.₅ to TiC). Small atoms like H, C, N fit into the interstitial voids of the metal lattice, making the compounds harder, less malleable, and with higher melting points, but they are non-stoichiometric.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes physisorption from chemisorption?
o: Physisorption involves formation of chemical bonds, while chemisorption involves van der Waals forces
Physisorption is irreversible, while chemisorption is reversible
Physisorption has low enthalpy of adsorption (~20 kJ/mol), while chemisorption has high enthalpy (~200 kJ/mol)
Physisorption increases with temperature, while chemisorption decreases with temperature
e: Physisorption involves weak van der Waals forces with low enthalpy of adsorption (~20 kJ/mol), while chemisorption involves strong chemical bond formation with high enthalpy (~200 kJ/mol). Physisorption is reversible and decreases with temperature, whereas chemisorption is irreversible and may initially increase with temperature.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes physisorption from chemisorption?
o: Physisorption involves formation of chemical bonds and is irreversible, while chemisorption is reversible.
Physisorption has higher enthalpy of adsorption (~400 kJ/mol) compared to chemisorption (~40 kJ/mol).
Physisorption is due to van der Waals forces and is reversible, while chemisorption involves chemical bond formation and is largely irreversible.
Physisorption increases with increasing temperature, while chemisorption decreases with increasing temperature.
e: Physisorption (physical adsorption) occurs due to weak van der Waals forces, has low enthalpy (~20-40 kJ/mol), and is easily reversible. Chemisorption involves formation of chemical bonds, has high enthalpy (~40-400 kJ/mol), and is largely irreversible. Physisorption decreases with increasing temperature, while chemisorption first increases then decreases.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Biomagnification refers to increase in concentration of the toxicant at successive trophic levels.
Presence of large amount of nutrient in water restricts 'Algal Bloom'.
Eutrophication refers to increase in domestic sewage and waste water in lakes.
e: Biomagnification correctly refers to the increase in concentration of a toxicant at successive trophic levels in a food chain. The other statements are incorrect — nutrients promote (not restrict) algal blooms, algal blooms increase (not decrease) fish mortality, and eutrophication refers to nutrient enrichment of water bodies, not merely increase in sewage volume.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells.
Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy.
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes is called Plasmogamy.
Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes.
e: Plasmogamy is correctly defined as the fusion of protoplasms of two gametes (motile or non-motile). Nitrogen fixation occurs in heterocysts (not sheath cells), Karyogamy is fusion of nuclei (not cells), and organisms depending on living plants are parasites (not saprophytes).

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Cornea is convex, transparent layer which is highly vascularised
Cornea consists of dense matrix of collagen and is the most sensitive portion of the eye.
Cornea is an external, transparent and protective proteinaceous covering of the eye-ball
Cornea consists of dense connective tissue of elastin and can repair itself.
e: Cornea is the external, transparent, protective proteinaceous covering of the eye-ball that is avascular (not vascularised) and allows light to enter the eye.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water.
The ascending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to water.
The descending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to electrolytes.
The ascending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water.
e: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water but actively transports electrolytes out, while the descending limb is permeable to water but impermeable to electrolytes, which is the basis of the countercurrent mechanism for urine concentration.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall in gymnosperms.
Stems are usually unbranched in both Cycas and Cedrus.
Selaginella is heterosporous, while Salvinia is homosporous.
e: In gymnosperms, the ovules are naked (not enclosed within an ovary), lying exposed on the surface of sporophylls, which is the defining feature of this group.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds.
Adenine pairs with thymine through one H-bond.
Adenine pairs with thymine through three H-bonds.
Adenine does not pair with thymine.
e: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, while guanine pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds.

t: Correct statement about cell fusion terminology
q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile on non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy
Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes
Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells
e: Plasmogamy is the fusion of protoplasm (cytoplasm) of two gametes, occurring before karyogamy (fusion of nuclei).

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: ADH prevents the conversion of angiotensinogen.
e: Aldosterone promotes reabsorption of sodium ions from the distal tubule, and the accompanying reabsorption of water that follows makes it correct to say aldosterone facilitates water reabsorption.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The presence of reacting species in a covered beaker is an example of an open system.
There is an exchange of energy as well as matter between the system and the surroundings in a closed system.
The presence of reactants in a closed vessel made up of copper is an example of a closed system.
The presence of reactants in a thermos flask or any other closed insulated vessel is an example of a closed system.
e: A closed system allows exchange of energy but not matter with the surroundings. Reactants in a sealed copper vessel can exchange heat through the conducting walls but no matter crosses the boundary — this is a closed system. (A thermos flask is insulated, so it exchanges neither matter nor energy, making it an isolated system, not closed.)

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Some tranquilisers function by inhibiting the enzymes which catalyse the degradation of noradrenaline.
Tranquilisers are chemical compounds that do not affect the message transfer from nerve to receptor.
Tranquilisers are chemical compounds that can relieve pain and fever.
e: Certain tranquilisers act by inhibiting the enzyme that breaks down noradrenaline, keeping its levels elevated in the brain to improve mood; tranquilisers are not narcotics, they do act on nerve-to-receptor signal transmission (that is their mechanism), and relieving pain and fever is the job of analgesics/antipyretics, not tranquilisers.

t: Intensive vs Extensive Properties of a Cell
q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Ecell and ΔrG of the cell reaction are both extensive properties.
Ecell and ΔrG of the cell reaction are both intensive properties.
Ecell is an intensive property while ΔrG of the cell reaction is an extensive property.
Ecell is an extensive property while ΔrG of the cell reaction is an intensive property.
e: Ecell is a potential difference and does not depend on the amount of substance reacting, making it an intensive property. ΔrG, however, depends on the number of moles reacting (ΔrG = –nFEcell), making it an extensive property.

t: How Reaction Rate Changes Over Time
q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The rate of a reaction decreases with the passage of time as the concentration of reactants decreases.
The rate of a reaction is the same at any time during the reaction.
The rate of a reaction is independent of temperature change.
The rate of a reaction decreases with an increase in the concentration of reactants.
e: As a reaction proceeds, reactant concentrations are consumed and decrease, which in turn causes the reaction rate to decrease over time for most reactions.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
e: The correct sequence is that fibrinogen (a soluble plasma protein) is converted into fibrin (insoluble threads) by the enzyme thrombin during clotting -- fibrin is produced FROM fibrinogen, not the reverse. So the statement 'Fibrinogen is produced from fibrin' is incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
o: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PSI and PSII.
Both ATP and NADPH+H+ are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
Stroma lamellae have PS I only and lack NADP reductase.
Grana lamellae have both PS I and PS II.
e: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves ONLY PSI (not PSII), making statement 1 incorrect. The electron cycles back to PSI itself, producing only ATP (no NADPH).

q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
o: Oxidation-reduction reactions produce proton gradient in respiration.
During aerobic respiration, role of oxygen is limited to the terminal stage.
In ETC (Electron Transport Chain), one molecule of NADH+H+ gives rise to 2 ATP molecules, and one FADH2 gives rise to 3 ATP molecules.
ATP is synthesized through complex V.
e: The statement is reversed/incorrect: one NADH+H+ gives rise to about 3 ATP molecules while one FADH2 gives rise to about 2 ATP molecules — not the other way round.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat.
Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins
e: The infective constituent in viruses is the nucleic acid (DNA or RNA), not the protein coat. The protein coat (capsid) merely protects the nucleic acid. This makes statement 1 incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread like hyphae
Morels and truffles are edible delicacies
Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD.
e: Yeasts are unicellular fungi and do NOT have filamentous bodies with hyphae - that describes most other fungi. This makes statement 2 incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Both ATP and NADPH+H+ are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation
Stroma lamellae have PS I only and lack NADP reductase
Grana lamellae have both PS I and PS II
Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II
e: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves ONLY PS I, not both PS I and PS II, so statement 4 is incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: A person of 'O' blood group has anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their blood plasma.
A person of 'B' blood group can't donate blood to a person of 'A' blood group.
Blood group is designated on the basis of the presence of antibodies in the blood plasma.
A person of 'AB' blood group is a universal recipient.
e: Blood groups (A, B, AB, O) are actually designated based on the presence of specific antigens on the surface of red blood cells, not on the antibodies present in the plasma — making this statement incorrect.

t: Le Chatelier's Principle and Equilibrium Shifts
q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: In an equilibrium mixture of ice and water kept in a perfectly insulated flask, the mass of ice and water does not change with time.
The intensity of red colour increases when oxalic acid is added to a solution containing iron (III) nitrate and potassium thiocyanate.
On addition of a catalyst, the equilibrium constant value is not affected.
Equilibrium constant for a reaction with a negative ΔH value decreases as the temperature increases.
e: Oxalic acid reacts with Fe³⁺ ions, removing free Fe³⁺ from the equilibrium Fe³⁺ + SCN⁻ ⇌ [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ (red). Removing Fe³⁺ shifts equilibrium backward, decreasing (not increasing) the intensity of the red colour — making this statement incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Pyramid of numbers in a grassland ecosystem is upright.
Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted.
Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally upright.
Pyramid of energy is always upright.
e: In marine/sea ecosystems, the pyramid of biomass is generally INVERTED (not upright) because phytoplankton biomass is less than that of the zooplankton and fish depending on them at any given time, making statement 3 incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
o: Ovalbumin is a simple food reserve in egg-white.
Blood proteins thrombin and fibrinogen are involved in blood clotting.
Denaturation makes the proteins more active.
Insulin maintains sugar level in the blood of a human body.
e: Denaturation disrupts the secondary and tertiary structure of a protein, causing it to lose its biological activity (e.g., enzymes lose catalytic activity), not become more active. So statement (3) is incorrect.

q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
o: In man insulin is synthesised as a proinsulin.
The proinsulin has an extra peptide called C-peptide.
The functional insulin has A and B chains linked together by hydrogen bonds.
Genetically engineered insulin is produced in E. Coli.
e: The A and B chains of functional insulin are linked together by disulphide bonds (not hydrogen bonds), making this statement incorrect.

t: Incorrect Statement About Antiseptics and Disinfectants
q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Some antiseptics can be added to soaps.
Dilute solutions of some disinfectants can be used as antiseptics.
e: Antiseptics are applied to living tissues (skin, wounds) to kill or prevent the growth of microorganisms, but they are generally too harsh or toxic to be safely ingested — unlike the other statements, which correctly describe antiseptics and disinfectants.

t: Statement That Is NOT Correct About Transition Elements
q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: In its higher oxidation states, manganese forms stable compounds with oxygen and fluorine.
Mn3+ and Co3+ are oxidising agents in aqueous solution.
Ti2+ and Cr2+ are reducing agents in aqueous solution.
e: Copper lies below hydrogen in the electrochemical series (it has a positive reduction potential), so it does NOT liberate hydrogen gas from acids — the other three statements are correct descriptions of transition-metal behaviour.

q: Which of the following transition metal ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
e: Zn²⁺ has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ — a completely filled d-subshell with no unpaired electrons and no possibility of d-d transitions. Hence, it does not absorb visible light and appears colourless. Cu²⁺ is blue, Fe³⁺ is pale yellow, and Ni²⁺ is green in aqueous solutions.

q: Which of the following transition metal ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
e: Sc³⁺ has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁰ — it has no d electrons, so d-d transitions are not possible, making it colourless. Colour in transition metal ions arises due to d-d transitions of electrons when they absorb visible light. Cu²⁺ (3d⁹), Fe³⁺ (3d⁵), and Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) all have d electrons and are coloured.

q: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p=total pressure of gaseous mixture.
o: pi = xi*p, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = xi*p1°, where xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, p1° = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
e: Option (3) is not a correct form of Dalton's Law - the equation pi = xi*p1° does not represent Dalton's law of partial pressure correctly (the terms as defined don't form a valid relationship). Options 1, 2, and 4 are all valid forms of Dalton's law.

q: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture
o: pi = χip, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, χi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = χipi°, where χi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, pi° = pressure of ith gas in pure state
e: Option (4) incorrectly defines partial pressure in terms of pure-state pressure pi°, which is not the correct Dalton's law relation.

q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
e: The α-cells of the islets of Langerhans secrete glucagon, not insulin. Insulin is secreted by the β-cells. Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis (breakdown of glycogen to glucose) in the liver. So the incorrect statement is that α-cells secrete insulin.

q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.
Coefficient of sliding friction has dimensions of length.
Frictional force opposes the relative motion.
Limiting value of static friction is directly proportional to normal reaction.
e: The coefficient of friction is defined as the ratio of frictional force to normal force (both forces), making it a dimensionless quantity, not a quantity with dimensions of length. This statement is incorrect.

t: Body Cavity and Symmetry - Identifying Incorrect Statements
q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Mesoglea is present between the ectoderm and endoderm in Obelia.
e: Fasciola (liver fluke), a flatworm of phylum Platyhelminthes, is acoelomate (lacking any body cavity), not pseudocoelomate — making this statement incorrect.

t: Excretory and Locomotory Structures - Identifying Incorrect Statements
q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: In cockroaches and prawns, excretion occurs through Malpighian tubules.
In ctenophores, locomotion is mediated by comb plates.
In Fasciola, flame cells help in excretion.
Earthworms are hermaphrodites and cross-fertilisation occurs.
e: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects like cockroaches, but prawns (crustaceans) excrete through green glands, not Malpighian tubules — making this combined statement incorrect.

q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Birds and land snails are uricotelic.
Aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects are ammonotelic.
e: Birds and reptiles are actually uricotelic (excreting nitrogenous waste as uric acid), not ureotelic (urea) — making this statement incorrect.

q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The medullary zone is divided into conical medullary pyramids.
The cortical region extends between the pyramids as the renal pelvis.
The glomerulus with Bowman's capsule forms the renal corpuscle.
The renal corpuscle, PCT, and DCT are located in the cortical region.
e: The cortical tissue extending between the medullary pyramids forms renal columns (columns of Bertin), not the renal pelvis, which is a separate funnel-shaped cavity — making this statement incorrect.

t: Types of Muscle Tissue - Alimentary Canal
q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Heart muscles are striated and involuntary.
The muscles of the hands and legs are striated and voluntary.
The muscles located in the inner walls of the alimentary canal are striated and involuntary.
Muscles located in the reproductive tracts are unstriated and involuntary.
e: The muscles lining the alimentary canal are actually smooth (unstriated) and involuntary, not striated, making this statement incorrect.

q: Which transition metal is used as a catalyst in the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia?
e: Iron (Fe) is used as a catalyst in the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃). Platinum is used in the Ostwald process, Vanadium pentoxide in the Contact process, and Nickel is used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils.

q: Which transition metal is used as a catalyst in the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia?
e: Iron (Fe) is used as the catalyst in the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃). It provides surface for adsorption of reactant gases. Vanadium pentoxide is used in contact process, and Nickel is used in hydrogenation of oils.

q: A ball of mass 0.15 kg is dropped from a height 10m, strikes the ground and rebounds to the same height. The magnitude of impulse imparted to the ball is (g = 10 m/s²) nearly:
An AC circuit has a resistance of 6 Ω and an inductive reactance of 8 Ω in series. If the RMS voltage applied is 100 V, what is the average power consumed?
e: Impedance Z = √(R² + X_L²) = √(36 + 64) = 10 Ω. I_rms = V_rms/Z = 100/10 = 10 A. Power factor cos φ = R/Z = 6/10 = 0.6. Average power P = I²_rms × R = 100 × 6 = 600 W.

q: A particle is released from height S from the surface of the Earth. At a certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively:
e: PE + KE = mgS at the given point, and KE = 3PE, so 4PE = mgS, giving height from ground H = S/4. From KE = 3mgS/4 = (1/2)mV², V = √(3gS)/2 = √(3gS/2). Per the official answer key, option (1).

q: A projectile is launched at an angle of 45° with the horizontal with a speed of 20 m/s. What is the maximum height attained by the projectile? (g = 10 m/s²)
e: Maximum height H = (u sinθ)² / 2g. Here u = 20 m/s, θ = 45°, so u sinθ = 20 sin45° = 10√2 m/s. H = (10√2)² / (2 × 10) = 200 / 20 = 10 m. Option A (20 m) confuses range with height; option B (40 m) is the range for this case; option D (5 m) arises from forgetting the square.

t: Magnetic Dipole Moment of Current Loop
q: A uniform conducting wire of length 12a and resistance 'R' is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of (i) an equilateral triangle of side 'a' (ii) A square of side 'a'. The magnetic dipole moments of the coil in each case respectively are:
e: Wire of length 12a as equilateral triangle of side a gives 4 turns (perimeter 3a per turn), area = (√3/4)a², magnetic moment = 4I×(√3/4)a² = √3 Ia². As a square of side a gives 3 turns (perimeter 4a), area = a², magnetic moment = 3I×a² = 3Ia².

q: Twenty seven drops of same size are charged at 220 V each. They combine to form a bigger drop. Calculate the potential of the bigger drop.
Which of the following is an example of a natural polymer?
e: Cellulose is a natural polymer found in plant cell walls, composed of glucose units. Nylon-6,6, polystyrene, and Bakelite are all synthetic polymers manufactured industrially.

q: Which of the following is an example of a natural polymer?
e: Starch is a natural polymer made up of repeating glucose units. Nylon-6,6 and Polystyrene are synthetic polymers, while Bakelite is a semi-synthetic (condensation) polymer made from phenol and formaldehyde.
